| | | We know the SAVE America Act was fast-tracked by opponents of voting rights to be in place before November, folks. **This bill is a stunning assault on our fundamental right to vote,** and we can not afford to let this anti-democratic legislation become law. This bill would force every voter to present proof of citizenship to register, either a passport or a birth certificate that matches their current first and last name -- something millions of eligible American women don’t have. **And that’s the point. **The bill would also obliterate popular methods of voter registration for**** all voters, including:
---
* Registration by mail

* 3rd party voter registration drives

* Online voter registration in states that allow it

* Automatic voter registration

---
Some estimates say that **_this bill could disenfranchise anywhere from 11 million to 65 million eligible Americans_** , especially women and those who live in under-resourced communities. “ _There’s never been an attack on voting rights out of Congress like this_ ,” said Alexander Keyssar, a professor of History and Social Policy at the Harvard Kennedy School, and a leading historian of voting rights. “ _It’s always been the federal government trying to keep states in check on voting rights, for the most part._ ” **[The consequences of a bill like this passing would be simply catastrophic for our democracy. Listen to Senator Richard Blumenthal of Connecticut: = | | | | Donald Trump keeps demanding that Congress pass the SAVE America Act (the latest version of the anti-voting SAVE Act). With the House having passed it again, the Senate is all we have left to stop this suppressive legislation from becoming law ahead of the midterm elections , folks. Defenders of voting rights know that non-citizen voting is already illegal, extremely rare, and that this bill is written in a way that could disenfranchise millions of eligible women across the country. Here's Colorado Senator Michael Bennet on the impact of these bills: Opponents of voting rights in Congress -- and in the White House -- favor this bill because they know it could suppress millions of eligible voters, changing the composition of the electorate and potentially empowering them and their party for years to come. = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | | = | | = | | = | | | = | | = | | = | | | We know the SAVE America Act was fast-tracked by opponents of voting rights to be in place before November, folks. This bill is a stunning assault on our fundamental right to vote, and we can not afford to let this anti-democratic legislation become law. This bill would force every voter to present proof of citizenship to register, either a passport or a birth certificate that matches their current first and last name -- something millions of eligible American women don’t have. And that’s the point. The bill would also obliterate popular methods of voter registration for** all voters, including: Registration by mail 3rd party voter registration drives Online voter registration in states that allow it Automatic voter registration Some estimates say that this bill could disenfranchise anywhere from 11 million to 65 million eligible Americans , especially women and those who live in under-resourced communities. “ There’s never been an attack on voting rights out of Congress like this ,” said Alexander Keyssar, a professor of History and Social Policy at the Harvard Kennedy School, and a leading historian of voting rights. “ It’s always been the federal government trying to keep states in check on voting rights, for the most part. ” =** | | | | | | | ---|---|---|--- Integrity First Voter Action Project is dedicated to expanding ballot access and increasing voter participation across the country. Yet, a conservative federal court is trying to confuse voters on the eve of absentee voting. Think about that. **We are six weeks out from a major national election, and the congressional map is still in limbo — thanks to power-hungry Republicans who will stop at nothing to try to rig the rules.** Don’t forget: People in Missouri are _already_ voting! In fact, thousands more voters will cast their ballots before this gets resolved, including voting on the ballot referendum to overturn the very map Republicans are desperate to keep in place. The bottom line is the closer we get to the election, the more shameless and cynical this Republican Party becomes. clean_body: | | | | | Peter , I flew above battlefields, passing burning husks of armored vehicles, and in Iraq I poured enough sand out of my boots to fill a desert. You would think that after flying an Apache helicopter through an active war zone, and having God knows how many stray bullets shot my direction, there’s not a thing on this planet that could scare me. I thought so too, until my team reminded me about what’s coming in the next few days. Let me explain. This campaign’s bigger than anything I’ve done in Iraq. Rather than covering for a team on the ground, the fate of more than 10 million people will be decided in November. Campaigning isn’t easy, and sometimes it feels like the weight of the world is on my shoulders. Just before I typed this email, my team reminded me about our upcoming End-of-Month fundraising deadline. This isn’t just an arbitrary deadline; this is one of our last BIG goals before the November election. I’m not going to ask you to dig deep into your pockets. All I’m asking is a $1 or more donation, which will go right into my campaign's war chest and help me and President Trump take down the Democrat machine come November. As a combat veteran and a patriot - I give you my word that every dollar matters, and I’m eternally thankful for ANY gift you can make. Time is running out. body:
5 unelected bureaucrats just banned most of California's affordable tires. Sign Assemblyman Tri Ta's petition to fight back.
# Gavin Newsom's Bureaucrats Just Banned Your Affordable Tires.
Dpwillis67,
Five bureaucrats appointed by Governor Gavin Newsom just voted to ban up to **70% of the replacement tires** sold in California — including most of the affordable models drivers rely on.
No vote. No public input. Just the California Energy Commission deciding what goes on your car.
**About Assemblyman Tri Ta (AD-70):** Son of Vietnamese refugees who fled communism, raised in Little Saigon, former Mayor of Westminster. Now California's most vocal opponent of Newsom's tire ban.
[Sign Assemblyman Tri Ta's Petition ->](https://listmonk.server2.io/link/6a94b07c-8de5-493f-974e-73d6afd6d881/f6848afb-76b8-4266-b698-9d48ed995c52/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000)
## The Savings Are a Promise. The Cost Is Now.
When affordable tires disappear, families delay replacing worn ones — more blowouts, worse traction, longer stopping distances. This is a safety crisis, not just an affordability one.
[Add Your Name: Stop the Tire Ban ->](https://listmonk.server2.io/link/6a94b07c-8de5-493f-974e-73d6afd6d881/f6848afb-76b8-4266-b698-9d48ed995c52/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000)
**What Newsom's tire mandate means for California families:**
✓ Up to 70% of today's replacement tires — most of the affordable models — banned
✓ Families forced to pay more, decided by 5 unelected appointees
✓ Worn tires stay on the road longer, raising accident risk
**Assemblyman Tri Ta is fighting back. Sign the petition now.**
[Sign the Petition ->](https://listmonk.server2.io/link/6a94b07c-8de5-493f-974e-73d6afd6d881/f6848afb-76b8-4266-b698-9d48ed995c52/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000)

So, I want to say thanks for setting aside party affiliation for a second and hearing me out. You see, I'm not a progressive. And I'm definitely not a Democratic Socialist. I'm just a senator with a big mouth who happens to stand for common-sense things like... strong borders, safe streets, a powerful economy, bringing jobs to my constituents, and Israel and Ukraine's right to defend themselves, not to mention the basic machinery of our democracy (the Electoral College, the Senate, and the Supreme Court). If you see eye-to-eye with me, then I could sure use your help. The "DSA!" vision for Pennsylvania and for America is not a healthy one. It is a dangerous one.Common-sense people need to join together now to reject this vision before it's too late. | | | | | | Paid for by Fetterman for PA P.O Box 6061 Pittsburgh, PA 15211 |

Two NFL players were fined this month for words written on their faces. Not for hitting anyone. Not for breaking a rule of play. For ink.
Kei'Trel Clark, a backup cornerback for the Cardinals, owes the league $6,651 for writing "Glory Be 2 God ✌️" on his eye black. Azeez Al-Shaair, the Texans linebacker, owes $11,492 (some league-confirmed reports say $11,941) for writing "Hind Rajab" -- the name of a five-year-old Palestinian girl killed in Gaza in 2024. Al-Shaair, notably, has now been fined three times for eye black, totaling roughly $35,000: last January it was "Stop the Genocide."
The league's defenders will point to Rule 5, Section 4, Article 8, which prohibits players from displaying "personal messages" while visible to the stadium or television audience. Case closed, right?
Not quite. Because that same rule contains a carve-out: personal messages are prohibited unless they've been approved by the league office. Read that again. This isn't a ban on messaging. It's a monopoly on messaging.

clean_body: Two rating shifts in a month and Abbott just placed his first negative ad buy of the race. He’s scared. Peter, In the same 24 hours that Fox News moved the Texas governor’s race even further away from him, Greg Abbott did something he’s never done before in this race: he went negative on TV. Abbott just launched a $12 MILLION attack ad buy against me — his first negative spending of the entire campaign. Let’s be clear about why this is happening. Fox News has now moved this race in our direction twice in a month, from Solid Republican to Likely Republican in August and from Likely Republican to Lean Republican today. Abbott even reversed course on his own data center policy this week as the pressure mounted. Now he’s panic-spending millions on attack ads. Abbott wouldn’t spend $12 million on negative attack ads against a candidate he thought he was beating easily. He’s opening his firehose of money to drown us out because he’s scared. We knew the attacks were coming. What we need is the resources to answer them, get our message in front of Texas voters, and keep our momentum going for the next six weeks until November 3. disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY THE INDIANA REPUBLICAN STATE COMMITTEE
body:
No images? [Click here](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-e-firhhhy-hhlljjcji-h/) **For Immediate Release:** September 22, 2026**Contact:** Kylie Glatfelter, Communications Director, [kglatfelter@indiana.gop](mailto:kglatfelter@indiana.gop)**Bayh Runs on His Last Name, Not His Party****Indianapolis, Ind. **- Beau Bayh has run television ads across Indiana for weeks now. Not one of them says the word "Democrat." That's not an accident. It's a strategy, because Bayh knows exactly what his party stands for, and he knows it doesn't sell in this state. Bayh is the Democratic nominee for Indiana Secretary of State. He accepted that nomination at the Indiana Democratic Party's state convention this June, less than a mile from a federal building named after his own grandfather, Democratic Senator Birch Bayh. Yet three months later, his campaign still won't put the word "Democrat" anywhere near his name. Bayh's ads never mention his party. His signage doesn't either. Compare that to Max Engling, whose website and social media have identified him as the Republican nominee from day one."Beau Bayh seems determined to run away from the Democratic label, but Hoosiers know which party nominated him," said Indiana Republican Party Chairwoman Lana Keesling. "A familiar last name doesn't substitute for a record of his own, and leaving the word 'Democrat' out of his ads doesn't change the fact that he is the Democratic nominee. Max Engling, on the other hand, has been clear about who he is, what he believes and what he'll fight for from day one." This November, voters have a clear choice: a Republican who's told them exactly who he is and what he believes from day one, or a Democrat too afraid of his own party label to put it on a yard sign, hoping his last name lets him skip the hard part.### [](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-firhhhy-hhlljjcji-r/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-firhhhy-hhlljjcji-y/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-firhhhy-hhlljjcji-j/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-firhhhy-hhlljjcji-t/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-firhhhy-hhlljjcji-i/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-firhhhy-hhlljjcji-d/) ** PAID FOR BY THE INDIANA REPUBLICAN STATE COMMITTEE. ****NOT AUTHORIZED BY ANY CANDIDATE OR CANDIDATE'S COMMITTEE. ****WWW.INDIANA.GOP.** | Indiana Republican State Committee 101 W. | The MAGA Offers | Dear Reader,
On June 18th, an advancement to a potential Digital Dollar happened...
And most Americans didn’t even notice it.
Five federal agencies, including the Federal Reserve, proposed a rule that would tie your identity to _every_ digital dollar transaction you make.
[](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjUwMDh9AAwAAAAAAxvivzChUTosXuI3KWjCYJQ7wcIpj-AEwH2plfPbNOdwUcYOry-BSQZiS3HmSLnYUq_fu73BmRkaeqTtUu0Gruzyo23_iei0wIU0NpXO)
The Fed wants certain stablecoin (digital forms of a dollar) companies to start identifying users just like banks do.
And the scary thing is...
It’s being framed as a consumer protection measure.
[](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjUwMDh9AAwAAAAAAxvivzCiosqdCD27cDNHh45_zPYdeW13kl55TLRJmq-pIUuUfzoAKyBQ8_g90QX0UzW9XLQE-O0Np4Re5ssC70D6QGNBJXo0o_JueUQ2)
It always is...isn’t it?
Like back in 1971, when the dollar was cut from gold.
Americans were told it was necessary and temporary...
**And yet, 50+ years later...your dollar has never been backed by gold again.**
Now, most people will completely ignore this ruling by The Federal Reserve...
And they’ll think:
“Whatever, it’s just another regulation.”
But this is EXACTLY why it matters.
Because although this may not be the Digital Dollar itself...
**It could certainly be an advancement to a Digital Dollar.**
One in which every digital dollar is tied to an identity...
And it’ll likely get more regulated through a series of ‘harmless’ rules just like this one.
That’s why I recorded this free presentation on our **[“Digital Dollar Immunity” System](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjUwMDh9AAwAAAAAAxvivzCj1i_myPmgLiEwhDkH99PVs67IFAQDQ7lOCILWx-O0Wq_LVIon4kMMBeHTaESEvVUZq2IhjHzWC8RRqgFdnPDrJ97IXRw6bDns)** \- allowing us to opt out of a digital dollar if it hits.

**[Click Here To Reveal The “Digital Dollar Immunity” System →](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjUwMDh9AAwAAAAAAxvivzCkVBpbl13YR1Ig_4r3wrvavseHiymkZwpv9-9XPTtg8bvbNnTWDQJ4fLI1UJY2Qlr5eDQA6dJyVma5jJcFGGQZX-JmbjlqIged)**
We already have 4,500+ members doing this.
If you have $50k+ saved for retirement...
And you want to protect your family from whatever comes next...
I strongly suggest you watch this now:
**[Click Here To Reveal The “Digital Dollar Immunity” System →](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjUwMDh9AAwAAAAAAxvivzClKk8s3kbeLLvSrJFNbUHk43BZJ7EIz-5pW4lUrNTqCg9QTZpH1qXXZeB7Yk7QEbeQBMiG6nq7k5WCEdKNdJwwEG8rpu4qMbX_)**
To your wealth,
Tan Gera, CFA©
Decentralized Masters

name: Cooper HQ
subject: Seriously worrying trend
body:
The GOP is outspending us – by a lot.
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1412&source=&t=1&akid=3823%2E124072%2EAeiB_f) | | | |
---
Peter, we're worried.
The election is just over a month away. The polls show this race is _super_ close – and we’re falling short of our fundraising goals.
[**_If you’re able to chip in for the first time today to help us get back on track, it would make a big difference to November’s outcome – and we’d really appreciate it._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1412&amount=5&t=8&akid=3823%2E124072%2EAeiB_f)
Because frankly, we can’t afford to miss a single fundraising target from here on out:
Republican super PACs are pouring over $100 million into this race to crush our momentum. President Trump and Vance personally came to North Carolina to spread lies about Roy within a single week. The GOP’s efforts are working – the polls are now **statistically tied.** If we don’t turn this concerning trend around, we could be in real trouble come Election Day.
Roy has never lost a race. He’s still got a razor-thin lead in the polls. We have incredible grassroots support. But it won’t matter if we keep getting outspent by the GOP.

body:
Her base has a doorman. Mine has a dog on the porch.

| [](https://trk.email.tim-burchett.-nhBLA)
---
[A radical Democrat wants my job.](https://trk.email.tim-burchett.-6iUWDQ)
I won't say her name. She's got an army of folks saying it for her, and not one of them could find Knoxville on a map.
---
[](https://trk.email.tim-burchett.)
---
Washington. New York. San Francisco. That's her base. That's her people. That's who's writing the checks - fat (or as the libs say, “pleasantly plump”) ones.
She's betting on one thing: that y’all won't look too close before November.
So let's look closely.
* Abortion: Not "reproductive healthcare." Not "choice." Not whatever focus-grouped label they're hiding behind this week.
* Trans surgeries on children: Kids too young for a tattoo. Too young for a beer. Too young to rent a car. Old enough, she reckons, for a scalpel.
* Gun Control: They'll call it "common sense" right up until somebody's reading names off a confiscation list. I'd bet the farm mine's at the top.

That's her agenda. Here's mine:
* I'll continue to chainsaw Washington's spending addiction as chairman of the DOGE subcommittee.
* I'll defend the Second Amendment as the God-given right it is — not a privilege some bureaucrat hands out.
* And I'll continue standing up for Tennessee values in a city that treats them like a punchline at a cocktail party.

That's the contrast in this race. Ain't close or complicated.
But I'd be doing you wrong to sugarcoat this, Peter: [a good record doesn't win elections by itself anymore.](https://trk.email.tim-burchett.)
They've got the donors, consultants in three time zones. and a machine built to swallow districts like ours whole and never even burp.
The only thing between them and my seat is patriots like you, Peter.
[Please, chip in a few bucks right now and show them East Tennessee isn't a prize sitting on a shelf with a price tag hanging off it](https://trk.email.tim-burchett.-afMZhfIQZltg).
---
| [CHIP IN NOW →](https://trk.email.tim-burchett.-XRYyzS_q91mUCtg)

Thank y'all for sending me here,

## Trump Tells UN He May 'Annihilate' Iran
President Trump told [the U.N. General Assembly](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLvO3CAUhJ_G7rC4-EZBkcbdpk1pHcPBPhEGC9i19u2j3Sr9384njeabP4_1ARQo7r_hRFN9WiPeJWCtmNean-dVnrFciPY4IXraj1pyWiWXI-OaSbWCrfTCtYfWGY8oUbVoxKS5GCat-vYw0rvZD7Of-Sy8nlCNbht6MTrnuNDj1pL59HEtleB8UKITflYCrLbTBh5ha3qOjmrK3d9EsR7owzu9MHc2nW0wR61XadSvRi6NXO777uJmPx4f3sjlSoEq2dLI5avEwJ0UqdQMlVL8L3YZS2HPSBUdi19a2I4RMwQGpeC5hTejDJHdkFm2EQat-Ty02bjrphCojFPT8_0ECt959Yevvoz8FwAA___6v5Fs) on Tuesday that he is weighing whether to strike a deal with Iran or "annihilate" the Islamic Republic and predicted a deal would come only after November's midterms. Also in his speech, Trump called Cuba a failed state and said it would fall, leading Cuba's delegation to walk out. [Watch it here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGOnDAQxvGnMd2szJhdjoJio4jqLk2KpEODGS9OjI3sYdG9fcTmEa6e0Sf9f78-xg_ywcfHD1q5F5fGyEcJLMJ5lLyvW9lj2ZjtslJ0_rFIyWlEjTfQHaAZyYp_8thQNfeOGdlU3Ndtp-tr25mmWvqpbbF1aEm_6abjhmxT32w3zWRcO92ule_PPd2hqbW-mvpSuzdTk-1sO5FjmlSjefaS8uVP8lEWduEzPTlfbFqr0C8iW1HmrnBQOBzHcVlLPG8KB46wF4XDmaVwSLJwVjjYfaIIMwd-kPgU4aDwt0DaBZKDPQKVwusUPoEKvBxgyhTnAvH_P4EjH3iGIiSscHh6uN_Rvv--viszJOtnZb5_O2X5KD85b1Xu5-3wIfhya1WjHyv58CqQL8I_e_wXAAD__zQvm94). Trump also noted that the U.S. will start referring to artificial intelligence as "superintelligence" in official documents, and that his administration will encourage it rather than rein it in. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian addresses the assembly on Wednesday, and Trump told the media he would "probably" be open to meeting him. [Watch Trump's full address here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGSpCAQgOGnwWwsaHQcAoJLzObSC60GG-UOwYIep-7tt3b3ETb5wy_4_zyXJ8YU8_YbD7IcypLp3RIxU124vo6zvXI7ifx-YA5x27nVsoCE-02aG-gFPceLlgG71QYiIN2RVZORapyMHrrdOueldyPAQ-LojTZqXKdHWMcwoJPSd9F-etKAVlKOWvUqPLRCb_zkMBA6MUhaI5fa_y0x804h_S8X1d6Xo0t2Zz6b0L8EzALmNzm--lfuS90EzJQFzNgasYD5n5q-e21c8H501a7nO6YU230Sg9wOjOlL5R_OuCx8BAAA__89zXSL).
## September Nor'easter Aims at New England
A rare September [nor'easter is expected](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL9q9DAQxJ9G7nxIWp__FCo--HB3aUJIadbyylYiS0bau-PePjivkGZgGBhmfp-36YY--Li-4U6GXZoiPUsgZsoT5_t-lHssB5HddozOrxuXnCYtdVvLodYwoWX_oKnBajGOSBNUZFQ3SHXtBmiqzVhF155QSsABFxwIlMN-dppAwdx3lTdnnxw0KCmvoC7K9aDQDrab0RHOopG0eE758pV85I1ceKUH5YtNexXMxnwUAf-EHoUecbbnhzMTevx4F3qMKRMWplxvhIuPa33a2qZTn0TfFJc6IFPh2qVMFgsLPRZO-SVg9IuA_wratmm1giqb5Xj6EHxpO9HIdUcffpfwHwE-jP4JAAD__2mWh2U) to hit the East Coast this weekend, with Boston and Cape Cod in line for the worst of it. The latest track keeps the storm east of New York City. Eastern Massachusetts could see several inches of rain and [coastal gusts of 40 to 55 mph](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD2OpDAUhE9jMiP_AUvgYBOy3nRD9LCfG-8aG9mvG83tR0wwF5iwqqRS1ff3sT4gppiff-BAS6GsGa-WkAjrSvV1nO2V24no9gNyiM-dWi2rEmrkYuZKr-AovnE10HkbEBXqDq2cZiGHadam262Xg5mMnwJCED5MfpCj18pIbUYl3NBFe_eJWWkpxKBlL8MvLcHNbtogIGzMCPSRSu3_lZhpx5A-yhtr78rRJbsTnY3p30wtTC3XdfVua_ePO2dq2Uqjkplabu9b8wP4hUA7Vh5KRQeN-IX4H7PnZyHMFCHxXCpCI6xMLV21_rxiSrGNEzPieUBMXyPoh-zeVn0GAAD__xgLh30) from Saturday into Tuesday, with flooding along northeast-facing shores. Residents and travelers should expect flight disruptions between New York and Boston and coastal flooding from North Carolina to New Jersey as swells meet a full moon's high tides. [Check your local forecast here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykzz1u7CAUQOHV2N1Y_NkMBcVrppvXpkR38MUQYWPBHaPsPkq2kAWcI30fT_eElNOx_YcdLYXiDuwtIxFWR_W9n-19tBPRxx2OkLZIrRYnmFhuzNyEdOApXegUjKsNiALliJZrw_isjVRjtMGo-cU595qh9rMRZglM3iVbuQJY5jHZnx8zQnLGZsknHu6SgzdevyAgvAbFcE1U6vRZ0kERQ_4qF9bJl33MNhKdbZD_BvEYxKP3PnUEilinrVyDeIzVrmdPOae26EGxbYeUf1v6I_my4jsAAP__qHprwQ). On the other coast, California Gov. Gavin Newsom [declared a state of emergency](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDGu5CAMhk9DuozAyQyhoNiG7m27ZeRHzIQVgQg8E83tV-wVXmdLnz_b_5-v9Qtjivn5Gw-yHMqa6WqJmKmuXF_H2V65nUR-PzCH-Ny51bKChMcozQjTip7jm9YZh80GIqBpIKu0kequzTQPu8U7bLMmI33QflEPpeVCBqWByTxo3oZou6_3Ssr7pG4qLJNCb7z-xkD4LWZJW-RSb39LzLxTSJ_ypnrz5RiS3ZnPJqZfApwAd13X7dWQy4afDghwjUv9CHD9t04Q8k5VgOt7BThpeg0CHKUxx1xGjymGUnPEsQ-VY2yMTCMdVJ-UfbcZtSxaKpBSC3BDtdt5xZRie2gxy-eBMf0_kH-Y69vCvwAAAP__bdSMDg) to prepare for an El Niño winter forecasters say could be the strongest since 1950, with repeated heavy rain, mountain snow, flooding, and landslides expected.

Peter,

Have you been following the whole Ed Sheeran, Macklemore, and Robert Kraft
situation? 👀

TLDR: Billionaire Trump and AIPAC megadonor and New England Patriots owner
Robert Kraft demanded singer Ed Sheeran drop opening act Macklemore from
his tour for his pro-Palestine message on stage.

Other billionaire stadium owners joined Kraft in threatening to pull the
concerts if Macklemore wasn’t dropped. Sheeran caved and cut Macklemore
from the lineup, using a weak “both sides” argument and complaining that
he “never wanted to be an activist-musician.”

In response to his cowardice, Sheeran’s backing band and other opening
acts pulled out in solidarity with Macklemore and the people of Gaza.
Standing on the right side of history in defense of human rights was more
important to them than this career opportunity.

The whole ordeal has been yet another example of the billionaire class and
corporate interests attacking our freedom of speech for the sake of
protecting Israel at all costs — and the public response reflects what we
already knew: the vast majority of people (regardless of party) in the
United States are fed up with enabling a genocidal regime.

And the actions of billionaires like Robert Kraft don’t just affect
concerts and football games, there’s a direct line to our politics and
policies. Kraft has given millions of dollars to AIPAC’s Super PAC,
funding attacks directly against our candidates and movement.

Israel and AIPAC are increasingly unpopular, yet many establishment
Democrats (including leadership) refuse to listen to their constituents
and do what’s right because billionaires like Kraft have bought their
silence.

That’s why we’re keeping up the movement to elect progressive leaders to
Congress who will represent the interests of voters — not a lobby group on
behalf of another country — and stop sending bombs and weapons for Israel
to use against Palestinians.

Peter: According to a release from Secretary Doug Burgum, the Department of the Interior could break ground on the Arc de Trump at any moment.
But since that news broke, Trump’s started flipping the script entirely. Now, he’s trying to turn the arch into a “military installation” to justify its construction as a National Security necessity. It is complete nonsense.
This moment matters, and it’s bigger than the arch alone. It’s a matter of whether we’re going to stop Trump or let him do whatever the hell he wants. We know what side VoteVets is on this. What about you?

---
* * *
[](https://act.votevets.org/go/21732?t=2&akid=35614%2E3013755%2EUcRqIl)
**_Trump Says His Contested Arch Would House Drones and Snipers_**
The president’s announcement on Sunday echoed his justification for the White House ballroom: that the project was necessary for national security.
[](https://act.votevets.org/go/21732?t=3&akid=35614%2E3013755%2EUcRqIl)
---
_Doug Mills/The New York Times_
President Trump said on Sunday his planned 250-foot triumphal arch in Washington would be built to host “large numbers of drones,” snipers and ammunition, as the administration appeared prepared to justify another construction project by citing national security.
Mr. Trump said the arch would be “a top grade Military Complex/Triumphal Arch, to house, store, and have the rapid ability to use large numbers of drones, plus Snipers, on both the roof and plaza areas, and additionally have and hold large quantities of sniper ammunition in storage.” The proposal would appear to place an arsenal and military staging ground in the center of the nation’s capital.
“There will be no facility like this anywhere in the World,” Mr. Trump said in a social media post.
The administration has already been rushing to clear the final hurdles of the arch in recent days, brushing aside concerns from architects, historians and veterans who say it could disrupt the historical area between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery. Now, Mr. Trump appears prepared to return to a familiar playbook he has used to circumvent normal processes and defend some of his more contentious projects in court.
The White House did not immediately answer questions about the sudden need for a giant arch to host drones in a region with a high concentration of military bases and facilities. The Department of Defense declined to provide additional comment beyond Mr. Trump’s social media post.
After initially emphasizing that his ballroom was necessary mainly to host bigger crowds for social events at the White House, Mr. Trump shifted his argument as the $400 million project faced legal scrutiny. He switched to arguing that the construction was a national security imperative because it included a major upgrade to the bunker beneath the now-demolished East Wing of the White House. That argument has appeared persuasive in the Supreme Court hearings over the project.
Mr. Trump has invoked national security concerns for a host of reasons since returning to office. He has cited it as the reason for deploying the military to the U.S.-Mexico border, stripping union rights from thousands of federal workers, pausing the construction of wind farms off the East Coast and exempting oil and gas drilling in the Gulf of Mexico from protections for endangered species of whales.
Even before he said the arch would be turned into a drone-dispatching sniper station, the project had faced scrutiny. When a panel stacked with Trump allies earlier this year gave preliminary approval to the project, it also suggested significant changes to the construction plans.
And the Federal Aviation Administration released a hazard study this week requesting the arch have a constant flame atop the structure to make it safe for planes to pass by in one of the busiest airspaces in the country. The arch would sit along a flight path less than a mile from Ronald Reagan National Airport.
Nicolas Sansone, an attorney with the Public Citizen Litigation Group, which is representing a group of Vietnam War veterans who have sued to stop construction, said Mr. Trump was “trying to paper over a patently unlawful project by giving it a veneer of national security justification.”
The project, he said, continues to be illegal “with or without this concocted justification.” Mr. Sansone added: “It simply has no legal foundation whatsoever unless and until Congress passes a law saying he can build it.”

* * *

**🇺🇸 An Important Message to VoteVets Supporters: 🪖**
You know the Arc de Trump is not a military installation. We know it. Even Trump knows it.
Trump is doing this because he wants you exhausted. He wants us to throw our hands up and let him do whatever he wants. And that’s why it is so important that we don’t.
We need to stay the course, because this is something we can actually do something about. VoteVets will stop the Arc de Trump from being constructed, and we’re humbly asking for your help as we continue this fight.
[**Please, make a donation to help us continue our campaign to defend Arlington National Cemetery and our honored war dead from a 250 foot tall gilded monument to Donald Trump’s ego.**](https://act.votevets.org/go/2927?c0=vv-pac-em-sep26.f1bOKp&refcode=em260923-1-180-b&t=4&akid=35614%2E3013755%2EUcRqIl)

He switched to arguing that the construction was a national security imperative because it included a major upgrade to the bunker beneath the now-demolished East Wing of the White House. That argument has appeared persuasive in the Supreme Court hearings over the project. Mr. Trump has invoked national security concerns for a host of reasons since returning to office. He has cited it as the reason for deploying the military to the U.S.-Mexico border, stripping union rights from thousands of federal workers, pausing the construction of wind farms off the East Coast and exempting oil and gas drilling in the Gulf of Mexico from protections for endangered species of whales. Even before he said the arch would be turned into a drone-dispatching sniper station, the project had faced scrutiny. When a panel stacked with Trump allies earlier this year gave preliminary approval to the project, it also suggested significant changes to the construction plans. And the Federal Aviation Administration released a hazard study this week requesting the arch have a constant flame atop the structure to make it safe for planes to pass by in one of the busiest airspaces in the country. The arch would sit along a flight path less than a mile from Ronald Reagan National Airport. Nicolas Sansone, an attorney with the Public Citizen Litigation Group, which is representing a group of Vietnam War veterans who have sued to stop construction, said Mr. Trump was “trying to paper over a patently unlawful project by giving it a veneer of national security justification.” The project, he said, continues to be illegal “with or without this concocted justification.” Mr. Sansone added: “It simply has no legal foundation whatsoever unless and until Congress passes a law saying he can build it.” 🇺🇸 An Important Message to VoteVets Supporters: 🪖 You know the Arc de Trump is not a military installation. Last March, when I traveled to Cuba on a reporting trip, I had a number of things I was trying to find out, but chief among them was the mystery of the ill-fated assault on Cuba launched from the Florida keys by a band of Cuban-Americans hoping to overthrow the government. The attack was a disaster--it got nicknamed the Bay of Piglets--and ended up with half the men dead and the other half in Cuban custody. Along with Reed Lindsay, a reporter at the great news outlet Belly of the Beast, we pressed the Cuban government for access to the survivors of the boat raid. Four of the five men eventually agreed to speak while still in Cuba's custody. Their stories, of course, must be viewed with skepticism, as is the case with any interview subject who is behind bars and at the mercy of a government. But their stories can be checked against testimony from their comrades, interviews with others back in the United States, and forensic and other evidence from the scene. What follows is the most thorough account to date of the February assault by a band of would-be counterrevolutionaries.
It begins, of course, on TikTok.
--Ryan Grim

Jose Manuel Rodriguez Castello, one of the men detained during a failed attempt to land in Cuba and spark an overthrow of the government on February 25, 2026, during an interview in Havana. Photo: Belly of the Beast.
_Story by Reed Lindsay. Published in collaboration with Belly of the Beast and Miami New Times_
HAVANA, Cuba--Last November, 33-year-old truck driver Jose Manuel Rodriguez Castello was scrolling TikTok when he came across a live video posted by Raul Quevedo, a Cuban living in the United States.
It had been nearly a decade since Rodriguez immigrated to the United States from Cuba via a fiance visa. He later became a permanent resident and was living with his girlfriend and her daughter in Nashville, Tennessee. Still, he harbored deep resentment toward what he saw as a dictatorial government repressing the Cuban people, and he was glad to see Quevedo calling it out.
Quevedo's account, [La Nueva Cuba](https://substack.com/redirect/7ea6e60e-062b-4649-87bf-802cb0e9e569?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (The New Cuba), is largely populated with images depicting armed resistance and an imagined post-communist Cuba, many of them AI-generated. Rodriguez messaged Quevedo. Quevedo messaged him back. The two hit it off, and Rodriguez said that Quevedo invited him to Florida to meet a group of like-minded exiles.
"They were looking for people who had the courage to join an armed uprising in Cuba," Rodriguez said.
Half a year later, Rodriguez would be in Havana, explaining to a reporter how he wound up in Cuban custody--but unbowed in his determination to overthrow the government.
On the evening of February 24, Rodriguez joined nine other men on a fishing boat full of weapons bound for Cuba from the Florida Keys. They planned to seize a police station, ignite an uprising, and prompt U.S. intervention.
"The action plan was simple: Get the Cuban people to rise up in arms, control a province for 72 hours, and ask for a military intervention from the U.S. government," Rodriguez said in an interview.
Rodriguez and the nine other men encountered the Cuban Border Guard before reaching Cuban soil. A firefight broke out, leaving four of the men--Ledian Padron Guevara, Pavel Alling Peña, Michel Ortega Casanova, and Hector Duani Cruz Correa--dead. A fifth, Roberto Álvarez Ávila, would later die from his wounds. The Border Guard suffered no fatal casualties, although the commanding officer of the patrol boat was shot.
Cuban authorities detained the five survivors.**** The incident made major headlines, but the details--what group the men represented, who funded them, and what their ultimate goal was--remained hazy. Drop Site and Belly of the Beast reached out to Cuban authorities to request interviews with the men and officials investigating the incident. In June, Cuban authorities said they had granted the requests and that four of the five survivors agreed to talk.
Jose Manuel Rodriguez Castello, Christian Ernesto Acosta Guevara, Leordan Enrique Cruz Gomez, and Conrado Galindo Sariol all spoke from custody in July while they awaited trial on terrorism-related charges that could carry sentences up to 30 years in prison. The fifth survivor, Amijail Sanchez Gonzalez, is also awaiting trial and either declined to be interviewed or was not permitted to speak to journalists.
These interviews offer the first public account of the failed operation from its participants, but, as with any interview conducted with a person in detention, the conditions were less than ideal. Still, even as the men remained at the mercy of Cuban authorities, some were willing to speak in blunt terms about their hostility to the Cuban government and to complain of mistreatment. Where possible, their accounts have been checked against forensic evidence, property records, and interviews with family members and allies in the United States.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7fb981f5-a8c9-47c8-9adb-e0b71377330a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Clockwise from top left: Christian Ernesto Acosta Guevara, Conrado Galindo Sariol, Leordan Enrique Cruz Gomez, and Jose Manuel Rodriguez Castello. Photos: Belly of the Beast.
## **The Interviews**
The four men were interviewed one at a time in a conference room at a large house in a residential neighborhood of Havana belonging to the Interior Ministry's International Relations Department (MININT). Each was brought to the house in an orange jumpsuit and handcuffs, which an officer from MININT's Special Tactical Unit removed for the interview. Each interview lasted between 30 and 55 minutes. Follow-up interviews were not possible.
The interviews were conducted in the presence of Edward Robert Campbell, the case's prosecutor, and Col. Francisco Estrada Portales, who heads the Interior Ministry's investigations into crimes against national security. All four detainees said they were not pressured into speaking to a journalist or promised anything in return, though that could not be independently verified.
They also said they voluntarily agreed to be interviewed without the presence of legal representation. Their access to lawyers has been uneven. Rodriguez said he had not yet found a lawyer willing to take his case. Cruz said he had not asked for a lawyer yet. Acosta said he had met with his attorney several times. According to his wife, Ana Segui, Galindo has been represented by a lawyer since March.
The four men answered questions about how they became involved, the voyage, the clash with the Cuban Border Guard, and their time in custody. None showed outward signs of duress, but their accounts of their involvement and their attitudes toward the operation varied. Galindo said he had been forced to go; Acosta expressed regret; Cruz remained committed to "freedom" for Cuba but questioned whether armed struggle was the right path; Rodriguez was openly defiant and committed to fighting to overthrow the Cuban government.
Their accounts broadly corroborated one another on the operation's objective and what happened once they encountered the Border Guard. But they diverged over who funded and planned the operation and how involved Cuban exile organizations were. Those unresolved questions center largely on Maritza Lugo Fernandez, a longtime Cuban activist living in Miami who knew most of the ten men on the boat and whom the four men interviewed said provided a small farm in Florida as their training ground.
Cuban authorities also granted interviews with a senior Border Guard official, the MININT's lead investigator, a ballistics expert, a forensic pathologist, the top MININT doctor, and the prosecutor.
## **Recruited on TikTok**
Like Jose Manuel Rodriguez Castello, Christian Ernesto Acosta Guevara found out about the group last year through TikTok. At the time, he was working as a driver for a moving company in Austin, Texas. A permanent resident, Acosta had been in the U.S. for about ten years and planned to apply for citizenship this year.
He connected with Pavel Alling Peña, a 45-year-old naturalized U.S. citizen living in Florida who created a [TikTok account](https://substack.com/redirect/b313fff9-84ae-4092-b03a-62e79618cb57?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in late May 2025 called the Cardumen Movement (_cardumen_ means a school of fish).
"I wrote a comment that I wished Cuba could prosper, be more liberal. That's when he contacted me," Acosta said. "He asked if I wanted a free Cuba. I said yes, I hoped it would happen one day."
Alling invited him to join the Cardumen Movement, Acosta recalled, telling him it was a group dedicated to publishing videos, posters and other material in favor of Cuba's freedom. Later that year, Alling told Acosta about a group of people training for a "military intervention" in Cuba.
"He asked if I was willing to join them and I said no problem, just tell me where," Acosta said. "He said, 'Come to my house, and I'll take you with me."
In November, they went to a _finca_ , or small farm, near Fort Myers, Florida, to begin training. Amid the peppers, sugarcane, and farm animals, there was a rustic shooting range.
Acosta and the other three detainees interviewed said they were told the _finca_ belonged to Maritza Lugo Fernandez, a Cuban-born political activist who runs an anti-communist organization called the Partido 30 de Noviembre (November 30 Party). Lugo denied any knowledge of the operation but confirmed she gave one of the men--Amijail Sanchez--access to the property.
The party [traces its roots](https://substack.com/redirect/cc2b15e8-fdf5-49a8-92e2-a91d29b8310d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to the Movimiento Revolucionario 30 de Noviembre "Frank Pais," an underground anti-Castro group that was founded in Cuba in 1960 and later reorganized in Florida after several of its leaders went into exile. In 1991, the exile movement [helped establish](https://substack.com/redirect/04890972-933d-42f9-b9e9-91d52b043c8b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the 30 de Noviembre Party inside Cuba. Lugo was among its founding members and later assumed its leadership after her husband, Rafael Ibarra Roque, was imprisoned in 1994. She moved to South Florida in 2002 and continued the party's work from exile.
While Acosta and Rodriguez each made multiple trips to the _finca_ to train for the mission, they both insisted they knew few details about what the group's leaders were planning. They identified the leaders as Roberto Álvarez Ávila, who died a week after being shot during the clash with the Cuban Border Guard, and Leordan Enrique Cruz Gomez. Acosta said Amijail Sanchez Gonzalez, co-founder of a militant organization called the Auto Defensa del Pueblo (ADP), was also a leader.
"[The leaders] kept the plans hidden for security reasons, to avoid leaks," Rodriguez said.
In January, the group's leaders asked Acosta, Rodriguez, and several others who had been training to remain at the _finca_ while they readied a boat for the trip to Cuba.
According to Rodriguez's girlfriend, Yeni Rodriguez, he left their house in Nashville on Friday, January 23, telling her he was going to a camp in Florida with some friends. She said he collected magazines about guns and owned two or three firearms, which he took with him. She said he had a full-time job driving a dump truck, hauling dirt and stone to construction sites, and she expected him to return soon.
The operation was a "complete surprise" to her. "Who throws his life away like that?" she said.
Ultimately, Raul Quevedo--a 40-year-old carpenter who runs a [home renovation company](https://substack.com/redirect/e64dbe58-1d52-4c55-a8af-8f33b81eae8d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [incorporated in Bradenton, Florida](https://substack.com/redirect/0f921484-248f-48da-9682-47c4b4ce2011?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in addition to La Nueva Cuba Corp, [registered in the state](https://substack.com/redirect/b1c4caec-65cb-4212-bc7c-d39ab23901a6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) as a nonprofit organization--did not join the other men on the boat. Reached by phone, Quevedo said he was in touch with most of the men through TikTok, but declined to answer questions about his relationship to them and whether he was involved in the operation.
"I have nothing to say about that," he said. "The more you talk, the more your enemy knows about you."
Quevedo said overthrowing the Cuban government is "doable" with enough money, but he was critical of the operation. "It wasn't the right timing. It wasn't the right organization. It wasn't organized," he said. "For something like that, you have to have a plan, structure, a Plan B and Plan C, and an escape plan. If you don't have that, being only 10 people, you're lost. And it's a shame because they were good guys."

## **Trying to Light a Spark, Maybe**
Before the operation, Leordan Cruz Gomez said he lived in Tampa and worked as an industrial painter for a Missouri-based company called Thomas Industrial Coating. He had left Cuba in 2014 aboard a makeshift boat and landed in the Marquesas Keys, later obtaining permanent residency and ultimately U.S. citizenship.
Cruz said someone he met on a WhatsApp group invited him to the _finca_. He said that initially the training there had no specific operation in mind, but the worsening crisis in Cuba--and the relentless stream of desperate images from the island circulating on social media--inspired them to make concrete plans for armed action.
"It had become almost unbearable," said Cruz, who left behind his wife and nine-year-old son. "There was the constant bombardment on social media. Everything we were seeing: mothers with children searching the garbage for food, buildings collapsing, all those crises. That perhaps made it feel more serious."
Since President Donald Trump's first term, the U.S. government has hammered Cuba with "maximum pressure" sanctions that have ravaged the country's economy, fueling unprecedented migration and a growing humanitarian crisis that the UN high commissioner for human rights [says](https://substack.com/redirect/f741d01d-be10-46a9-9d62-14259596e9da?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) is "endangering lives."
However, many Cubans on and off the island blame the Cuban government for the economic crisis. This view has been amplified by social media feeds inundated with content minimizing the role of sanctions--some of it produced by U.S. government-funded media outlets and other organizations, and some coming directly from U.S. officials such as Secretary of State Marco Rubio.
Cruz said he initially began training militarily with an armed group called La Nueva Nacion Cubana en Armas (The New Cuban Nation in Arms)--an organization[ Cuban authorities](https://substack.com/redirect/5c26ad2f-0609-417c-ae85-517729471515?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) allege was behind a 2023 terrorist plot that also aimed to provoke an armed uprising.
But after becoming disillusioned with the group's lack of a political vision for a post-Communist Cuba, he gravitated toward Lugo's 30 de Noviembre Party and the [Republican Party of Cuba](https://substack.com/redirect/6e29ab28-7ccf-458e-9c57-afd743be664d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), a conservative exile group based in Florida.
Cruz said he and the other men began planning the incursion approximately a year in advance. Although he had no formal military training, he attempted to prepare himself by reading books and watching videos of Navy SEALs and Delta Force soldiers. "I often led the military training sessions and taught people how to shoot," he said.
Cruz insisted there were no leaders and decisions were made collectively, although he said Álvarez was more involved in planning the operation.
Although one of the Republican Party of Cuba's members, Michel Ortega Casanova, joined the operation, the group's president, Ibrahim Bosch, denied any links to the armed incursion and said he did not know Cruz.
In a phone interview, Bosch said he knew Ortega, who had led the party in Tampa but had stepped down for work-related reasons.
Bosch said he had heard of training and shooting practice happening at "Maritza's _finca_ ," but was unaware of any plans to stage an incursion and of Ortega's involvement.
"It's possible that some of our people went at the same time as [the men training for the incursion], but they didn't go as Republican Party members to train and shoot, but as individuals," Bosch said.
The plan, according to Cruz, was to seize control of a police station in Cardenas, Matanzas, a city about 90 miles east of Havana, and to then incite people to take the streets. Another member of the group already in Cuba planned to meet the boat on the coast to organize transportation inland, Cruz said. Cuban authorities later arrested Duniel Hernandez Santos, who they allege was the group's ground contact.
(The account Cuban officials obtained through interrogations was slightly different. According to Col. Estrada, the plan was to seize the police station in Santa Marta, about eight miles away from Cardenas, and the nearby Varadero Border Guard Unit. Cruz said he understood only the broad outlines of the operation and that Álvarez had worked out the details.)
"It's illogical to think that 10 men can declare war on a country. That would be absurd," Cruz said. "But we were aware of the social discontent. We knew people wanted something to happen. A spark, maybe."
The men never made it to shore.
## **A Plot in Plain Sight**
As the men honed their shooting skills at the farm and plotted to spark a rebellion in Cuba, they made no secret of their intentions.
On May 29, 2025, two days after creating the Movimiento Cardumen TikTok account, Pavel Alling Peña[ posted an image](https://substack.com/redirect/82ea51ac-6f94-4475-b465-f6b2b5e8b0de?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of two semi-automatic rifles with a text that read: "Collecting funds for Cuba's freedom." In the comments, he wrote: "More information will be provided soon. This didn't just begin. We've been planning this for 2 years. But as you'll understand, there is a lot at stake."
In the following months, Alling's posts offered glimpses of the preparations underway.
Last September, he[ posted a photo](https://substack.com/redirect/3e90082f-0021-449e-b5c0-e526fd2bb328?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of a camouflaged waterproof backpack with the text: "My new acquisition." In a[ selfie video](https://substack.com/redirect/aa36d8ac-764a-4d78-ada7-f342a18d3cd6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) posted a month later, Alling announced: "We are very close. And soon the first steps will be taken."
[](https://substack..RglrXZvBRZ0TlFJeP_Lp1Ybqp0KxNT248QdeUWzn8Ks?/#tiktok-iframe?media=1&app=1&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.tiktok.com%2F%40movimientocardumen%2Fvideo%2F7558882345135131917&key=e27c740634285c9ddc20db64f73358dd)

## **Ten Men, 25 Guns**
After sunset on February 24, the men set out in two boats from Marathon in the Florida Keys.
Cuban authorities said the boats contained weapons and other equipment: 25 firearms--14 long arms and 11 handguns--along with some 13,000 rounds of ammunition, more than 100 magazines, homemade pipe bombs packed with fragments of nuts and bolts and black powder, Molotov cocktails, bulletproof vests, camouflage uniforms and helmets, knives, night-vision equipment, a drone, a Starlink satellite-internet terminal, and medical supplies.
They had purchased one boat for the operation, and they had been told the other was borrowed. About halfway to Cuba, the motor on the purchased boat stopped working, Acosta said. The men transferred their weapons and gear to the other boat--_El Tornado_ --and all ten continued.
_El Tornado_ was a 24-foot Pro-Line fishing boat built in 1981, bearing the Florida registration number FL7726SH. One of the men on board, Hector Duani Cruz Correa, who [had been doing tile work](https://substack.com/redirect/e987c083-fbe1-49a3-9a2e-6e19f90d97d8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) as a contractor for its owner, took the fishing boat.
El Tornado, the 24-foot Florida fishing boat used by the group to travel to Cuba. Investigators documented 23 impacts on the fishing boat and 14 on the Cuban Border Guard vessel.
According to Acosta, Cruz Correa told the group that he had permission to take the boat fishing. The boat's owner, Angel Walter Montera, later[ reported the boat stolen](https://substack.com/redirect/52fe4d70-4d81-47aa-b408-3491ae0337e4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and told the Monroe County police that he wished to press charges.
The men had planned to arrive under cover of darkness, but the breakdown delayed them, according to Cruz Gomez. "We knew that if daylight caught up with us, there was a chance they'd see us," he said.
At approximately 7 a.m., a lookout at a Cuban Border Guard post on Cayo Bahia de Cadiz, a cay off Cuba's northern coast, spotted the boat less than four nautical miles to the northwest. A radar operator confirmed the sighting and began tracking its course and speed, according to First Col. Ybey Carballo Perez, the Border Guard's chief of staff.
Cruz Gomez said they steered the boat toward a small cay near shore, hoping to hide until nightfall. But the tide was out, and _El Tornado_ ran aground in shallow water.
"Almost everyone got out of the boat to try to dislodge it and keep going, and to add more fuel because we were almost out," Acosta said. "That's when we saw a boat coming toward us. We didn't know it was the Border Guard, but we assumed it was. We got the boat free, and everyone got on board."
But _El Tornado_ , at a maximum speed of 24 knots, could not outrun the Border Guard vessel.
"By the time we took off, the Coast Guard boat was almost on top of us," Acosta said. "That's when Leordan Cruz Gomez shouted: 'Get ready. They're going to shoot. Look for the magazines.'"
Most of the weapons aboard _El Tornado_ were wrapped in moving blankets and packed inside bags. "The magazines and the guns were in different bags," Acosta said. The group had expected to slip ashore undetected, Cruz and Rodriguez said--not fight its way onto the island.
Cuban authorities say someone aboard _El Tornado_ fired first, striking the Border Guard captain in the abdomen. All four men confirmed that the first shot came from their own boat.
"One of us fired the first shot. I have to admit that," said Rodriguez, who was the most critical of Cuban authorities. Rodriguez, Cruz and Galindo said they did not know who fired first.
Acosta said Amijail Sanchez took the first shot. "Amijail grabbed a magazine for the Chinese-made AK-47 he had and opened fire on the Coast Guard. That's when a shootout began. I don't know exactly what happened because at that point I got scared and threw myself onto the floor of the boat so I wouldn't get hit by the gunfire," he said.
The five-man Border Guard crew carried just five weapons: the captain's handgun, three AKM assault rifles (a modernized version of an AK-47) and an RPK light machine gun, a longer-barreled relative of the AKM. According to Estrada, none of the five Border Guard officers had combat experience.
Lt. Col. Avelino Guilarte Paumier, the forensics ballistics expert assigned to the case, said that after the shooting, investigators found five rifles and three pistols outside the bags. Spent casings recovered from the boat were matched to just three weapons: a Glock 19 pistol and two Ruger Precision rifles.
Guilarte said the number of recovered shell casings did not necessarily reflect the number of shots fired because the clash occurred on the water and evidence had fallen into the sea. Divers searched the area but found no additional casings, he said.
Nine of the ten men were shot, while on the Cuban side, only the Border Guard captain was wounded. All four men interviewed said they did not fire a shot.
"It was only when I managed to pull out a rifle that a bullet hit me," said Cruz, adding that the all-night voyage had left the men physically depleted and slow to react.
"We had been vomiting [from sea sickness]," he said. "We were wet, cold and exhausted. It kept us from thinking. It paralyzed us."
"At that moment, all I could think to do was put the weapon beside me and lie down in the boat," Acosta said. "I got scared," he added. "I always said back at the farm that shooting at a target, a bullseye, is not the same as facing people in real life who are shooting back at you."
The exchange lasted minutes, according to the survivors and Cuban authorities. Cruz eventually raised an arm to signal surrender. Galindo said one of the Border Guards continued firing until the wounded captain ordered him to stop.
"The captain shouted at him--shouted strongly," Galindo said. "If the captain had let him continue, he would have killed us all."
Ledian Padron Guevara, Hector Duani Cruz Correa, and Pavel Alling Peña died aboard _El Tornado_. Michel Ortega Casanova died while being evacuated. Roberto Álvarez Ávila died a week later, on March 4, from complications associated with his wounds.
Investigators counted 14 bullet impacts on the Border Guard vessel and 23 on _El Tornado_. The boats were moving throughout the firefight, making it difficult to reconstruct events and impossible to establish a precise firing distance, according to Cuban ballistics expert Guilarte.
"We can't know if it was 20, 25, or 30 meters," he said. "What we can show scientifically is that it wasn't at close range." Álvarez was the only one who died from a gunshot wound above the neck--a bullet entered through his shoulder blade and struck him in the jaw--but investigators determined he was not shot at close range.
"Perhaps the idea was somewhat naive because we hadn't prepared for every possible situation," said Cruz. "We weren't prepared to face the Border Guard."
"We had no training to confront the Cuban Border Guard," Rodriguez said.

## **A Long History of Violence --and Impunity**
In the years before the attempted incursion, Cuba had already placed two of its participants--[Amijail Sanchez Gonzalez](https://substack.com/redirect/2ca6deb3-d303-4961-b222-94b227496dc3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in 2023 and[ Leordan Enrique Cruz Gomez](https://substack.com/redirect/e0b89fe6-9c4d-4c54-92a9-8d6fcc6602c6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in 2025--on its national list of terrorism suspects for financing acts of violence on Cuban soil. Cuba also submitted the list to the United Nations as part of its reporting under U.N. Security Council Resolution 1373.
Sanchez's[ Facebook page](https://substack.com/redirect/0f06fa7c-1c73-4241-8c15-8e496de4b2a9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) is littered with videos of burning sugar cane fields in Cuba and graffiti featuring the name of the organization he co-founded, the Auto Defensa del Pueblo, or ADP. The page of [ADP's co-founder](https://substack.com/redirect/4b2f406c-1c85-49de-bfeb-fc800e7d0ece?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Michel "Kiki" Naranjo Riveron,[ features a post](https://substack.com/redirect/39ee113b-a7ec-436b-af7e-20da13dfa10a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) offering to pay $1,000 to anyone who kills a Cuban police officer.
"Burning a building, cutting fiber optic cables in Camaguey, lighting fire to a hospital, burning an electrical generator," Col. Estrada said. "In a year and a half, one person [in Cuba] committed 18 acts of terrorism that were financed by Amijail and his organization, the Auto Defensa del Pueblo, designated as a terrorist organization and which is based and acts openly in the United States."
The U.S. has not designated this organization as a terrorist group. Nor is there any indication that U.S. authorities took any action to dissuade Sanchez, who in 2021 [was convicted](https://substack.com/redirect/a9475852-8a6d-4def-8dcb-aab87c3e4616?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in Florida of aggravated battery on a law enforcement officer [for striking a moving police car](https://substack.com/redirect/2b4227be-adae-4b4f-adda-435ad4979b24?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with a vehicle he was driving in Miami, and the other men despite their open preparations for armed action in Cuba.
Since the Cuban revolution, the U.S. has frequently tolerated acts of violence and terrorism aimed at overthrowing the communist government.
In March 1960, President Dwight Eisenhower[ approved](https://substack.com/redirect/762de1d0-8668-4b9d-bb34-be481c10e1f0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a[ CIA plan](https://substack.com/redirect/3735f5f8-842c-4c54-975f-a1a5109a0243?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to topple the Cuban government by forming exile groups, launching a radio station to broadcast U.S. propaganda on the island, creating "a covert intelligence and action organization" inside Cuba, and training paramilitary forces outside the island. This culminated in the failed April 1961 Bay of Pigs invasion. Shortly after, the CIA launched Operation Mongoose to coordinate acts of sabotage and terrorism[ aimed at civilian targets](https://substack.com/redirect/c893011e-92f1-486e-9c6d-72fb03edcdb1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in Cuba.
After direct CIA support was phased out, exile paramilitary groups continued staging attacks from Florida. In 1971, when the Coast Guard sought to rein in Alpha 66, a U.S.-based Cuban-American terrorist organization, President Richard Nixon[ wrote](https://substack.com/redirect/81fc42c4-5364-43c5-9832-1a5d018bdda6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg): "We should not inhibit Cuban exile activity against their homeland."
Five years later, two bombs killed 73 people aboard Cubana Flight 455 in the deadliest act of airline terrorism in the Western Hemisphere at the time. The suspected masterminds were paramilitary leaders Orlando Bosch and Luis Posada Carriles. Both men lived in Florida until their deaths and were never prosecuted in the United States for the bombing.
Militants based in Florida and New Jersey also staged attacks on U.S. soil, including [bombings of businesses](https://substack.com/redirect/4be64ed4-69ee-488b-b38d-4754d75e0e30?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that dealt with Cuba and the assassinations of a Cuban diplomat and a Cuban-American advocate for dialogue with Havana. The FBI considered one of the armed groups, Omega 7, to be [the most dangerous terrorist organization](https://substack.com/redirect/3ef1ef98-c2d7-4b57-a293-4fe63c1cd36c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in the United States.
The acts of terrorism continued into the 1990s, as militants in speedboats[ sprayed beachside resorts](https://substack.com/redirect/08128aeb-d41a-47cc-9f6a-e4cbb1ba4e68?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with machine gun fire and a[ bombing campaign](https://substack.com/redirect/aaea5afa-60bf-4745-9323-a4531670a380?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) targeted hotels in Havana, killing an Italian tourist and injuring several others.
In 1998, Cuban officials[ handed the FBI](https://substack.com/redirect/4f3fe845-1e14-477f-b211-ad3cf7d74c36?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) extensive documentation detailing dozens of U.S.-based terrorist plots. The FBI[ responded](https://substack.com/redirect/20fee7d5-fc9d-44c5-9642-90df8b12196c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by arresting undercover Cuban agents in Florida who had infiltrated the terrorist networks.
As recently as December 2023, Cuban authorities[ said](https://substack.com/redirect/cd06a33a-0003-4f51-8be8-c72c4e6a1b66?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) they foiled an attempt by people linked to La Nueva Nacion Cubana en Armas to foment an armed rebellion. They captured a Florida man who had traveled to Cuba with handguns and ammunition on a jet ski and then tried to recruit people to commit acts of violence and arson.
"We've been attacked for 67 years and while it may seem that these things are something of the past, it's not the past," said Col. Estrada, the Interior Ministry investigator. "For those of us working to combat terrorism, we've seen how this type of activity is constantly happening in the United States."
## **Maritza Lugo**
Cuban authorities say the operation involved multiple leaders, but they allege that Maritza Lugo, head of the 30 de Noviembre Party, was its mastermind.
"She was the one who organized, financed and oversaw the logistics of everything," Estrada alleged. "[The _finca_] is where everything was prepared. It's where they trained, prepared, and tested the explosives. Even the [purchased] boat was there. They left from there for the coast, for Marathon Key."
Lugo denies any involvement in the operation. "The Castro regime has accused me endlessly--of being a terrorist, of paying for things," she said. "What could I possibly pay for? I live on [Social Security]. I receive $700 a month, which isn't enough for anything. I try to save. I do odd jobs. My family helps me if I need something extra. But I don't have the money to finance absolutely anything."

Born in 1963 on the outskirts of Havana, Lugo became politically active in the 1990s alongside her then husband, Rafael Ibarra Roque. Together they founded the 30 de Noviembre Party, but Lugo assumed its leadership when Cuban authorities arrested Ibarra in 1994 and [sentenced](https://substack.com/redirect/30f38975-9d09-4710-9325-03b1b0a6dc98?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) him in February 1995 to 20 years for sabotage. Cuban authorities accused Ibarra of setting off an explosive device at a military building. Lugo[ maintains](https://substack.com/redirect/3cd288ee-608e-4c0b-9b7d-338dac406993?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the charges were trumped up.
Lugo herself was[ arrested and imprisoned](https://substack.com/redirect/fc8e2c2b-105e-4c59-bc3d-2736c367320d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) multiple times and[ identified by Amnesty International](https://substack.com/redirect/7cd1b3a7-a198-4f34-a59b-b644af925503?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) as a prisoner of conscience. She[ says](https://substack.com/redirect/637f65d9-d3b4-4ab6-9363-6ae0d8af2382?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) she was kept in isolation and subjected to torture.
In 2002, Lugo left Cuba for South Florida, where she has been a persistent, albeit relatively fringe, presence among Cuba's exile opposition. She has occasionally had the spotlight,[ being interviewed](https://substack.com/redirect/1b059ba7-cdde-490c-9969-ac946e0ff3ab?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) about rights abuses in Cuba,[ appearing](https://substack.com/redirect/2e7c3dc0-b5d9-480f-80e1-2c926737aff7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at a Capitol Hill news conference,[ meeting](https://substack.com/redirect/939e9e07-ab60-4743-9488-49cbdf95c9dd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with members of Congress, and[ greeting](https://substack.com/redirect/4cd2bbf4-d11a-433d-a0a7-3b722c02556b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) President George W. Bush during a White House visit.
Recently, Lugo has also been associated with figures linked to political violence. She was featured prominently at a[ July 2025 event](https://substack.com/redirect/1c231550-54c8-4432-a151-480fef1fe51b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) sponsored by the Hispanic Republican Club of Collier County, Florida, alongside Enrique Tarrio, the former Proud Boys leader[ convicted of seditious conspiracy](https://substack.com/redirect/b4b372c0-8aad-4eba-88e7-96cc3b4a3772?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for his role in the January 6 attack on the Capitol and subsequently[ pardoned by President Donald Trump](https://substack.com/redirect/85fe2532-458c-41c7-be04-dd9c64fabe21?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
In 2018, Lugo[ posted a photo of herself](https://substack.com/redirect/09930d2c-aac5-4c90-8783-da693bd03736?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with Luis Posada Carriles, the paramilitary leader, a month before he died.[ Another photo of their encounter](https://substack.com/redirect/74a5994a-ebd8-46ed-940b-474deb60ef0b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) was posted earlier this year on a Facebook page called "10 Cuban Patriots," which Lugo says she created in support of the men involved in the February incursion. The post praises Posada Carriles as "a great man and friend, a great patriot" and "the terror of the great demon Fidel Castro."

In recent years, Lugo's 30 de Noviembre Party forged an alliance with ADP, which has openly endorsed violence and sabotage as a means of overthrowing the Cuban government. Their relationship was both political and personal. According to Lugo, she was romantically involved with Amijail Sanchez, ADP's co-founder, for about a year, and he was living with her before he joined the incursion.
While ADP was the military arm of the group that went to Cuba, the 30 de Noviembre Party was the political arm, according to Cruz.
"If we succeeded, 30 de Noviembre was the group that would present its political program to the people," he said.
The fatigues and helmets that Cuban authorities say they seized bore patches featuring the insignia of both ADP and the 30 de Noviembre Party.
Since February, Lugo has been most visible as a prominent public advocate for the imprisoned men, organizing events to support them and posting frequently online about their case.
In a telephone interview from Miami, she said she knew most of the men before their ill-fated trip.
Yet, despite her romantic relationship with Sanchez and the alliance between their two organizations, she said she knew nothing about the operation and would have opposed it had she known.
"They are very good people who did something crazy," she said. "They went far beyond the bounds of what is normal because what they did was truly madness. Who in their right mind could think that 10 men could accomplish anything against a dictatorship like that?"
"I am very much in favor, and I've said so publicly, of a military intervention, but a military intervention by the United States, a country that has enough power to overthrow such a cruel regime," she continued. "Trump has all the resources, all the intelligence and all the means necessary for it to succeed and achieve its objective. But doing it the other way is a waste of courage. It's a tragedy for any Cuban to lose their life over something like that."
## **The** _**Finca**_
The Hendry County Property Appraiser's records show Lugo [owned a 13-acre farm](https://substack.com/redirect/64f2c2c2-777b-40d1-ae55-a18a64e9ef6d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in LaBelle, Florida, a rural area an hour east of Fort Myers, from March 2020 until September 2024. She [sold the property to her daughter](https://substack.com/redirect/a7b9547f-15fb-4e9a-b228-e4c10210137e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Rosalia Agnello, and Alexis Martinez, a Miami resident who [took full possession](https://substack.com/redirect/9e5a6b42-a2da-4332-a241-e2dafe78e9eb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in July 2025.
Acosta, Rodriguez, and Cruz said they trained at the farm in the months leading up to the February 2026 operation, even after it was sold to Martinez. But both Martinez and Lugo acknowledge that she continued to have access to the property.
Lugo said that the _finca_ was used for shooting practice and hunting rabbits, doves and wild hogs. "At the _finca_ , you can shoot safely, and it's permitted in that area," she said. "We hunt animals there. We shoot because we like guns."
She said she never witnessed any military training or preparations for an incursion into Cuba. "Anyone who trained on my _finca_ , who said they trained, that's their problem," she said. "Here in the United States, that is against the law. It's a crime."
From his home in Miami, Martinez said Lugo was formerly his romantic partner and that they remained friends. He said he demolished the shooting range shortly after taking full possession of the property, and knew nothing about any training taking place there.
However, in response to an inquiry for this story, Hendry County Sheriff's detectives went to the property in August and observed what appeared to be "a three-sided berm designed for multidimensional shooting exercises."
According to the detectives, the structure appeared designed "to facilitate training that incorporates multiple shooting angles and directions rather than functioning as a traditional shoot house."
The Hendry County Sheriff's Office has received no reports or complaints of any gunshots, explosions or any criminal activity happening at the address, according to Public Information Officer Capt. Susan Harrelle.
The sheifff's office contacted the FBI, ICE, Homeland Security Investigations, the Florida Office of Statewide Prosecution, and the Florida Department of Law Enforcement, but Harrelle said they have received no information confirming that military training took place on the property.
Cruz and Rodriguez said that Lugo was often present while they met and trained, though she was not involved with planning the incursion or obtaining weapons.
"She was always at the _finca_ , helping with the logistics, food, transportation, making sure we weren't lacking for anything," said Rodriguez.
Lugo gave a different account.
"I'm almost always in Miami," she said. "I would go to the _finca_ , spend one, two or three days there, and then return to Miami. [Sanchez] had free rein there and did whatever he wanted because I trusted him."
Rodriguez said individual members of the group provided the weapons. "Nobody ever paid us anything," said Rodriguez. "We were self-financed. We bought our own bullets, our own rifles, our own military equipment."
Lugo was not involved in the planning, Acosta said, but her party was their "sponsor." "What she did mostly was handle the political part," said Rodriguez.
