# Other International News
* **U.S. claims neither Sudanese army nor RSF has legitimate authority** : The U.S. State Department [said](https://substack.com/redirect/da67590c-c52a-441b-9f3c-6b0c23b1e321?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Tuesday that neither Sudan's army nor the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces have legitimate authority to govern the country, with spokesperson Thomas Pigott saying both sides rule "purely through force of arms" and accused both of failing to commit to ceasefire efforts and of escalating the conflict instead.
* The statement called Sudan's war the world's worst humanitarian crisis, and said Washington would work to "raise the cost of continued conflict on all belligerents."
* **South Sudan 's Kiir dissolves transitional government, consolidates power in interim: **South Sudan President Salva Kiir [dissolved](https://substack.com/redirect/5728b3a3-4cc1-4ea1-8918-c1a94db3c2d1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the country's transitional government Tuesday, hours after signing amendments to election laws that removed requirements to complete a permanent constitution and census before holding a vote, in preparation for the country's first-ever national elections.
* The transitional government was originally established under a 2018 peace deal that ended a years-long civil war in the country.
* Under the amended National Elections Act, passed by parliament Monday, Kiir's executive leadership retains full constitutional powers through the election period, and the National Legislative Assembly will shrink from 650 to 270 members, with state assemblies cut from 100 to 58 seats.
* The moves come as Kiir's longtime rival, opposition leader Riek Machar, remains under house arrest since March 2025 and on trial for treason and murder charges he denies.
* Elections were initially expected in 2022 but have been delayed twice.
* **Tigray forces launch offensive against Ethiopia 's government:** Tigrayan forces [launched](https://substack.com/redirect/3d07da11-79ef-4d85-ae48-790addf58f49?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a major offensive against Ethiopia's federal government Wednesday, a senior Ethiopian official said, shattering the Pretoria Agreement that ended the 2020-2022 civil war, with the officials from the Tigray People's Liberation Front saying they entered a "defensive war" against government "aggression."
* Getachew Reda, an adviser to Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed, said the TPLF seized federally controlled airports in Tigray and launched an "all-out offensive" into neighboring Afar and Amhara regions, where Tigrayan forces are fighting alongside local armed groups and the Fano militia. Ethiopian Airlines has suspended flights to Tigray.
* The fighting follows the announcement of a seven-group alliance on Sunday, which declared its aim at overthrowing Abiy's government.
* **Survivors: Nigerian guards sprayed substance into packed cell before 37 detainees died** : Three survivors [told](https://substack.com/redirect/41d2ddf2-faae-41e3-a1b5-e24f57baa353?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Reuters that Nigerian prison guards sprayed an unidentified substance into an overcrowded cell holding dozens of detained gold miners near Minna, then kept the doors locked; 37 detainees died.
* The Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps paramilitary agency jailed the miners after raiding suspected illegal mining sites. Many of those jailed were teenagers.
* President Bola Ahmed Tinubu ordered an investigation in response. The deaths, which authorities initially attributed to a possible disease outbreak before saying the cause remains under investigation, sparked protests that turned deadly Friday, leading officials in the country's Niger state to impose a 24-hour curfew.
* **Venezuelan opposition leader Machado makes unsuccessful bids to return home, adviser says:** Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado [made](https://substack.com/redirect/5bec276a-327e-4568-a480-5fb6e7c9c53e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) three unsuccessful attempts by sea and air to return to Venezuela in recent hours, her adviser Pedro Urruchurtu said on social media, bringing her total failed return attempts to seven since she clandestinely left the country nine months ago, according to the Spanish newspaper ABC.
* The paper did not report who blocked her Tuesday attempts.
* Machado's efforts coincided with interim President Delcy Rodriguez's first meeting with President Trump in New York following President Nicolas Maduro's capture by U.S. forces in a January raid.
* **Alleged fentanyl trafficker arrested in Mexico City in joint U.S.-Mexico operation** : Mexican authorities [arrested](https://substack.com/redirect/63b8a501-9fa0-4229-8a7b-625c389f5fa4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Jose Angel Rivera, known as "Don Flaco," in Mexico City Tuesday for allegedly coordinating and financing an organization that transported fentanyl chemical precursors from China to Mexico and the U.S., in a joint operation with the FBI and DEA, Security Minister Omar Garcia Harfuch said on X.
* Rivera had been sanctioned by the U.S. State Department in January 2023 over his alleged role in fentanyl trafficking.
* Harfuch said the arrest reflected "international cooperation, shared responsibility, and unrestricted respect for our sovereignty."
* The arrest came the same day President Trump told the United Nations that Mexico was "the epicenter" of drug cartel violence and needed to "reclaim control of its territory."
* **Taiwan says it will stay in "close contact" with U.S. on arms sales:** Taiwan's defense ministry [said](https://substack.com/redirect/e00b5b81-291c-4217-9072-a6237aaa5361?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Wednesday it would continue close coordination with the U.S. to implement arms sales "according to plan," ahead of an expected meeting between President Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington this week, where Xi is expected to press Trump to halt the sales.
* A $14 billion arms package remains in abeyance following Trump's December approval of an $11 billion package, the largest ever.
* **UN report finds Nicaragua 's crackdown on dissent amounts to crimes against humanity**: Nicaraguan state institutions, coordinated through a chain of command reaching senior government levels, have [carried](https://substack.com/redirect/3c2700f6-5cf3-4adb-b2cd-cd9b57b9809b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) out enforced disappearances, torture, and arbitrary detention of political opponents amounting to crimes against humanity, according to a report published by UN human rights officials on Tuesday.
* The report documents 161 cases of enforced disappearance and eight deaths in state custody since April 2018.
* The report also noted a shift, beginning in 2023, toward long-term disappearances and nationwide police raids targeting dissidents, church members, Indigenous leaders, and former officials. Female detainees have been subjected to threats of sexual violence.
* In July, Ortega said that Nicaragua would no longer hold elections, and in September, Nicaragua's Congress passed a constitutional reform banning opposition parties from participating in future votes.

This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday UN General Assembly Trump threatens to "annihilate" Iran: During his speech before the UN General Assembly on Tuesday, President Donald Trump to "annihilate the Islamic republic" of Iran if the two countries fail to reach a deal. "Will a deal be made with Iran that lets them rebuild and create a far greater country than it ever was before, maybe one of the greatest in the Middle East or even the world?" Trump said, suggesting that Iran was waiting to see the outcome of the midterm elections. "Or do I annihilate the Islamic Republic and do it quickly, never giving them a chance to kill and destroy people and countries again?" Trump also defended recent U.S. moves in the Western Hemisphere, saying "to the victor belong the spoils" when he discussed the U.S.'s seizure of Venezuelan oil after U.S. forces snatched Venezuelan president Nicolas Maduro from his home in Caracas. He called Cuba a "failed state" that serves as a "haven for foreign adversaries to threaten America," and said its government would soon fall. These remarks prompted Cuban delegates to walk out. Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodriguez Parrilla later said: "The U.S. government proves incapable of accepting that Cuba is, and has the right to be, a fully independent and sovereign country." Trump also attacked the International Criminal Court as a "rogue institution," called for its members to resign, and dismissed climate change as a "hoax." He rejected any "globalist scheme" to control advances in artificial intelligence, which he proposed be called "super intelligence," as a "test" of his influence on the world stage. Iran military warns of "more crushing" attacks after Trump threats: Iran's military warned Wednesday that it was prepared to launch "more crushing and less predictable" attacks against the U.S. and Israel after Trump threatened to "annihilate" the Islamic Republic during his UN General Assembly address Tuesday. Responding in a carried by Mehr, Iran's General Staff of the Armed Forces and the Khatam Al-Anbiya Central Command accused Trump of using the UN podium to justify U.S. "aggression" and described his threats as evidence of Washington's "strategic desperation," warning that Iranian forces were prepared to strike the U.S. and Israel with attacks more severe than those carried out earlier in the war. Lula warns against foreign election interference, defends Brazil 's sovereignty: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva Tuesday against domestic or foreign interference in Brazil's October 4 election, telling the UN General Assembly "Brazilian democracy belongs to Brazilians" and "Brazil will remain a sovereign country." Lula did not name Trump directly, though he did appear to reference the United States when he condemned the resurgence of "hegemonic ambitions" in the region and asserted that the country did not "need aircraft carriers in its waters," a probable reference to the U.S.'s Operation Southern Spear. "Brazil does not belong in anyone's backyard," he said, calling attempts to divide the world into spheres of influence "anachronistic." Lula's comments follow accusations that the Trump administration, allied with his election rival Sen. Flavio Bolsonaro, is trying to influence the vote through economic pressure, after Washington imposed two new rounds of tariffs on Brazilian goods in July. Macron condemns Israeli aid restrictions in UNGA speech; UK, France, Canada talk Palestinian statehood in committee: French President Emmanuel Macron Israel's aid restrictions on Gaza as "a shame for the world" in his UN General Assembly address Tuesday, asking "what credibility do we have if we continue to remain inactive in the face of Gaza?" Macron also criticized what he characterized as Israel's "daily" violations in the occupied West Bank. Macron, alongside UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham, Canadian Prime Minister Mike Carney and Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud, chaired a meeting on Palestinian statehood, where Burnham warned that failing to deliver a two-state solution "will corrode trust in the political, diplomatic, and international process." Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney also announced his intention to introduce restrictions on goods produced in West Bank settlements, following the UK's earlier announcement of similar restrictions. U.S.-Iran UN hold first indirect talks since June MOU unraveled: Trump administration special envoy Steve Witkoff said U.S.-Iran talks on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly were conducted through mediators who shuttled between the two delegations, clarifying that the sides did not hold direct discussions after President Donald Trump said Tuesday that three-hour talks with the Iranian delegation had been "very good." Iran separately said the communications took place through a Qatari mediator and that Tehran presented conditions for ending the war, including an end to U.S. "acts of aggression," a halt to the naval blockade and economic warfare, and the release of Iranian assets. Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei said Iran maintained its negotiating stance in the discussions. "This was not anything new," Baghaei said of Iran's conditions. Witkoff said, in a on X, the mediators had completed a round of discussions that he hoped would prove "constructive and promising" and would continue their work. Macron says France ready for greater role in reopening Strait of Hormuz: French President Emmanuel Macron France was prepared to become more involved in efforts to secure transit through the Strait of Hormuz, while stressing that Paris did not want a confrontation with any country. Macron told ABC News that the "main objective" of his meeting with Trump was to find an agreement to reopen the vital waterway and address the global energy crisis. He reiterated France's opposition to the U.S. decision to go to war with Iran, saying "regime change by bombing a country" was not feasible and that Washington had not consulted its allies before launching the war. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi met French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly and criticized France's "interventionist" positions toward Iran and its stance on U.S. and Israeli attacks. U.S., Denmark, Greenland sign deal expanding U.S. military presence : The United States, Denmark and Greenland signed an agreement Tuesday at the UN General Assembly granting Washington expanded military access to Greenland, allowing it to modernize the Pituffik Space Base and build new facilities at Narsarsuaq and Mestersvig. The agreement resolves months of tension between the U.S. and Denmark, with President Donald Trump repeatedly threatening to seize the territory. The open-ended agreement bars non-NATO countries from establishing military installations without unanimous approval from Denmark, Greenland and the U.S., restricts investment from "sensitive sectors" outside NATO and the EU, and grants the U.S. undersea access and unrestricted overflight rights. Zelenskyy says Ukraine ready for energy truce after "productive" Trump talks: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said after a 40-minute meeting with President Donald Trump in New York at the UN that Ukraine remains ready for a bilateral "energy ceasefire" with Russia, telling reporters "we are ready" to halt strikes on Russian refineries if Moscow stops targeting Ukraine's energy system. Separately on Tuesday, Zelenskyy warned on Telegram that Ukrainian intelligence indicated Russia was "preparing a new massive attack" against Ukraine. Trump called his talks with the Ukrainian president "positive and productive" and said ending the war is likely, though a similar energy truce he announced last week collapsed almost immediately after strikes resumed. Zelenskyy also said he asked Trump for additional Patriot air defense missiles for winter, proposing to swap future Patriot deliveries from a German deal in exchange for supplies from U.S. stockpiles now, though Trump had not yet agreed to this arrangement. U.S. withholds visa for Sudan 's Burhan, tying it to ceasefire proposal Khartoum has resisted: The United States is a visa for Sudanese army chief Abdel Fattah al-Burhan ahead of his scheduled UN General Assembly speech, contingent on his acceptance of a 90-day ceasefire proposed by U.S. Senior Advisor Massad Boulos, Reuters reported. The suspension prompted Sudan's UN ambassador to appeal to Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, who said he is "deeply concerned" and engaging with the U.S. on the issue. Canada pledges $71 million in Palestinian aid, imposes restrictions on Israeli settlement goods: Canada will provide about $71 million in assistance for the Palestinian government and impose trade restrictions on goods produced in Israeli settlements, Prime Minister Mark Carney said Tuesday on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York. He described the restrictions on settlement products as a "pragmatic, practical" measure intended to help preserve "the possibility of a two-state solution, and ultimately a durable peace for Israelis and Palestinians." Trump and Latin America allies invoke Rio Treaty against cartels: The Trump administration is seeking to turn its campaign against Latin American cartels into a hemispheric security framework under the umbrella of the Shield of the Americas initiative. Fourteen governments joined a U.S.-backed declaration at the UN General Assembly pledging coordinated action against 24 organizations designated as "narco-terrorist". The declaration calls for sanctions, intelligence sharing, security cooperation and a commitment to invoke the Inter-American Treaty of Reciprocal Assistance, or Rio Treaty, to consider collective military action against the groups. Yemen Ansarallah, Saudi-backed forces clash near Bab al-Mandab: Ansarallah and Saudi-backed forces are fighting over the strategic area linking Taiz and Lahj governorates with Yemen's western coast near the Bab al-Mandab Strait. Ansarallah military spokesperson Yahya Saree said the group shot down an armed reconnaissance drone conducting "hostile missions" over Mocha in Taiz governorate. On the opposing side, the Saudi-backed National Shield Brigades claimed they repelled an Ansarallah offensive in the strategic Kahboub mountain range and shot down three Ansarallah drones before they could reach their positions. The Southern Giants Brigades, also deployed along the front, said they were continuing to target Ansarallah fortifications and reinforcements. Iran Cargo vessel hit by projectile in Strait of Hormuz: A cargo vessel was struck by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, leaving the ship on fire and adrift and causing two casualties, the UK Maritime Trade Operations said. All crew members were evacuated from the vessel and no environmental impact was reported. New U.S. sanctions on Iranian aviation take effect: A new package of U.S. sanctions targeting Iran's aviation sector took effect Wednesday, after Washington pledged to ground Iranian airlines and penalize entities that continue doing business with them, AFP reported. Iran's Civil Aviation Organization said airports in Baghdad and Muscat would stop receiving Iranian flights from midnight, while negotiations were underway to reroute Baghdad-bound flights to Najaf and reach arrangements with Oman. Other international services, including flights to Istanbul, remained scheduled, according to Tasnim. Iraqi authorities have not formally announced measures, but several sources, including a senior government official, told AFP that Baghdad would comply with the U.S. restrictions. Separately, AFP reported that an Iranian commercial aircraft landed in China despite Washington's threat of sanctions. Palestine Killed and wounded in Gaza: Over the past 24 hours, three Palestinians were killed and 18 injured in Israeli attacks across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 has risen to 73,922 killed, with 174,995 injured. Since October 11, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,402 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 4,881, while 834 bodies have been recovered from under the rubble. Israeli attacks kill six Palestinians across Gaza since dawn: Israeli attacks across the Gaza Strip six Palestinians and wounded others since dawn Wednesday, WAFA reported. In Gaza City, an Israeli drone strike near Al-Wafa Hospital killed one Palestinian and wounded others, while several Palestinians were wounded in a separate attack targeting a group of people near the Abu Khadra complex in the western Rimal neighborhood. In central Gaza, another Israeli drone strike in Deir el-Balah killed one Palestinian and wounded others. Israeli forces carry out demolitions across the occupied West Bank as settlers block Salfit road: Hebron: Israeli forces homes, agricultural structures, livestock pens, and water wells belonging to Palestinian families in Janba village in Masafer Yatta, south of Hebron, on Wednesday, according to WAFA. Jenin: Israeli bulldozers agricultural and residential structures in the Abba village, southeast of Jenin, including four horse stables, greenhouses, sheep pens, a house under construction, a wall, and two agricultural rooms. Salfit: Israeli settlers Wadi Al-Shaer road connecting Salfit city with Al-Lubban Al-Sharqiya by placing rocks and metal spikes on the road, damaging several vehicles before Palestinians removed the obstacles and reopened it. Israeli forces also reclosed the northern entrance to Salfit city. East Jerusalem: Israeli authorities sheet-metal industrial structures belonging to Palestinians in Jaba, northeast of Jerusalem, and bulldozed the surrounding land. Military court extends detention of Palestinian-American journalist: A military court on Wednesday extended the detention of Palestinian-American journalist and Drop Site contributor Naqaa Hamed until September 28, according to her lawyer, Khaled Mahajneh. Hamed was by Israeli forces on September 15 as she was returning from a reporting assignment in the occupied West Bank. Israeli authorities have accused her of incitement against Israeli settlers and the army, communicating with the enemy, and cooperating with the enemy. She is currently being held in Damon Prison in northern Israel. Mahajneh previously told Drop Site "the whole case is related to her journalistic work" and that her arrest came solely because of a campaign targeting her by Israeli settlers. Hamed is a freelance journalist who has worked for various international outlets, including Drop Site News. Maryland Sen. Chris Van Hollen, Michigan Rep. Rashida Tlaib, and other U.S. officials, as well as the Committee to Protect Journalists, have called for her release. Israeli forces arrest senior PA security official : Israeli forces arrested Majdi Amer, a colonel in the Palestinian Authority's Preventive Security Service during an overnight raid on the village of Kafr Qallil, south of Nablus, according to the Times of Israel. In a statement, the Israeli police said that undercover Border Police officers apprehended a "wanted operative in the Fatah terror group." Pregnant Palestinian detainee suffers bleeding, harsh conditions in Israeli prison: Pregnant Palestinian detainee Baraa Abu Khadija, 36, from Tulkarm suffered abdominal pain and bleeding after being detained by Israeli forces and subjected to hours of restraint and a strip search, according to the Palestinian Commission of Detainees and Ex-Detainees Affairs. The commission said Abu Khadija, detained since August 27, was blindfolded and tightly handcuffed with plastic restraints that caused her hands to swell before being taken to an unknown location, where she was strip-searched and kept bound to a chair for hours. She was later transferred to Hasharon Prison for about five days, where she was held in a filthy, insect-infested cell without adequate drinking water, clean bedding, a shower, or a change of clothes, before being moved to Damon Prison. The commission said Abu Khadija is now held in a room designated for pregnant detainees, where three pregnant women receive no specialized meals and are given an egg or a piece of meat only about once every three or four days. Trump 's "Board of Peace" to unveil $2.45 billion Gaza plan: Trump's Board of Peace will a six-month, $2.45 billion Gaza recovery plan Wednesday covering 66 projects, including temporary housing, rubble removal, hospital repairs, economic recovery, governance, and security, Axios reported. The plan estimates Gaza's physical damage at $35.2 billion and full reconstruction costs at $71.4 billion over the next decade. About $1 billion is allocated to infrastructure, including $400 million for temporary shelters and $275 million for rubble and unexploded ordnance clearance, while $885 million would go toward security, including the International Stabilization Force, Palestinian police and a $20 million weapons buy-back program. Representatives from 35 countries, including the EU and several non-Board member states, are expected at Wednesday's briefing. The full $2.45 billion has not yet been secured. Hamas agreed July 30 to a roadmap linking decommissioning of weapons to Israeli withdrawal, which Israel has refused to implement. Israel is also reportedly blocking vetted Palestinian police recruits from leaving for training in Egypt and preventing the Board-approved Palestinian technocratic committee from entering Gaza. Lebanon Israeli ceasefire violations continue in southern Lebanon as blast in Khiam damages homes, school, and power lines: Israeli artillery shelling the outskirts of Baraachit in the Bint Jbeil district and Wadi Zibqin in the Tyre (Sour) district on Wednesday, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. Separately, a large explosion carried out by Israeli forces around midnight in the town of Khiam extensive damage in nearby Jdeidet Marjayoun and Qlayaa, shattering windows and cracking walls in several homes. Marjayoun National School also sustained extensive window damage and temporarily suspended classes for repairs. The blast electricity supply lines in the Nabaa al-Hamam area, causing a complete power outage across Hasbaya, Shebaa, and the Arqoub region. U.S. News DoorDash settles NYC underpayment probe for $131.5 million : DoorDash a record $131.5 million settlement with New York City's Department of Consumer and Worker Protection Tuesday over findings that the company underpaid or delayed payments to delivery workers, paying the City $16.7 million in fines and giving nearly $115 million in relief to about 264,000 "Dashers," who received a median payout of roughly $48. DoorDash said in a statement, "Simply put, we screwed up... Our mistakes meant some Dashers were underpaid or paid late." The deal is the largest worker settlement in New York City history and the largest settlement involving food delivery workers in the United States. It comes nearly eight months after the city agency accused DoorDash and Uber Eats of using "design tricks" to deprive workers of more than $550 million in tips. Federal judge orders Texas to air condition all prisons by end of 2029: U.S. District JudgeRobert Pitman Texas to develop and implement a plan to install air conditioning across all 104 of its prison facilities by Dec. 31, 2029, ruling Tuesday that lockups without cooling violate the Eighth Amendment and that the Texas Department of Criminal Justice's response to extreme heat constitutes "deliberate indifference." Just over a third of Texas correctional facilities were fully air conditioned as of Sept. 1, and Pitman noted the agency's recent $289 million legislative funding request for air conditioning fell well short of what it told the court it could obtain from state lawmakers. Installing air conditioning could cost up to $1.5 billion, the agency has noted. Inmate advocates have attributed at least 10 heat-related deaths to lack of air conditioning between 2022 and 2025. ShinyHunters hackers claim to have breached FBI, stolen data on all employees: Hacking group ShinyHunters on Tuesday to have breached multiple FBI-related services and stolen data "on all FBI employees and applicants," including names, home addresses, phone numbers and spouse information, according to 404 Media. The group also defaced the FBI's jobs website Tuesday with a message reading "this site has been seized by ShinyHunters." A group representative provided a sample containing data on 5,000 FBI employees, some of which 404 Media verified through open-source tools, and said the group used a zero-day exploit in an Oracle PeopleSoft product to access AWS GovCloud servers and exfiltrate between two and three terabytes of data. An FBI spokesperson said the agency is "aware of claims" and investigating the incident. The group, which typically extorts victims after breaches, said its motivation here is not financial but rather "coercion" tied to a prior FBI report describing ShinyHunters' tactics, which it demanded be corrected or removed within a week. Trump administration asks Supreme Court to overturn release of pro-Palestinian scholar : The Trump administration the Supreme Court Monday to overturn a lower court's release of Georgetown scholar Badar Khan Suri , an Indian citizen and postdoctoral fellow arrested by masked ICE officers in March 2025 amid a broader crackdown on pro-Palestinian activism on college campuses, after a district court judge freed him in May 2025 on grounds he was likely to succeed in proving his arrest was retaliation for constitutionally protected speech. Solicitor General D. John Sauer argued the 4th Circuit's July 2-1 ruling upholding Suri's release--which found lower courts could hear constitutional detention challenges even amid pending immigration proceedings--threatens nationwide immigration enforcement by letting detainees "bypass immigration courts." Trump backs diesel export ban amid GOP pressure over record fuel prices : President Donald Trump Tuesday he has called for a ban on U.S. diesel exports, with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent confirming the administration is examining whether a full or partial ban is feasible. The administration had previously resisted calls for a diesel export ban, which had come from farmers and truckers squeezed by fuel price increases. Iowa Republicans Sen. Chuck Grassley and Rep. Ashley Hinson made public calls for the policy earlier this week, and Senate Majority Leader John Thune said last week he was "open" to the idea. Trump officials plan to allow up to 17,500 more White Afrikaner refugees over next year : The Trump administration Congress Tuesday it plans to allocate up to 17,500 refugee spots for fiscal year 2027, "primarily" for White Afrikaners from South Africa, according to a notice obtained by CBS News. The State Department, which has effectively shuttered U.S. refugee resettlement program for all other groups, said Afrikaners "face the seizure of agricultural property without compensation" and discriminatory policies, claims the South African government has consistently denied. The effort--which the announcement projects will cost $500 million--follows new U.S. sanctions imposed last week on South African officials accused of discriminating against the group. Trump officials cut 760,000 from ACA over alleged fraud: Vice President JD Vance and administration officials Tuesday they are removing about 760,000 people from Affordable Care Act coverage over suspected fraud, with an additional 419,000 enrollees facing further verification. At the press conference announcing the removals, Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz also said his agency would be imposing a six-month moratorium on new insurance brokers selling ACA plans. Officials claimed the removals would save $2.2 billion in federal spending. The crackdown comes as ACA enrollment, which peaked under President Joe Biden , has already fallen by more than 1 million since Trump took office. GOP Sen. John Curtis calls for Senate probe of Donald Trump Jr. over Russian oligarch 's wedding gift: Sen. John Curtis (R-Utah) a letter to Senate Judiciary Committee leaders Chuck Grassley and Dick Durbin calling for an investigation into "the use of presidential family relationships for private financial benefit" urging subpoenas for Donald Trump Jr. after ProPublica reported that Russian businessman Umar Kremlev , who has close ties to Vladimir Putin, paid for a lavish Bahamas wedding afterparty for Trump Jr. "A toaster is a wedding gift. A private-island party paid for by a Putin-connected oligarch is something else," Curtis said, also citing Trump Jr.'s crypto ventures and international real estate dealings. Curtis also called in his letter for an investigation into Hunter Biden. ICE officer who shot Austin man was not wearing body camera: The ICE officer who Wilber Garc es Perez in Austin over the weekend was issued a body camera but was not using it during the incident, two former DHS officials told the Washington Post, despite an agency mandate rolled out after two prior shootings of unarmed immigrants by camera-less officers. The officer is also a recent recruit, the officials told the paper. ICE sent officers an email Tuesday reminding them cameras "must" be activated during enforcement activity. Garces Perez's attorney, Kate Lincoln-Goldfinch , said he was taken to another hospital Monday night after reporting paralysis on his left side, with a bullet still lodged near his spine. El-Sayed defends Harris support: After campaigning alongside former Vice President Kamala Harris , in Detroit, Michigan, Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed her support, with particular attention to the controversy surrounding her role in the Biden administration's conduct during Israel's genocide in Gaza and El-Sayed's support for the "Uncommitted" movement in Michigan. El Sayed noted that his positions on Gaza had not changed. "I was very clear that I disagreed with my party when it came to the genocide," he said. "None of those positions have changed at all. I'm not going to change them." El-Sayed nevertheless urged Democrats divided over Gaza to build a coalition against Trump, arguing the country would be better positioned on "everything from gas to groceries to Gaza" had Trump lost in 2024. Byron Donalds scrubs Trump references from campaign website amid president 's sinking approval: Florida gubernatorial candidate Byron Donalds at least eight prominent references to President Donald Trump's endorsement from his campaign website, including a homepage banner, a "Chip in" button, and a photo of Donalds with the president, according to the Miami Herald. Trump's endorsement now appears only in a rolling banner alongside other conservative endorsers, and Donalds' policy page no longer lists "Enact the Trump Agenda" as a top priority, replacing it with affordability. Spokesperson Gates McGavick said the site "reflects Byron's focus on the issues that matter most to Floridians" and that Donalds remains "proud to have President Trump's endorsement." 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News U.S. claims neither Sudanese army nor RSF has legitimate authority : The U.S. State Department Tuesday that neither Sudan's army nor the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces have legitimate authority to govern the country, with spokesperson Thomas Pigott saying both sides rule "purely through force of arms" and accused both of failing to commit to ceasefire efforts and of escalating the conflict instead. The statement called Sudan's war the world's worst humanitarian crisis, and said Washington would work to "raise the cost of continued conflict on all belligerents." South Sudan 's Kiir dissolves transitional government, consolidates power in interim: South Sudan President Salva Kiir the country's transitional government Tuesday, hours after signing amendments to election laws that removed requirements to complete a permanent constitution and census before holding a vote, in preparation for the country's first-ever national elections. The transitional government was originally established under a 2018 peace deal that ended a years-long civil war in the country. Under the amended National Elections Act, passed by parliament Monday, Kiir's executive leadership retains full constitutional powers through the election period, and the National Legislative Assembly will shrink from 650 to 270 members, with state assemblies cut from 100 to 58 seats. The moves come as Kiir's longtime rival, opposition leader Riek Machar, remains under house arrest since March 2025 and on trial for treason and murder charges he denies. Elections were initially expected in 2022 but have been delayed twice. Tigray forces launch offensive against Ethiopia 's government: Tigrayan forces a major offensive against Ethiopia's federal government Wednesday, a senior Ethiopian official said, shattering the Pretoria Agreement that ended the 2020-2022 civil war, with the officials from the Tigray People's Liberation Front saying they entered a "defensive war" against government "aggression." Getachew Reda, an adviser to Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed, said the TPLF seized federally controlled airports in Tigray and launched an "all-out offensive" into neighboring Afar and Amhara regions, where Tigrayan forces are fighting alongside local armed groups and the Fano militia. Ethiopian Airlines has suspended flights to Tigray. The fighting follows the announcement of a seven-group alliance on Sunday, which declared its aim at overthrowing Abiy's government. Survivors: Nigerian guards sprayed substance into packed cell before 37 detainees died : Three survivors Reuters that Nigerian prison guards sprayed an unidentified substance into an overcrowded cell holding dozens of detained gold miners near Minna, then kept the doors locked; 37 detainees died. The Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps paramilitary agency jailed the miners after raiding suspected illegal mining sites. Many of those jailed were teenagers. President Bola Ahmed Tinubu ordered an investigation in response. The deaths, which authorities initially attributed to a possible disease outbreak before saying the cause remains under investigation, sparked protests that turned deadly Friday, leading officials in the country's Niger state to impose a 24-hour curfew. Venezuelan opposition leader Machado makes unsuccessful bids to return home, adviser says: Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado three unsuccessful attempts by sea and air to return to Venezuela in recent hours, her adviser Pedro Urruchurtu said on social media, bringing her total failed return attempts to seven since she clandestinely left the country nine months ago, according to the Spanish newspaper ABC. The paper did not report who blocked her Tuesday attempts. Machado's efforts coincided with interim President Delcy Rodriguez's first meeting with President Trump in New York following President Nicolas Maduro's capture by U.S. forces in a January raid. Alleged fentanyl trafficker arrested in Mexico City in joint U.S.-Mexico operation : Mexican authorities Jose Angel Rivera, known as "Don Flaco," in Mexico City Tuesday for allegedly coordinating and financing an organization that transported fentanyl chemical precursors from China to Mexico and the U.S., in a joint operation with the FBI and DEA, Security Minister Omar Garcia Harfuch said on X. Rivera had been sanctioned by the U.S. State Department in January 2023 over his alleged role in fentanyl trafficking. Harfuch said the arrest reflected "international cooperation, shared responsibility, and unrestricted respect for our sovereignty." The arrest came the same day President Trump told the United Nations that Mexico was "the epicenter" of drug cartel violence and needed to "reclaim control of its territory." Taiwan says it will stay in "close contact" with U.S. on arms sales: Taiwan's defense ministry Wednesday it would continue close coordination with the U.S. to implement arms sales "according to plan," ahead of an expected meeting between President Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington this week, where Xi is expected to press Trump to halt the sales. A $14 billion arms package remains in abeyance following Trump's December approval of an $11 billion package, the largest ever. UN report finds Nicaragua 's crackdown on dissent amounts to crimes against humanity: Nicaraguan state institutions, coordinated through a chain of command reaching senior government levels, have out enforced disappearances, torture, and arbitrary detention of political opponents amounting to crimes against humanity, according to a report published by UN human rights officials on Tuesday. The report documents 161 cases of enforced disappearance and eight deaths in state custody since April 2018. The report also noted a shift, beginning in 2023, toward long-term disappearances and nationwide police raids targeting dissidents, church members, Indigenous leaders, and former officials. Female detainees have been subjected to threats of sexual violence. #
Everyone can feel the shift happening beneath them in Texas, Peter.
Headline after headline talks about the historic shift in Texas politics, and multiple polls in the last month show Democrats surging among Hispanic voters, placing major races across the state on the verge of flipping blue.
[](https://act.votolatino.org/go/57?c0=em-ms-voto-20260923-1._W23lf&amount=3&refcode=em20260923-612&t=1&akid=612%2E1366028%2EweUO_d)

But there’s one thing that these major headlines don’t mention.**Democrats will lose in Texas unless Latinos actually turn out to vote.** In our latest poll, 14% of Latinos reported they would not vote this election. The highest share of any voter group polled.
[**Peter, will you donate any amount right now to make sure we have the resources to reach, register, and mobilize as many voters in Texas as possible to flip Texas BLUE?**](https://act.votolatino.org/go/57?c0=em-ms-voto-20260923-1._W23lf&amount=3&refcode=em20260923-612&t=2&akid=612%2E1366028%2EweUO_d)

But there’s one thing that these major headlines don’t mention.Democrats will lose in Texas unless Latinos actually turn out to vote. In our latest poll, 14% of Latinos reported they would not vote this election. The highest share of any voter group polled. Leading poll numbers are not the same thing as ballots in a box. And Republicans know how high the stakes are. That’s why they’re pouring tens of millions of dollars into expensive Texas media markets to defend their seats and suppress Latino voter turnout. So if we don’t do the hard work of getting voters to the polls NOW, these historic poll numbers won’t mean anything on Election Day. Thank you, Voto Latino

name: The Flyover
subject: Your Wallet Says One Thing. The Numbers Say Another.
body:
Why does everything still feel so expensive? We dug into the number behind your costs.

| | |
---

**Good Morning!** If the economy is improving, **why does everything still feel so expensive?** Your grocery bill is higher. Buying a home feels out of reach for more Americans. Saving for retirement is harder. And for millions of seniors, the annual Social Security increase is supposed to help them keep pace. All of those things are connected to a number we hear about constantly: [**the cost of living.**](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyszzFuhDAQQNHTQLdoPAZjChdpkFJsuiilZWC8OPHaKzws4vZRohwhB3hf-h9Xe3UhhnR7c3cy7LP1ed6LTXSUSMy02TPv2-FiJC7uLDkRryHdeCWLgOoCwwXlnxL1YjwRkqzJiH4A0SsBWK-m63UnJwU0aa9BTQMs0g3OezdrueBcB_NTgwGl6ECjaLT2UrdCtS2i7MBVLdASOG_NZw6JV_LxzE_amjnf62hW5kep5EuFY4XjmXfem4kqHN9Bi1c7Tl9J15tZHkeIMRTVVy3c7i7EX8__sP40-B0AAP__3BVvYA) But here's the bigger question: **Does the number everyone quotes actually reflect what you 're paying?** In this week's [_**Flyover Focus**_](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyszzFuhDAQQNHTQLdoPAZjChdpkFJsuiilZWC8OPHaKzws4vZRohwhB3hf-h9Xe3UhhnR7c3cy7LP1ed6LTXSUSMy02TPv2-FiJC7uLDkRryHdeCWLgOoCwwXlnxL1YjwRkqzJiH4A0SsBWK-m63UnJwU0aa9BTQMs0g3OezdrueBcB_NTgwGl6ECjaLT2UrdCtS2i7MBVLdASOG_NZw6JV_LxzE_amjnf62hW5kep5EuFY4XjmXfem4kqHN9Bi1c7Tl9J15tZHkeIMRTVVy3c7i7EX8__sP40-B0AAP__3BVvYA), Amy digs into how the cost of living is really calculated--and why the official figure doesn't always match what you see at the grocery store, in your mortgage payment, or in your bank account. We look at **who 's feeling the squeeze the most**, whether Social Security increases are actually keeping up, and one number buried in the data that helps explain why rising costs hit some Americans much harder than others. **➤****Your groceries. Your mortgage. Your savings. Your retirement check.** They're all part of the equation. But the number may not tell the whole story. clean_body: Why does everything still feel so expensive? We dug into the number behind your costs. | | | Good Morning! If the economy is improving, why does everything still feel so expensive? Your grocery bill is higher. Buying a home feels out of reach for more Americans. Saving for retirement is harder. And for millions of seniors, the annual Social Security increase is supposed to help them keep pace. All of those things are connected to a number we hear about constantly: But here's the bigger question: Does the number everyone quotes actually reflect what you 're paying? In this week's , Amy digs into how the cost of living is really calculated--and why the official figure doesn't always match what you see at the grocery store, in your mortgage payment, or in your bank account. We look at who 's feeling the squeeze the most, whether Social Security increases are actually keeping up, and one number buried in the data that helps explain why rising costs hit some Americans much harder than others. ➤Your groceries. Your mortgage. Your savings. Your retirement check. They're all part of the equation. But the number may not tell the whole story. name: Roy Cooper
subject: What a landslide in North Carolina looks like
body:
I want you to know something, Peter.
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1394&source=&t=1&akid=3782%2E124072%2EwSpPVV) | | | |
---
Peter,
There’s something I want you to know about elections in North Carolina – especially the race for U.S. Senate:
**For Democratic candidates, winning by a “landslide” here in a federal race means winning with, at most, 51% of the vote.**
Not 60%. Not 75%.
**51%.**
That’s how tight and competitive our races are – and it’s why my biggest concern is that people will start taking this one for granted.
**North Carolina has only sent two Democrats to the Senate in the last three decades. President Trump swept the state all three times. With the GOP pouring over $100 million and counting into attack ads against me, it’s no wonder recent polling shows us under 50%.**
Nothing has changed that we didn’t anticipate, Peter. I **know** we can flip this seat blue for the first time since 2008 – but not if we get complacent. It will come down to every last vote, and I need your help to fight for each one.
[**_That’s why I’m asking you to chip in to our campaign today. I need you with me to defy the odds, flip this seat and take back the Senate for Democrats. Please, Peter, will you give $5 or whatever you can spare?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1394&amount=5&t=8&akid=3782%2E124072%2EwSpPVV)

Democrat Roy Cooper is running for U.S. Senate to help take back the Majority for Democrats. North Carolina is Democrats’ best chance to flip a seat from red to blue — the path to stopping Republicans in Washington starts here.

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.

Texas is worth defending. I have said that since day one, and I’ll say it until I die.
The fathers of Texas came from all corners of America to forge civilization from the void and build an oasis of freedom and liberty amidst the cruelty of the formless frontier. Through their work, these great patriots willed into existence the greatest state in the Union from nothing.
You and I are the inheritors of this same animating spirit, transmitted across generations since the first foundations of our State were laid. This Texan spirit was passed down to us from the fathers of Texas through the promises made and kept at Goliad, the Alamo, San Jacinto, and beyond.
As Texans, we have always understood that the cornerstone of our identity was opposition to tyranny and despotism.
The same forces of tyranny and despotic oppression that first took aim at our forefathers are once again stirring, coming together in the shadows with their sights set on Texas.
As the country looks on, the DNC party apparatus and its billionaire donors are waiting to see if Texas will go blue. This coalition of anti-prosperity communists known as the “Democratic Party” wants to extinguish the flame of liberty that burns in Texas. That Texas flame, fueled by Texas Oil and Gas, is the beacon of freedom that calls to the whole of America and the world.
If you believe, like I do, that Texas must be defended, I urge you to step up and chip in whatever you can today.
_**[Help me keep the flame of Texas Liberty lit!](https://link.emails.bofrench.)**_

body:

41 days. That’s all that stands between us and the
midterms, Peter.

For years, deep-pocketed special interests and right-wing networks have
relentlessly targeted our rights — dismantling fundamental freedoms,
attacking our democracy, and attempting to roll back every inch of
progress we’ve fought to secure.

And at every turn, our Squad has stood on the front lines fighting back.

Now, their opponents and outside forces are working with one objective: to
unseat our champions and silence them. But we know the Squad will never
cave to pressure and never back down from the fight for working people.

Here’s what’s on the line:

* Accessible healthcare
* Affordable housing
* Economic justice
* Climate action
* Civil rights across the board
* Racial justice
* Reproductive freedom

Every single one of these is exactly what the Squad has been fighting to
protect — and exactly what the far right is working to strip away.

The final countdown is on. Every resource we put to work over these next
41 days will determine whether we protect our champions or let outside
forces drown us out.

We have less than six weeks to organize, mobilize, and make sure our Squad
stays right where they belong: fighting for the communities that need them
most.

We can’t afford to lose even one seat,
Peter — which means we need
grassroots supporters like you to step up today and make sure we can fight
back.

body:
As we race toward the midterm elections, there are two things Americans must know.

Senate races are national and electing conservatives is all that matters.
| | | |
---
|
---
Fellow Conservative: As we race toward the midterm elections, there are two things Americans must know. **1) U.S. Senate races are _NATIONAL_ elections that impact ALL AMERICANS regardless of where you live.** **2) Electing strong _CONSERVATIVES_ is what matters, because another spineless Republican majority will not save our country.** Let's break these down... First, we often hear people say they don't really care about elections outside their home state. They can't vote for the candidates, so why bother? The reason is simple: _U.S. Senators make national policies that impact the lives of ALL Americans._ So while you may not be able to vote for them, their votes in Washington affect you and your family. **This is why conservatives in all 50 states must use their Constitutionally protected freedom of speech to influence the outcomes of Senate races around the country.** But if the entire Senate map is important to every American, which candidates matter most? The answer: _Conservatives_. Notice that it's not Republicans because many Republicans will not fight for our priorities when it matters. We've all painfully watched the current Senate Republican majority squander its mandate and fail to pass even the most popular policies like voter ID. Meanwhile, it has worked with the Democrats to spend so much that our national debt now exceeds $40 trillion. **The bottom line is that electing more moderate, pro-establishment Republicans is not worth our time and money.** That's why the Senate Conservatives Fund has selected eight conservative candidates across the nation who deserve our votes _AND_ our financial support.

I want to take a break today from ranting about whatever stupid thing Donald Trump is doing and talk about something more personal: my weight.
Earlier this week, my governor, JB Pritzker, shared that he's lost 80 pounds after going on a GLP-1. Millions of Americans have been through some version of that same journey, and I think it matters a great deal when our elected leaders are willing to talk openly about their struggles, whether it's their weight, their mental health, or anything else they're carrying.
And then I watched the Trump White House, the Republican Party, and the MAGA media machine spend the better part of two days mocking him for it. Mocking a man for improving his health. For doing the exact thing that so many people have spent years telling big guys like JB and me to do.
It was something to behold, because the people behind it have to be such sad, miserable pricks. And I don't just mean the people who made the content. I mean everyone who engaged with it gleefully, as well.
I've always hated it when politics turns to mocking people's appearance. I hated it when it happened to Chris Christie. I disagreed with plenty of what he did as governor of New Jersey, but I never thought he deserved to be ridiculed for his weight. Honestly, as a big guy myself, someone who once weighed 600 pounds just a few years ago, I found it inspiring to see somebody closer to my shape holding high office. I felt the same way about Governor Pritzker.
For those of you who don't know, I've lost 300 pounds over the last couple of years. But that journey started somewhere much darker than I usually talk about. During the pandemic, I hit one of the lowest points of my life. The thought of killing myself grabbed hold of me so viscerally that I became afraid of what might happen if I was left alone. I will never forget looking at my wife and begging her not to leave for a trip to visit family because I was scared of what I might do to myself if she did.
That was the moment I knew something had to change. And eventually, I did.
Most of that came from hard work, discipline, and learning how to take care of myself. And yes, some of it came from a GLP-1. I lost the last hundred or so pounds on one. Earlier this year, I had surgery to remove 25 pounds of excess skin around my abdomen that was dramatically holding back my ability to do anything physical. A lot of you already know this part. The recovery was a complete and total nightmare.
So I have some personal stake in this. And here's what I want to say: even in this era of politics, when it's so easy to hate one another, when it's so easy to make fun of Donald Trump's weight or anybody else's, we should try to be human beings first. There are plenty of reasons to hate what somebody does with power. We don't need to hate them for being human.
I know that's a little naive. There will always be nasty, cruel people who want to divide us that way. I've faced my fair share of attacks about my weight or my mental health from right wing loons like Laura Loomer. but I believe the world becomes a far more interesting place when people share their struggles instead of pretending we're all perfect.
* * *

Just $8/month makes a huge difference:](https://substack.com/redirect/893ec77b-7705-42b4-9eb9-0c8e61149fa3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

* * *
I loved the videos AOC made about freezing her eggs from earlier in the summer. Not because it's something I've experienced myself, although my wife and I have been through several rounds of IVF and many miscarriages. I loved them because I know there are people out there going through the same thing who now get to see a little of themselves in someone who could be a future presidential contender. That matters.
On the other side of it, I was extremely critical of Congressman Tom Kean when he disappeared for months. If he really was dealing with severe depression that required medical care, I wish he'd felt he could be honest with his constituents about it. Imagine how many people in his district, and around the country, could have been helped by hearing a member of Congress say, "I'm struggling, and I'm getting help."
Every time someone like Governor Pritzker, or AOC, or even someone like me, comes forward to talk about our challenges with mental health or weight or anything else, the world gets a little better. And more to the point, it helps people. That's the part that gets lost when vulnerability becomes something we punish.
There are people sitting on the fence right now, trying to decide whether to talk to their doctor about a GLP-1. People who want to be honest with their friends about their weight but haven't found the words yet. People who know they need to take that first step, the one that eventually leads to losing 80 pounds like the governor or 300 like me, and who just need a little push.
You can be that push. All it takes is sharing a little more of yourself. Being vulnerable. Giving people that 5% of your life nobody likes to talk about, the 5% good and the 5% bad. You never really know who needs to hear it.
We spend so much of our time on trivia that doesn't really matter. Meanwhile, the things we're actually ashamed of, afraid of, struggling with, or trying desperately to change are the things we hide from each other. Maybe we've got that backwards.
That's what I was reflecting on this morning, and I wanted to share it with you instead of ranting about stupid Trump shit for the thousandth time. Because every once in a while, I think it's worth remembering that being honest about the shit we're carrying might do more good than we realize. Don't worry, we'll keep doing that, and I'm sure we'll be back to your regularly scheduled MAGA bashing tomorrow.
But this is what's on my mind today. And Governor Pritzker, if you happen to read this: thank you for sharing a little bit of yourself. Somebody out there needed to hear it. I appreciate you all.
With Urgency,
-Mike

body:
The push to privatize public lands continues
The push to privatize public lands continues

| [|
---](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/i9sAXQ45Fa8cRYeMlnv7iA~~/AAUS1hA~/F1txX3NnVG-bKcOubLLXnYTAuXF4mpRvYLM33047AKNLZjwFd42Wh-8uEXUq0XRNHtEmG-TDz7dSpwTHp95niyGFBf6iQqp76z898dsH22gVlcEg4LNju9l6M5HXgteT)
| | | | Peter, A Nevada energy company just applied to take over 3,700 acres of federal public land just outside Boise, Idaho. Their plan is to build a 4-million-square-foot AI data center—**four times the size of a massive Meta facility** —right across the street from a pristine bird reserve and a local public shooting range. **And just for good measure, they are planning to drop a 450-megawatt gas-fired power plant right in the middle of it.** They are literally trying to turn your public hunting and recreation lands into a sprawling, fossil-fuel-burning industrial complex for Silicon Valley billionaires. And the best part? The federal government wasn't even going to formally notify the public until this winter, when the backroom deal is already halfway out the door. [**This is the exact blueprint for the corporate takeover of our public lands. Will you pitch in $10 today to our rapid-response war chest to help us kill this project before they break ground?**](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/0UWEgHOINojedOox7oJBEQ~~/AAUS1hA~/lzySmchYZWUtoXkEpG9ES-CLZigh0dKfDbMrY2x2dbwXgyO-l9aS20-sLn6_9r1CdEatZtugQBzpo1A86ruf1kIFg9rz7nj0lgOBf98YW0ZZrP60ic2Bh1mzhRwYNL7TniI8EwCC0VlWsBgnkn_2J5jWQlBYmGWgssWkUa3o2zaKAcHWhCELrH6X6wHZzXx40UJe0c6Fy20OcHjYJbqtMfuSbQ-wPwey6rDZPOMBW2NJyQyoz4bJrQkJPz6HT6Kn) Why are they doing this on public land? Because they know if they tried to drop a 4-million-square-foot, water-guzzling, gas-burning mega-factory in a regular neighborhood, the locals would run them out of town. So they use a loophole. They target federal land where local city councils have no say, secure massive corporate tax breaks, and leave local taxpayers holding the bag for the power grid upgrades and the drained aquifers. They get the profits; you get the smog and the utility hikes. They expect you to just sit around and politely wait for a bureaucratic public comment period while they finalize the paperwork. We aren't going to wait. With less than six weeks until Election Day, we are going on the offensive right now. At Public Land Warriors, we are preparing a surgical digital ad blitz to hit the airwaves in Idaho and across the Mountain West. We are going to make sure every single voter knows exactly which politicians are allowing tech conglomerates to turn our shared national heritage into a private, taxpayer-subsidized server farm. subject: Here’s what I had to say on CNN:
body:
|
#
Friend, I know you've seen it. Gas prices. Grocery bills. The cost of just about everything – it just keeps going up. I was on CNN to talk about exactly that – and specifically what skyrocketing gas prices are doing to families and farmers right here in mid-Michigan. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139799799/648549180/1362877128?refcode=em-9.23.26-all-a&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NjAyNCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhMjlhZTMwOS02YWI3LWYxMTEtYTZhOS0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=cZ_6d2u8dI-Ae7KOyt6XV-QHIdUn6xSalY66y4L_FFo=) Already, farmers in mid-Michigan have felt the strain caused by the unnecessary trade war and tariffs. And now with the cost of diesel rising past $7 a gallon in many places – it’s becoming _even harder_ just to make a living. And it isn’t just farmers who are struggling – families throughout the district are buckling under sky-high prices too. They don’t know how they’re going to afford the electric bill, put food on the table, or cover a trip to the doctor’s office. **Folks are frustrated. And they deserve real solutions.** That’s why I’m in this fight – because families shouldn’t have to break the bank or go without just to survive – all while the rich and powerful continue to line their pockets. subject: I'm always going to reject Socialism and the anti-American way of life

body:

[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e6039294/UaHR0cHM6Ly93cm8ubnVjbGV1c2VtYWlsLmNvbS9hbXBsaWZ5L3YvbmRSWndZZnNuRQ/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjA5MjM/LbmNsWjFOdHdyTQ/qP2hpZHM9bmNxNjFoYlgzVHBHMHJsc10/garP8rA/s6r722cee58

[Image showing logo and first aid]
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

Dear Friend who has common sense,

I'm always going to stand with America.

I'm always going to reject the extremes.

I'm always going to reject Socialism.

I'm always going to fight against the anti-American way of life.

And this has enraged a lot of people in the media, in my party, and
even former staffers --- disgruntled leakers who are viciously and
anonymously attacking me.

This is what happens when you put common sense and the wellbeing of
the people you are supposed to represent ahead of party loyalty.

But most of all, I think this is what happens when you clash with the
Socialist movement "DSA!" that is hijacking the Democratic party.

They want to...

Abolish our borders

Abolish the electoral college

Abolish Israel

Abolish the Senate and the Supreme Court (no, seriously, this is in
the "DSA!" platform)

That bad news is the "DSA!" crazies have gone from the political
fringe to controlling one of America's major political parties—and
onto ballots across the country.

The good news is the hardworking, common-sense Americans I talk to
every day still aren't buying it.

I mean, a recent Rasmussen poll kind of proves it:

71% of Americans reject socialism

67% of Democrat voters reject socialism

While 82% of Republican voters reject socialism

But here's the thing. The loudest voice in the room is often the one
that looks the most powerful.

And I've got to say, the "DSA!" voices in Washington are loud and
getting louder. The media is their megaphone.

Which is why you may be under the false impression that people really
do want the "DSA!" and their extreme policies

Nothing could be further from the truth.

I'M STANDING UP TO THEM.
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

But sadly I'm pretty much alone on this side of the aisle.

So, can I ask you a favor?

Whatever your party affiliation is, can I ask you to stand with me
against the daily barrage of hit-pieces

IF YOU CAN DONATE JUST $25 IT WOULD BE A BIG HELP TO ME.
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

But it will also send a message. It will show the truth that the
"real numbers" are on our side here in Pennsylvania, as well as around
the rest of America.

You know, I recently stood in front of the iconic U.S. Steel Mill and
recorded a video talking about how my friend Dave McCormick and I
banded together with President Trump to save this facility and the
larger steel industry. But I'm not backing down.

Even though I know the media... the "DSA!"... and the party
bosses... are going to try even harder to defeat me:

"FETTERMAN DRAWS SHADOW PRIMARY FROM DEMOCRATS EAGER TO REPLACE HIM:
THE PENNSYLVANIA SENATOR HAS LONG IRKED MEMBERS OF HIS OWN PARTY" ~
BLOOMBERG

If you'll stand with me today, I know we can show them that we're not
backing down and that the real numbers are on the side of common sense
and putting our country first.

Thank you!

John Fetterman

P.S. - I'll bet you're more than a little surprised to get this email
from me. So, I want to say thanks for setting aside party affiliation
for a second and hearing me out. You see, I'm not a progressive. And
I'm definitely not a Democratic Socialist. I'm just a senator with a
big mouth who happens to stand for common-sense things like... strong
borders, safe streets, a powerful economy, bringing jobs to my
constituents, and Israel and Ukraine's right to defend themselves, not
to mention the basic machinery of our democracy (the Electoral
College, the Senate, and the Supreme Court). If you see eye-to-eye
with me, then I could sure use your help. The "DSA!" vision for
Pennsylvania and for America is not a healthy one. It is a dangerous
one.Common-sense people need to join together now to reject this
vision before it's too late. CAN I COUNT ON YOU TO STAND WITH ME
TODAY?

name: Pramila Jayapal
subject: Accountability is long past due
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Pramila for Congress
body:
Trump’s outright corruption is unacceptable.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20260923-6753-footer&t=1&akid=6753%2E420207%2EaQ6oiO)
Peter, they aren’t even trying to hide their corruption anymore.
We’ve known for years about the corrupt deals and favors Trump and his family are taking advantage of.
**But now, after earning BILLIONS since re-entering the White House, they’re doing it out in the open.**
Crypto coins. Taxpayer money. Sweetheart deals for their friends. AI investments. Trump, his family, and his administration are prioritizing their own pockets over American workers. And they don't care who sees.
Meanwhile, families across this country are working themselves to the bone and still can't make rent, afford groceries, or pay for their prescriptions.
**It's disgusting, and I've had enough.**

Lansing -- September 23, 2026. The Michigan Court of Claims has denied the State's motion to dismiss McQueer v. Benson in its entirety -- every ground, every argument -- meaning the lawsuit by two Washtenaw County township clerks challenging Secretary of State Jocelyn Benson's electronic poll book deletion rule will now be decided on its merits. That is precisely the outcome the Department of State had fought to avoid since the day the complaint was filed. And it lands squarely in the middle of Jocelyn Benson's campaign to become Michigan's next governor.
**The rule, and the federal law it runs into**
At the center of the case is Mich. Admin. Code R 168.48, a state rule that took effect October 23, 2025. It directs local election clerks to delete electronic poll book software and associated files within seven days after an election is certified. An electronic poll book is the laptop-based record of every voter who checked in at a precinct -- names, movements through the line, ballots issued. It is, in a real sense, the doorway record of an election.

name: Doug Lindner, LCV
subject: We need a Supreme Court that works for all Americans
body:
To view this mail in a browser, copy https://links.messages.lcv.org/servlet/MailView?ms=MTM5NzQ3MTYS1&r=NjA3MDU0MTAzNTc3S0&j=MjU0MDQ4OTA0NAS2&mt=1&rt=0 into your browser.
Peter, Earlier this month, we had a major win for democracy: House Democrats took a
stand to protect the option to expand the Supreme Court. They blocked MAGA
Republicans in Congress from amending the Constitution to lock in a MAGA
majority on the Supreme Court for the rest of our lives. The Constitution gives Congress the power to set the number of justices. It’s
one of their most important checks and balances. Congress has used that power
seven times before, including in laws signed by George Washington, Thomas
Jefferson, and Abraham Lincoln. Under the next pro-democracy president, we believe it’s time for Congress to use
that power again — and expand and rebalance the Supreme Court. The current Supreme Court has been captured and corrupted by MAGA
authoritarians, Big Polluters, and billionaires. The justices serve for life, so
if we don’t act soon, they’ll keep abusing their power to roll back climate
action, access to clean air and water, and our freedom to vote for decades to
come. Expanding and rebalancing the Court isn’t a radical idea. This House vote, and
the public support that’s come after it, proves that. After extreme,
anti-constitutional decisions the Court has made over the last few years — such
as Louisiana v. Callais, which demolished the Voting Rights Act; Sackett v. EPA, which rolled back the Clean Water Act; and West Virginia v. EPA, which tied the EPA’s hands on climate under the Clean Air Act — it’s clear that we need justices who will work for the people, not
polluter-backed authoritarians. LCV supports expanding and rebalancing the Court with four new pro-environment,
pro-democracy justices. And most Americans support expanding the Court, too. Because to achieve a world
where everyone has a right to clean air, clean water, public lands, and a safe
climate protected by a just and equitable democracy, we need highly qualified, ethical justices who work for the people. This is a win for now, but our movement must continue advocating for the
rebalancing of power our country needs. We can’t allow corrupt MAGA politicians
and their handpicked judges to call the shots. The midterms are already upon us, and 2028 will be here before we know it. We’re
not wasting any time — under the next pro-democracy president, you can count on
LCV to advocate for expanding and rebalancing the Supreme Court with four new
pro-environment, pro-democracy justices, and we’re working hard to build support
until then. Together, we can achieve a safer, healthier, and more equitable
climate and country for us all. Thank you for standing with LCV. Doug Lindner

Senior Director of Judiciary & Democracy

| | | | 41 DAYS TO ELECTION DAY NOVEMBER 3, 2026
---|---
HELP US REACH EVERY VOTER
We have just **41 days** to get our message into every corner of PA-11 and make sure voters know they have a choice on November 3.
| | Reaching voters takes resources. Billboards, digital and traditional media advertising, mail, signs, and organizing across the district all cost money. **Your contribution today** will help us reach more voters and build the campaign we need to win!
---|---
| [ DONATE TODAY ](https://matj3.r.a.d.sendibm1.com/mk/cl/f/sh/1t6Af4OiGsEag4ErLzpEhPxLt9QUXR/HE9UtuWJ4Ui4)
---

**Help Us Reach Every Voter!********With just 7 days left in the final fundraising quarter before Election Day, recent polling showed a clear opening for change – and we need your help to seize it!**
Statewide surveys* found Democrats leading in U.S. House preferences, while voters cited deep economic strain:
*

* 44% said they were worse off financially than a year ago,
* 57% reported difficulty paying utility bills, and
* 55% struggled with grocery costs.

In a PA-11 poll sponsored by the Mannion campaign, 46% of registered voters – including 54% of independents – said it is time for a new representative, while only 39% said incumbent Lloyd Smucker should be reelected.*
These results reflect what Nancy Mannion is hearing across Lancaster and York counties: people are frustrated with current leadership, feel let down, and want a representative who listens, shows up, and is accountable. Nancy’s support grows when voters hear her priorities – affordable health care, government accountability, stronger public education, and workforce development – but reaching them requires resources now.

**We can win this! Here’s how you can help:**

* **[Make a donation today](https://matj3.r.a.d.sendibm1.com/mk/cl/f/sh/1t6Af4OiGsF30mRHkLv9rg1BGyPEFV/1Xwatvr8yeq0) to help fund door hangers, postcards, yard signs, digital outreach, and billboards. Every contribution helps carry this message to more voters and turn growing frustration into meaningful change at the ballot box.**

**Your donation can make a difference:**
---
* $65 pays for 100 postcard stamps
* $100 buys 500 door hangers
* $300 buys 100 yard signs
* $500 reaches up to 15,000 people on Meta
* $4,400 buys a 4-week billboard

---
* **Get a yard sign. Displaying signs across PA-11 increases visibility and awareness.** [Click here](https://matj3.r.a.d.sendibm1.com/mk/cl/f/sh/1t6Af4OiGsFVLUdi8i151w50enNxxZ/BbQ8qWOz8M_l) to reserve one now and a volunteer will deliver one to you or coordinate a pick-up.

---
***Polling Methodology**

* F&M surveyed 501 registered Pennsylvania voters from Aug. 17–23 by telephone and online; the reported margin of sampling error was plus or minus 5.5 percentage points.

* New York Times/Philadelphia Inquirer/Siena poll interviewed 760 registered Pennsylvania voters from Aug. 17–21; the reported margin of error was plus or minus 5.2 percentage points.

* Public Policy Polling conducted the poll for the Mannion campaign from Aug. 18 – 19. The firm reached 533 registered voters in Pennsylvania's 11th Congressional district: 51% Republican, 27% Democrat, and 22% Independent. The reported margin of error was plus or minus 3.9 percentage points.

---
## **Week in Review**
---
**The campaign team was busy this week – here are a few highlights!**
**Tenfold Annual Banquet** Nancy attended the [Tenfold](https://matj3.r.a.d.sendibm1.com/mk/cl/f/sh/1t6Af4OiGsFxgCq8X470CC8q2cMhfd/gVBaqoFTLPK3) Annual Banquet in Lancaster on Tuesday, September 15. The signature fundraiser benefits an organization that supports people experiencing homelessness, promotes housing stability, and helps prospective buyers prepare for homeownership. Attendees of the event learned about Tenfold’s community impact through personal stories of housing stability and new beginnings.
---
---
Photo: [Tenfold](https://matj3.r.a.d.sendibm1.com/mk/cl/f/sh/1t6Af4OiGsGQ0v2YvQCvMSCfQRLRNh/bDnbn_EnxI-L)
---

**Nancy’s Tenth Town Hall!** On Thursday, September 17, Nancy joined Ron Ruman, candidate for PA House (196th district), and Thomas Johnson, candidate for PA Senate (28th district) in Spring Grove. This was her 10th Town Hall this year meeting with future constituents! The candidates addressed a variety of questions from the sixty attendees and talked about their plans to address affordability for residents, among other concerns.
---
---
Photo: [Ron Ruman for PA 196](https://matj3.r.a.d.sendibm1.com/mk/cl/f/sh/1t6Af4OiGsGsLdEzJmIqWiGUoGKB5l/iJmbhAPzxJGH)

**Door Knocking with Brad Chambers and Jess Branas** The Mannion campaign team knocked doors with Brad Chambers, candidate for PA State House (41st district) on Friday, September 18, and with Jess Branas, candidate for PA State House (97th district) on Sunday, September 20.

I’ve said this from the beginning: I’m not in this fight to come close, or give Huizenga a good scare, or score some kind of moral victory.
I’m in this fight to win it — because this is my community, and we have gone without real representation in Congress for far too long.
We are right on the cusp now. A year ago, pundits didn’t think this race would be competitive. And thanks to people like you it’s quite literally the closest in the country.

Peter, Ever since Donald Trump kicked off the national redistricting crisis last summer, we’ve been in a whirlwind of uncertainty about new gerrymanders. **But the congressional map is now set for November.** It’s worth stepping back for a second to recognize a basic fact: _this is not normal! This should not be normal!_**That’s why we are[fighting for a national ban on gerrymandering.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139805103/648564583/1548394306?refcode=don_ndrc_tier1_email_MidcycleRedistricting_email_20260923-NDRC-Tier1-MidcycleRedistricting_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20260923-NDRC-Tier1-MidcycleRedistricting_&utm_campaign=MidcycleRedistricting&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjYxOTM0MjliLTcxYjctZjExMS1hNmE5LTAwMjI0ODJhOTMzYiIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=Gl-nQ-9uNVXA7bfgKpbRsWOH2dehnNwbfEd7qwbblww=)** Mid-decade redistricting used to be rare. Redistricting is supposed to happen once a decade, right after the census, to ensure districts accurately represent their communities. It’s not supposed to be a weapon for politicians to deploy whenever they get scared about the polls and decide to give themselves an unearned advantage. But now it’s a core political strategy for Republicans. In just over a year, the GOP manipulated maps to give themselves a leg up in eight states — a desperate attempt to gain as many as 12 districts in Congress. WIN more races. ** It's what Charlie called "the clipboard and tennis shoes" work to reach every voter. [ stdin# ]Jocelyn Benson for Governor
Hey there, I
wanted to make sure you saw my finance director Wes’s message from
yesterday.

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/18281?t=1001&akid=1895%2E181023%2EAJmGgs ]Yesterday morning, Wes and I decided to set a $300,000 goal for our
end-of-quarter deadline in just one week. It’s one of the most ambitious
goals we’ve set yet — but it’s what we need heading into the final phase
of this race. Will you help us take the first steps
towards meeting our $300,000 goal and make your
first donation today?

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/18281?t=1002&akid=1895%2E181023%2EAJmGgs ]Donate →

Wes explains why we made this decision below, but the big takeaway is
this: the only way we can defend ourselves against the millions being
poured into Michigan against us is if we have the grassroots power to
fight back.

So while $300,000 is ambitious, it’s exactly what the moment we’re in
demands.

I hope you can give Wes’s message a read — [ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/18281?t=1003&akid=1895%2E181023%2EAJmGgs ]and when you’re done, I hope
I can count on you to pitch in today →

Thank you,

Jocelyn
