it’s Wes, Jocelyn’s Finance Director.

I’m not typically the one reaching out with these types of asks, but our
team just made an important decision, and I wanted you to be one of the
first to hear.

At the end of the month, we’re facing our last end-of-quarter deadline of
the election. This is one of the biggest benchmarks our campaign will
face, and we’ve set our official end-of-quarter goal at $300,000.

I won’t lie: $300,000 can be a
shocking figure. It definitely stresses me out.

But compared to the chunk of cash Elon Musk is currently spending to send
deceptive mailers to boost John James, or the $4,000,000 Republicans spent
on John James’s behalf last month alone, or the false, disgusting ads John
James is currently running against Jocelyn — this goal is absolutely
necessary.

I know I don’t need to tell you just how high the stakes are in this race
— and just how competitive (and expensive) this election is shaping up to
be.

Everything we raise into our End-of-Quarter Fund will go back into winning
this race — from keeping our ads on air, to getting Jocelyn’s message on
one more undecided voter’s social media pages, to helping power our voter

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/18281?t=1011&akid=1895%2E181023%2EAJmGgs ]Hitting this goal is absolutely doable, but it’s going to take the
full force of this grassroots team. Everyone here at Benson HQ is working
day and night to make sure we have the resources to stay competitive and

| | Dear Friend who has common sense, I'm always going to stand with America. I'm always going to reject the extremes. I'm always going to reject Socialism. I'm always going to fight against the anti-American way of life. And this has enraged a lot of people in the media, in my party, and even former staffers --- disgruntled leakers who are viciously and anonymously attacking me. This is what happens when you put common sense and the wellbeing of the people you are supposed to represent ahead of party loyalty. But most of all, I think this is what happens when you clash with the Socialist movement "DSA!" that is hijacking the Democratic party. They want to... Abolish our borders Abolish the electoral college Abolish Israel Abolish the Senate and the Supreme Court (no, seriously, this is in the "DSA!" platform) That bad news is the "DSA!" crazies have gone from the political fringe to controlling one of America's major political parties—and onto ballots across the country. The good news is the hardworking, common-sense Americans I talk to every day still aren't buying it. I mean, a recent Rasmussen poll kind of proves it: 71% of Americans reject socialism 67% of Democrat voters reject socialism While 82% of Republican voters reject socialism But here's the thing. The loudest voice in the room is often the one that looks the most powerful. And I've got to say, the "DSA!" voices in Washington are loud and getting louder. The media is their megaphone. Which is why you may be under the false impression that people really do want the "DSA!" and their extreme policies Nothing could be further from the truth. **[I'm standing up to them.](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjUwMDh9AAwAAAAAAx6ZhfSpJFpffXZDHoJyRHeNNUP7jxEA2qkhBNImk5Lam_fYW0rf9hsej7ZIYvY_9QHiRiQrInOC_3z_UxJymmMT357_VDBugoU4cW25hg)** But sadly I'm pretty much alone on this side of the aisle. So, can I ask you a favor? Whatever your party affiliation is, can I ask you to stand with me against the daily barrage of hit-pieces **[If you can donate just $25 it would be a big help to me.](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjUwMDh9AAwAAAAAAx6ZhfSqjyfk1jeogNvNo2Du3G_wuVFYSJBUfKGUIMvgXij_XsJznZOj2Ylh_yZWvsT6ojqpwSpFEx-37W4BIgptcVnv2uRpn63E4Mri_g)** But it will also send a message. It will show the truth that the "real numbers" are on our side here in Pennsylvania, as well as around the rest of America. You know, I recently stood in front of the iconic U.S. Steel Mill and recorded a video talking about how my friend Dave McCormick and I banded together with President Trump to save this facility and the larger steel industry. But I'm not backing down. Even though I know the media... the "DSA!"... and the party bosses... are going to try even harder to defeat me:
---
**"Fetterman Draws Shadow Primary From Democrats Eager to Replace Him: The Pennsylvania senator has long irked members of his own party" ~ Bloomberg**
---
If you'll stand with me today, I know we can show them that we're not backing down and that the real numbers are on the side of common sense and putting our country first. Thank you! John Fetterman P.S. - I'll bet you're more than a little surprised to get this email from me. So, I want to say thanks for setting aside party affiliation for a second and hearing me out. You see, I'm not a progressive. And I'm definitely not a Democratic Socialist. I'm just a senator with a big mouth who happens to stand for common-sense things like... strong borders, safe streets, a powerful economy, bringing jobs to my constituents, and Israel and Ukraine's right to defend themselves, not to mention the basic machinery of our democracy (the Electoral College, the Senate, and the Supreme Court). If you see eye-to-eye with me, then I could sure use your help. The "DSA!" vision for Pennsylvania and for America is not a healthy one. It is a dangerous one.Common-sense people need to join together now to reject this vision before it's too late. **[Can I count on you to stand with me today?](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjUwMDh9AAwAAAAAAx6ZhfSrnaSGnH4fxgm7rpn0Rfsky6HZJYKopYQEPL4Au9WzBecVwfRgfterGpkE8Xz1TSb-kPdqjt3nT7RnRgwpnqftRkOYKeCWGShTCw)**

clean_body: | = = It's James Carville, folks. I’ve got just one question for you... Can you believe this $#!%?! Trump's second term feels like a nightmare I can't wake up from. His administration has plowed full steam ahead with his downright cuckoo agenda. Our civil liberties have been attacked so many times I lost count. Our public safety has deteriorated overnight. Our systems of due process? Completely tossed aside. We’re now living in a country where citizens exercising their First Amendment rights are shot by federal agents in residential neighborhoods, and journalists can be arrested for reporting national news. Meanwhile, Trump’s MAGA allies in Congress have abandoned their oversight authority. They're nothing more than a doormat for King Trump to wipe his shoes on. I’ve never seen anything like this before — and I've been in politics for a long time. This is unbelievable. For our safety and our future, we can't sit idle while this B.S. rages on. Now is the time to demand change, and Flipping the Senate is the first step. Reclaiming a Democratic Senate majority is our final, best shot at stopping Trump and holding his corrupt administration accountable. Everyone can see that Flipping the Senate this November is a very real possibility, but I won't sugarcoat it. It’s going to be one hell of a fight. Trump’s allies are fundraising BIG. They're dumping truckloads of cash into races across the country to protect their seats and attack Democratic champions. They're desperate to cling to their slim majority this November. And that desperation makes them dangerous. We’ve got to outwork, out-organize, and outsmart them, and there are only 41 days to make this happen, even fewer if you include early voting. clean_body: | Calling all keyboard warriors. | You already know the corners of the internet where the real conversations happen. Your group chats, your feeds, the comment sections you cannot help reading. Those are the places where people work out what to believe. MAGA extremists have spent years pushing misogyny, white supremacy, and contempt for working people in these spaces unopposed. That’s why we are pulling together a cohort of digital activist captains across Pennsylvania to take back our democracy. As a digital activist captain you’ll build a small team of 5 to 10 people you already know and you decide where to work, what to say, and how your team runs. We’ll provide you with training, tools, coaching and a community of organizers and fellow volunteer captains to support you in the fight. We’re hosting an orientation for the cohort to meet for the first time starting on Tuesday, September 29 at 6pm and hope to see you there. Jeffrey Lichtenstein One PA | One PA is a grassroots movement for racial, economic, and social justice in Pennsylvania. clean_body: Let’s clear the air.| | | | | Patriot , I flew above battlefields, passing burning husks of armored vehicles, and in Iraq I poured enough sand out of my boots to fill a desert. You would think that after flying an Apache helicopter through an active war zone, and having God knows how many stray bullets shot my direction, there’s not a thing on this planet that could scare me. I thought so too, until my team reminded me about what’s coming in the next few days. Let me explain. This campaign’s bigger than anything I’ve done in Iraq. Rather than covering for a team on the ground, the fate of more than 10 million people will be decided in November. Campaigning isn’t easy, and sometimes it feels like the weight of the world is on my shoulders. Just before I typed this email, my team reminded me about our upcoming End-of-Quarter fundraising deadline. This isn’t just an arbitrary deadline; this is one of our last BIG goals before the November election. I’m not going to ask you to dig deep into your pockets. All I’m asking is a $1 or more donation, which will go right into my campaign's war chest and help me and President Trump take down the Democrat machine come November. As a combat veteran and a patriot - I give you my word that every dollar matters, and I’m eternally thankful for ANY gift you can make. Time is running out. The following is the letter and its attachments that I sent the rabbis. Draw your own conclusions. If you reach the same conclusion I did then you will know how to vote in November.
September 23, 2026
Dear Rabbi,
I write to you as a concerned Jewish American, an America-first and pro-Israel candidate for Congress in Connecticut's Fourth District, and a former member of the Board of Trustees of Temple Sholom.
_**The views in this letter are mine alone and are not those of any organization with which I am or have been affiliated.**_
Clergy support, especially by Jewish clergy, is not a private courtesy. New York showed that, and Jews have paid that price across the world. When rabbis and Jewish organizations blessed--or appeared to bless--a campaign whose coalition included voices hostile to Israel and to Jews, including the orbit around Zohran Mamdani, the consequence was not "dialogue." It was a signal to congregants, to students, and to people who mean us harm. An endorsement, a shared stage, a banquet letter, or a careful silence next to the wrong partner all count.
The best a faith leader can do in an election is not to turn the bimah into a party headquarters. It is to inform the congregation: what is at stake, who has actually stood where, and what the record is. In a community this polarized, too many people stop at D or R and call that a moral conclusion. A letter after a candidate's name is not a kashrut certificate on Israel, on CAIR, or on the safety of your members.
I recently went to Capitol Hill for Israel Advocacy Day as a private individual, not as a candidate. I went because it mattered--to stand with Israel and to fight antisemitism here. Security funding for Jewish institutions is part of that fight, and I support strengthening the Nonprofit Security Grant Program. It is not the whole fight. Cameras and guards manage risk. They do not eradicate antisemitism.
I have been at too many gatherings after Jews were murdered in this country because they were Jews. Too often the official response, including from Congressman Himes, folded that grief into a single sentence with "Islamophobia." Both bigotries can be condemned. They must not be merged when Jews have just been killed and CAIR is in the conversation. That merger is how a massacre becomes a lecture about tone and minimizes the unique hatred that is antisemitism.
I am challenging Congressman Himes, in office since 2009. He has taken significant support from AIPAC and other pro-Israel donors. That does not close the file or confer a badge as a defender of the Jewish community. A member can take those checks and still treat CAIR as a partner and welcome its influence.
Himes's long-term relationship with CAIR is relevant information that congregants should have before they vote. CAIR has documented links to the Holy Land Foundation; CAIR leaders publicly supported Hamas's October 7 attack on Israel; Texas and Florida have designated CAIR a terrorist organization; and there is a substantial public record concerning CAIR's and its leaders' support for terrorist organizations. That record is not confined to advocacy groups. In January 2022, Newsweek published "CAIR Not Only Inspires Terrorists. It's Historically Linked to Them," documenting CAIR's founding out of the Islamic Association for Palestine, seed money from the Holy Land Foundation, and CAIR's listing by the FBI as an unindicted co-conspirator after HLF's conviction for funneling more than $12 million to Hamas. In August 2026, Newsweek again noted that CAIR's executive director said he was "happy to see" the October 7 pogrom, and that the United Arab Emirates, Texas, and Florida have designated CAIR a terrorist organization. _**Any political candidate who treats CAIR as a partner is not a reliable supporter of the Jewish people or of the survival of the State of Israel.**_
Please review the enclosed items.
**Exhibit A -- **CAIR-Connecticut, June 13, 2022: CAIR-CT said it was in Washington for Muslim Hill Day and would meet that day with the offices of Congressman Himes, Congresswoman DeLauro, and Congressman Larson.
**Exhibit B -- **Congressman Himes, Facebook, October 25, 2023, eighteen days after October 7: "When I met with CAIR-CT earlier this week, I heard about the fear and discrimination faced by too many of my Muslim constituents." He called it "heartbreaking" that families in Southwest Connecticut were "afraid to leave their homes." That is what he chose to put in public while Jewish families were still sitting shiva and hostages were still in tunnels.
**Exhibit C -- **Official letter, November 9, 2019, from Congressman Himes to CAIR's national office, sending warm regards to CAIR's 25th annual banquet, writing that he was "proud this organization is working together to build a better, kinder place to live," and that he "celebrate[d] with you all the long history of CAIR's accomplishments."
**Exhibit D -- **Rabbi Yaakov Menken, Newsweek, January 23, 2022, "CAIR Not Only Inspires Terrorists. It's Historically Linked to Them": CAIR was founded in 1994 by figures who had just left the Islamic Association for Palestine, described by the FBI as a Hamas front; within a month CAIR received seed money from the Holy Land Foundation; HLF was later convicted of providing more than $12 million to Hamas; and the FBI listed CAIR as an unindicted co-conspirator. See also Josh Hammer, Newsweek, August 14, 2026, "The Electoral Integrity Issue Isn't Israel--It's Islam," recording Nihad Awad's "happy to see" remarks on October 7 and the UAE, Texas, and Florida terror designations of CAIR.
You know CAIR's national record after October 7. You know the White House later distanced itself from CAIR. Meeting constituents is one thing. A banquet greeting and a post-massacre meeting with CAIR are another. _**A congregation that is told only "he is a Democrat" or "he gets AIPAC money" is not being informed. It is being spared the record.**_ There is also a tendency, when congregants see a rabbi with a congressman, to treat that rabbi as speaking for the entire Jewish community, as if there were one voice. That impression is rarely corrected in social media or any other form of communication.
On September 21, 2026, the Justice Department told the Fifth Circuit it agrees the government should not enforce the Johnson Amendment when a house of worship speaks about politics to its own congregation, in connection with religious services, through its customary channels. The statute has not been repealed. The government's own position is that ordinary pulpit and in-house speech is church autonomy, not a tax raid. I am not giving tax advice. I am asking you to tell your people what these documents show--not whom to vote for as a party, but who has stood where when it counted.
I will meet privately, walk through the exhibits, and answer for my own record. Party label is not the issue. The record is.
I welcome the opportunity to speak with you. If you give Congressman Himes the pulpit or the bimah, I would respectfully ask the same courtesy, for fairness. That is what is typically required in public forums for nonprofits.".
Respectfully,
**Dr. Michael Goldstein**
Candidate for Congress, Connecticut's Fourth District

**By[Rabbi Yaakov Menken](https://substack.com/redirect/1e55d155-e35a-4f67-95d3-47a64b1b064f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Managing Director, Coalition for Jewish Values
A recent report from the Council on American-Islamic Relations (CAIR), "[Islamophobia in the Mainstream](https://substack.com/redirect/f777a68e-7a75-4ebb-9171-fd03fe2d255a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)," is a case study in projection--the [psychological process](https://substack.com/redirect/21b21e4b-eaa5-49cb-8ce7-3252ceec3857?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of attributing one's own defects to others. In this case, the defect is hate, and the target is an all-too familiar one: the Jewish people and their allies.
It is not difficult here to discern the hater from the hated: Just days after CAIR issued its report, Malik Faisal Akram pursued [CAIR's antisemitic agenda](https://substack.com/redirect/ed8a7b28-8244-42e2-964b-62ab81d3aeae?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by entering a Texas synagogue with a gun. In a [speech](https://substack.com/redirect/d49ab556-cda8-49e8-b49b-52c9f7928f03?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) delivered to a Muslim audience in November, the executive director of CAIR's San Francisco office, Zahra Billoo, identified "Zionist synagogues" like Congregation Beth Israel and all "polite Zionists"--essentially all Jews--as "your enemies," both Islamophobic and opposed to "human rights." Billoo further advised those listening and watching to "fight back."
Rather than disavow her hateful and antisemitic remarks, CAIR [claimed](https://substack.com/redirect/c0f1c446-e6cb-4ef6-a372-acdf9448eda4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that Billoo was "[misquoted](https://substack.com/redirect/c0f1c446-e6cb-4ef6-a372-acdf9448eda4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)" and the victim of an "online smear campaign." Sadly for CAIR, the [video](https://substack.com/redirect/d49ab556-cda8-49e8-b49b-52c9f7928f03?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) is available for all to see.
**Read More on[Opinion](https://substack.com/redirect/167594c7-f4f9-4afd-b831-e3d13ef7cd63?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
In just the past two months, CAIR also organized a [series](https://substack.com/redirect/71a18011-6253-4620-8617-906e735fa758?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of [rallies](https://substack.com/redirect/6fe3e004-dc2a-4177-a085-17bc70043ec2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in Texas for the release of Aafia Siddiqui, just as Akram demanded. The connection between CAIR's statements and Malik Akram's beliefs is undeniable--and this is true regardless of whether Akram watched Billoo's speech or was aware of the rallies. This is because CAIR is part of a global network that promotes a hateful agenda that has targeted both Jews and democratic institutions for decades.
CAIR's report is an exercise in disinformation, dishing out terms like "hate group," "misinformation" and "propaganda" without, in most cases, even a single purported example of "Islamophobia." It is just a projection of CAIR's own bigotry, which frequently takes aim at a list of prominent pro-Israel advocates, the Israel Defense Forces and the international Jewish community at-large.
Undoubtedly, before long, the [Coalition for Jewish Values](https://substack.com/redirect/a3a68753-252d-4399-989d-35e5812fa65a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), where I serve as managing director, will be part of the assembly that CAIR attacks. When informed by a reporter that our organization had [called](https://substack.com/redirect/9fa37dce-e522-451e-8f94-de0b5ad086c2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the report "both pro-terror and antisemitic," CAIR [responded](https://substack.com/redirect/1272f483-716b-4415-a678-db6af044841e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by branding us an "extremist voice." And in calling our assessment of the antisemitic nature of the Texas attack "bizarre and unfounded," CAIR professes to know more about Jew-hatred than do 2,000 observant rabbis. Good luck with that.
Law enforcement vehicles sit in front of the Congregation Beth Israel synagogue on January 16, 2022 in Colleyville, Texas. | _Brandon Bell/Getty Images/Brandon Bell/Getty Images_
In its report, CAIR accused the [Committee for Accuracy in Middle East Reporting and Analysis](https://substack.com/redirect/0431617f-fdd6-4afb-b1fe-6a81396144d1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (CAMERA) of "Islamophobia" because CAMERA once published a [report on The Islamic Society of North America that "accuses multiple American-Muslim organizations and individuals to be front groups for terrorism."](https://substack.com/redirect/0e29dc01-db24-4cb5-8e16-a40ff7e43aa2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The problem for CAIR is that CAMERA's [assertions are true](https://substack.com/redirect/b98e7ea0-d201-4d6b-b358-002197aef83a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
CAIR was [incorporated](https://substack.com/redirect/d1741aa5-957d-4226-83cc-e6ae0ee4ebd7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by Omar Ahmad, Rafiq Jaber and Nihad Awad in 1994. To become its founding director, [Awad](https://substack.com/redirect/ef67e933-2f17-4d22-ad25-8b5aea08a3d4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) left his position as [public relations director](https://substack.com/redirect/e17f0681-58b7-4e31-8700-a072e8837e9f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for the Islamic Association for Palestine (IAP), which has been [described](https://substack.com/redirect/c7398880-4a04-44a6-b96f-162a6e708630?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by the [FBI](https://substack.com/redirect/fd28a663-d689-43b2-a013-6e5f2b6eedd2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) counterterrorism chief as "a front organization for Hamas that engages in propaganda for Islamic militants," and by the U.S. government itself as a [founding member](https://substack.com/redirect/716e979a-f671-4424-80a8-d35dad92bdbc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of the Muslim Brotherhood's "[Palestine Committee](https://substack.com/redirect/a9cae0e9-4865-4c88-b07f-39a419976136?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)." Ahmad was the IAP [president](https://substack.com/redirect/b39f154d-a106-467a-8b85-5bc82afaceaa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at that time, while Jaber [became](https://substack.com/redirect/2e6af740-421a-4ae5-8187-944a4c9779cc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) IAP president in 1996.
Within a month after its formation, CAIR, which was soon [listed](https://substack.com/redirect/01411490-5d2e-40c0-a5c4-0899d7b8ea2a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) as a "working organization" by the Palestine Committee, received a $5,000 check--followed weeks later by a $5,000 [wire transfer](https://substack.com/redirect/ff4040c3-b53d-41d1-ab5b-01cd51d87039?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--from the Holy Land Foundation (HLF).
The HLF was convicted in 2008 of providing over $12 million to Hamas, a U.S. State Department-designated [foreign terrorist organization](https://substack.com/redirect/84bfcf65-f297-4f67-a358-5d7668b44518?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The [FBI](https://substack.com/redirect/4643939f-9cbc-46f3-a46c-984a5ccf20ea?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) called this "the largest victory against terrorist financing in the U.S. since the 9/11 attacks." HLF's founders received [life sentences](https://substack.com/redirect/9dc5789c-5f17-453c-9dbb-5b6193e7bd0a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and CAIR was listed by the FBI as an unindicted [co-conspirator](https://substack.com/redirect/5fe6b9fc-af8e-4df0-be30-c6fb06e80cc5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), serving as the public relations arm of a web of terrorist-affiliated groups.
When CAIR was first accused in U.S. [Senate](https://substack.com/redirect/7bbbf9c9-9c6d-415a-98bd-c020f36a2675?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) testimony of receiving seed money from the HLF, Ahmad [denied](https://substack.com/redirect/ff4040c3-b53d-41d1-ab5b-01cd51d87039?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) it, while Awad [called](https://substack.com/redirect/acb54a10-d172-475b-8306-2a40134a50ec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) it an "outright lie." Presented with a copy of the check, Awad [revised](https://substack.com/redirect/ff4040c3-b53d-41d1-ab5b-01cd51d87039?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) his testimony, describing a $5,000 check less than three weeks after incorporation as "a donation like any other."
With its recent report accusing mainstream Jewish organizations as well as allies of the Jewish people of "Islamophobia," CAIR both inverts hater and hated and advances the extremist agenda of the Muslim Brotherhood: to make Jews less welcome, and to make terrorism against Jews more palatable. This is, in fact, what CAIR has done from effectively day one of its existence.
Now that CAIR has targeted Jews in such an open and egregious manner, it has lost any right to the benefit of the doubt--though, in fact, it never had any such right at the outset. CAIR has unmasked itself as the virulent hate group that it has always been. Americans must oppose CAIR and the antisemitism that it foments and disseminates.
_Rabbi Yaakov Menken is managing director of the[Coalition for Jewish Values](https://substack.com/redirect/a3a68753-252d-4399-989d-35e5812fa65a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)._

Although he did not author the legislation that provides funding to religious organizations for security infrastructure he has gone to Synagogues touting this legislation and its impact on protecting religious worshipers. The funding covers all houses of worship including Churches and Mosques. Thanks for reading The Goldstein Substack! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work. The first response of any Clergy for government assistance is thank you. If you go no further this is a win for Himes. However while Himes is touting funding for security upgrades he is failing to mention his support for CAIR, a pro Islamic organization that has been designated a terrorist organization by Texas and Florida. This organization based on statements by their leaders and articles in the public domain, is in fact ideologically linked to the people that the security funding that Himes touts , is designed to protect against. Himes can't have it both ways, on the one had supporting organizations that have ties to terrorists and then providing funding to protect against these organizations and their sympathizers. The following is the letter and its attachments that I sent the rabbis. Draw your own conclusions. If you reach the same conclusion I did then you will know how to vote in November. September 23, 2026 Dear Rabbi, I write to you as a concerned Jewish American, an America-first and pro-Israel candidate for Congress in Connecticut's Fourth District, and a former member of the Board of Trustees of Temple Sholom. The views in this letter are mine alone and are not those of any organization with which I am or have been affiliated. Clergy support, especially by Jewish clergy, is not a private courtesy. New York showed that, and Jews have paid that price across the world. When rabbis and Jewish organizations blessed--or appeared to bless--a campaign whose coalition included voices hostile to Israel and to Jews, including the orbit around Zohran Mamdani, the consequence was not "dialogue." It was a signal to congregants, to students, and to people who mean us harm. An endorsement, a shared stage, a banquet letter, or a careful silence next to the wrong partner all count. The best a faith leader can do in an election is not to turn the bimah into a party headquarters. It is to inform the congregation: what is at stake, who has actually stood where, and what the record is. In a community this polarized, too many people stop at D or R and call that a moral conclusion. A letter after a candidate's name is not a kashrut certificate on Israel, on CAIR, or on the safety of your members. I recently went to Capitol Hill for Israel Advocacy Day as a private individual, not as a candidate. I went because it mattered--to stand with Israel and to fight antisemitism here. Security funding for Jewish institutions is part of that fight, and I support strengthening the Nonprofit Security Grant Program. It is not the whole fight. Cameras and guards manage risk. They do not eradicate antisemitism. I have been at too many gatherings after Jews were murdered in this country because they were Jews. Too often the official response, including from Congressman Himes, folded that grief into a single sentence with "Islamophobia." Both bigotries can be condemned. They must not be merged when Jews have just been killed and CAIR is in the conversation. That merger is how a massacre becomes a lecture about tone and minimizes the unique hatred that is antisemitism. I am challenging Congressman Himes, in office since 2009. He has taken significant support from AIPAC and other pro-Israel donors. That does not close the file or confer a badge as a defender of the Jewish community. A member can take those checks and still treat CAIR as a partner and welcome its influence. Himes's long-term relationship with CAIR is relevant information that congregants should have before they vote. CAIR has documented links to the Holy Land Foundation; CAIR leaders publicly supported Hamas's October 7 attack on Israel; Texas and Florida have designated CAIR a terrorist organization; and there is a substantial public record concerning CAIR's and its leaders' support for terrorist organizations. That record is not confined to advocacy groups. In January 2022, Newsweek published "CAIR Not Only Inspires Terrorists. It's Historically Linked to Them," documenting CAIR's founding out of the Islamic Association for Palestine, seed money from the Holy Land Foundation, and CAIR's listing by the FBI as an unindicted co-conspirator after HLF's conviction for funneling more than $12 million to Hamas. In August 2026, Newsweek again noted that CAIR's executive director said he was "happy to see" the October 7 pogrom, and that the United Arab Emirates, Texas, and Florida have designated CAIR a terrorist organization. Any political candidate who treats CAIR as a partner is not a reliable supporter of the Jewish people or of the survival of the State of Israel. Please review the enclosed items. Exhibit A -- CAIR-Connecticut, June 13, 2022: CAIR-CT said it was in Washington for Muslim Hill Day and would meet that day with the offices of Congressman Himes, Congresswoman DeLauro, and Congressman Larson. Exhibit B -- Congressman Himes, Facebook, October 25, 2023, eighteen days after October 7: "When I met with CAIR-CT earlier this week, I heard about the fear and discrimination faced by too many of my Muslim constituents." He called it "heartbreaking" that families in Southwest Connecticut were "afraid to leave their homes." That is what he chose to put in public while Jewish families were still sitting shiva and hostages were still in tunnels. Exhibit C -- Official letter, November 9, 2019, from Congressman Himes to CAIR's national office, sending warm regards to CAIR's 25th annual banquet, writing that he was "proud this organization is working together to build a better, kinder place to live," and that he "celebrate[d] with you all the long history of CAIR's accomplishments." Exhibit D -- Rabbi Yaakov Menken, Newsweek, January 23, 2022, "CAIR Not Only Inspires Terrorists. It's Historically Linked to Them": CAIR was founded in 1994 by figures who had just left the Islamic Association for Palestine, described by the FBI as a Hamas front; within a month CAIR received seed money from the Holy Land Foundation; HLF was later convicted of providing more than $12 million to Hamas; and the FBI listed CAIR as an unindicted co-conspirator. See also Josh Hammer, Newsweek, August 14, 2026, "The Electoral Integrity Issue Isn't Israel--It's Islam," recording Nihad Awad's "happy to see" remarks on October 7 and the UAE, Texas, and Florida terror designations of CAIR. You know CAIR's national record after October 7. You know the White House later distanced itself from CAIR. Meeting constituents is one thing. A banquet greeting and a post-massacre meeting with CAIR are another. A congregation that is told only "he is a Democrat" or "he gets AIPAC money" is not being informed. It is being spared the record. There is also a tendency, when congregants see a rabbi with a congressman, to treat that rabbi as speaking for the entire Jewish community, as if there were one voice. That impression is rarely corrected in social media or any other form of communication. On September 21, 2026, the Justice Department told the Fifth Circuit it agrees the government should not enforce the Johnson Amendment when a house of worship speaks about politics to its own congregation, in connection with religious services, through its customary channels. The statute has not been repealed. The government's own position is that ordinary pulpit and in-house speech is church autonomy, not a tax raid. I am not giving tax advice. I am asking you to tell your people what these documents show--not whom to vote for as a party, but who has stood where when it counted. I will meet privately, walk through the exhibits, and answer for my own record. Party label is not the issue. The record is. I welcome the opportunity to speak with you. If you give Congressman Himes the pulpit or the bimah, I would respectfully ask the same courtesy, for fairness. That is what is typically required in public forums for nonprofits.". Respectfully, Dr. Michael Goldstein Candidate for Congress, Connecticut's Fourth District 10 Sandy Ln, Greenwich, CT 06831 914-589-8443 MichaelGoldstein4ct@gmail.com www.goldstein4ct.com Enclosures: Exhibits A -D (as referenced above). Law enforcement vehicles sit in front of the Congregation Beth Israel synagogue on January 16, 2022 in Colleyville, Texas. | Brandon Bell/Getty Images/Brandon Bell/Getty Images In its report, CAIR accused the (CAMERA) of "Islamophobia" because CAMERA once published a The problem for CAIR is that CAMERA's . | ...fundraising is one of my least favorite parts of campaigning.
I knew it came with the territory, but I'm also mindful that plenty of families are watching every dollar right now. Between the gas tank and the grocery cart, I don't take these asks lightly.
So if you're tired of all the fundraising emails you're getting right now, believe me, I get it.
The real fix is bigger than this campaign. I want publicly financed elections so people without generational wealth or the backing of private equity can run without begging for money, and we can shut corporations out of our politics for good. Until we win that, grassroots contributions are what keep this campaign answering to you instead of them.
[If money's tight, close this email and don't think twice. If you've got room, $26 keeps us organizing through November.](https://cefuo8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001nwrInfOWdSmFhLTgq2tgKifIScebGOnWcS7UlfsVcUn7IXz61vPwpEmqrP2Y9c1Xu7q39ufpvaL3RsZEVK07dTFhkMHbi3w3uJ8SiniPfA2F8zHzDAL73XhMMr7q0ucn2kfw_VbluBrN07SszmbvDjU-9S0aKtvB1S8YN7ybeubo0JuxO-5__Vj23GDqmyJQTF8PyZWunYCe0ccQcSimdClNG0qewR2En3rlUVTAkbC99gclZEZd7A==&c=DoMJW4pJrDquYtXNU-8oWkVRiQF_4V7NhoW3lYIhnQzWtQ7T4NJXiw==&ch=8B8llJUUMY7HpdVgOx22DhJG2sMD2LQLZaj4WQhHZ_7l_F-GTD2sdA==)

body:
As one of my strongest supporters, I wanted to let you know that my official merchandise store just launched!

As one of my strongest supporters, I wanted to let you know that my official merchandise store just launched!
With each purchase, my team can continue knocking on doors, calling voters, and organizing to keep this seat blue in November.

| | | My Republican opponent is counting on us to stay quiet. Let’s show him who we are by showing up with our pride on a shirt, hat, or sticker – all available on the store today.
Visit our online store at [**shop.derektranforcongress.com**](https://us.list-manage.com/C7KaNaguGcu?e=fa48019594&c2id=2d2f4814b3c86de5c7569386ec1a86b4).
---
| | Together, we’ll make sure Southern California families are always put first. I’m grateful for your support.
Sincerely,Congressman Derek Tran
---
| | ###
_The son of refugees who worked hard and sacrificed for the American Dream, Congressman Derek Tran joined the Army at 18 to give back to the country that has given him so much. Wanting to continue his career in public service, he ran in California's 45th district to put people ahead of politics and protect democracy, and won. Now, he's running again to ensure everyone no matter what neighborhood they come from has the opportunity to succeed without fear of their freedoms being taken away._
_California’s 45th Congressional District remains one of the most contested battleground races in the country. Last cycle, Derek Tran flipped the seat by just over 600 votes (a 0.2% margin) in the second-closest and most expensive House race ($46 million spent) in the country. A majority-minority district, the District has the third largest AAPI population (41%) of any Congressional District, is 28% Latino, and is home to the largest Vietnamese community in the country. Following Proposition 50, this district brings in over 15,000 new Hispanic voters and over 7,000 new Vietnamese voters, and has a DPI of 52.8%._ _It includes all or part of the cities of Garden Grove, Westminster, Fountain Valley, Cerritos, Buena Park, Placentia, Hawaiian Gardens, Cypress, Artesia, Los Alamitos, La Palma, Norwalk, Stanton, Lakewood, Santa Ana, Seal Beach, and Fullerton, as well as the unincorporated community of Midway City._

name: Sherrod Brown (via DNC HQ)
subject: Crypto dark money PACs are coming after me. I have nowhere else to turn.
body:
We're already getting pummeled. It's about to get worse.
---
Please don't look away, Derek. I just learned that a crypto dark money PAC is dumping $30 million into defeating our campaign. Ohio is their biggest target, and it’s with a historic amount in the final stretch of our race. **These attacks have already started, and we have less than 24 hours to respond.** [**Please rush a split contribution between my campaign and the DNC to help fend off these attacks.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-brown-split?amount=20&refcode=em_20260923_9369_fr&refcode2=9369_22930333_h9_EO9&akid=9369%2E22930333%2Eh9_EO9) **[RUSH $20](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-brown-split?amount=20&refcode=em_20260923_9369_fr&refcode2=9369_22930333_h9_EO9&akid=9369%2E22930333%2Eh9_EO9)** There are a lot of moving pieces, but here's what I know right now: As of today, the Republican establishment was already spending $14 million each week against us. That includes Jon Husted's super PAC, Elon Musk's contributions, Peter Thiel's dark money, and Donald Trump's multi-million-dollar investment. **With these crypto dark money PACs jumping in, that weekly amount is skyrocketing.** For reference, our campaign is currently spending about $2 million on TV ads each week. Combined Republican spending is now at over $100 million against me this cycle. I'm never one to say the sky is falling or sound the alarm unnecessarily. But, Derek, this is not one of those times. **Crypto's new spending could bury us.** They're doing it because Jon Husted is _extremely_ vulnerable and the GOP has seen this tactic work before. In my 2024 race, when crypto started spending against me and we weren't able to respond, the polls started turning in Republicans' favor. _We lost that race._ A few weeks ago, Senate Republicans put out a call for outside groups like data centers and AI to bail Husted out with enormous cash infusions in the Ohio Senate race.**And Derek, this is them answering the call.** **We had no choice but to raise our fundraising goals so we could mount a response to these attacks from Big Tech. Hamada Msallam stands in front of his house in Kuwayya in southwestern Syria, overlooking Wadi Al Raqqad which separates him from the Israeli-occupied Golan Heights. June 10, 2025. Photo by Sam Kimball.
NAWA, Syria--"The Israelis passed through five other villages to get to us," Abdullah Al-Saqr said. The septuagenarian was sitting on an embroidered cushion in a darkened room surrounded by other men from Nawa, a small town in southwestern Syria with houses built of concrete and basalt--the signature black volcanic rock pulled from the earth of Daraa province.
Al-Saqr recounted in detail what happened on April 3, 2025, when the Israeli military that has come to occupy a large swathe of southwestern Syria over the past two years, conducted a violent raid on Nawa. That night, the local residents fought back.
Israeli troops reached the village of Jubaylia, six kilometers (3.7 miles) away, before guards hired to look after vacant farmland spotted the advance and called in young men from Nawa.
"Everyone was armed," Al-Saqr said. "They went out with hunting rifles, army rifles--whatever weapons they had--to stop the Israeli advance."
The first groups raced to the location on motorbikes and engaged the soldiers with small arms. The Israelis called in reinforcements, and the young men of Nawa did the same, calling on their cousins and neighbors; the battle grew as more people arrived in waves. Israeli drones and helicopter gunships struck overhead, targeting locals on the ground. A contingent of Israeli troops hid themselves in a position behind the locals and first responders arriving at the scene, "effectively setting a trap" for those arriving to help the wounded, Al-Saqr said. Israeli artillery positioned in the far distance targeted the road leading to the battle.
In all, nine men from Nawa were killed and 12 wounded. Despite the losses, they managed to turn back the advancing Israeli troops. The battle was just one of several incidents over the past 18 months when local residents in towns and villages across southwestern Syria fought back against occupying Israeli forces.
In that time, resistance to Israeli occupation in Syria has stayed largely local and spontaneous--young men grabbing arms and confronting soldiers during raids in places like Nawa, Kuwayya, and Beit Jinn--with no formal command structure and no government support.
Yet it has produced a real deterrent: in every town that saw armed firefights, Israeli troops have reportedly not returned as of August 2026. Acts of unarmed resistance have been growing as well, with outraged families and residents launching impromptu street demonstrations to protest the Israeli military.
## **Expanding Israeli Occupation**
Syria's entire political and security landscape was transformed on December 8, 2024 when, after nearly 14 years of revolution and war, a lightning offensive led by Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham (HTS), a former al-Qaeda affiliate, [swept into Damascus](https://substack.com/redirect/6d4cba31-170f-497c-84a4-d7b9f9d88c9c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and toppled Bashar al-Assad's government. Within hours, Israeli troops crossed from the occupied Golan Heights into a UN-patrolled buffer zone and later advanced farther into southwestern Syria. Meanwhile, Israeli warplanes launched [hundreds of strikes](https://substack.com/redirect/c4dd2475-6881-415a-8565-45b8c6942daf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Syrian bases, airfields, naval vessels, weapons depots, missiles and air-defense systems, decimating Syria's military capability.
At first, Israel said the ground deployment was a temporary defensive measure and claimed the bombing was intended to prevent strategic weapons from reaching HTS or other groups it considered hostile. It subsequently abandoned any pretense of a limited military presence on the ground, with Defense Minister Israel Katz declaring that [Israeli forces would remain](https://substack.com/redirect/14423add-0788-4863-a35b-76bcf823336c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Syrian Mount Hermon (Jabal al-Shaykh) indefinitely and later reaffirming the military would remain in Syria for an "[unlimited amount of time](https://substack.com/redirect/21362d03-4858-4e6f-a182-300733a444ae?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)." The Syrian government has repeatedly demanded the "immediate and unconditional withdrawal" of Israeli forces to the lines held before December 8, 2024, though it has done little more than issue statements.
In southwestern Syria's Quneitra, Dara'a, and Rif Dimashq (Damascus Countryside) provinces, which abut the UN-patrolled buffer zone, Israeli incursions are almost daily, with night patrols, house raids, checkpoints, and drone flights overhead.
To the north of Nawa, lies the Circassian village of Breiga, whose land spreads out over scenic hills inside the UN buffer zone. Just outside of the village, two locals on a motorcycle warned Drop Site about IDF checkpoints ahead. "Never turn around if you spot one. Just stay calm, or you'll be followed," the local men said.
Under what the Israeli military calls the ["New East" project](https://substack.com/redirect/49feae44-c504-411d-bdc9-90f45551706e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), troops are digging a continuous barrier of earthen walls and trenches four meters deep and four meters wide that passes less than a mile from Breiga. The barrier stretches from the northern Israeli-occupied Golan Heights, down to the southern border tripoint between the Israeli-occupied Golan Heights, Jordan, and Syria, with increased surveillance over the entire area.
Hamza Ghadban, the head of Syria's Sijil Center, has tracked nine Israeli military bases established from Mount Hermon on the Syria-Lebanon border in the north to the Yarmouk River in the southern border with Jordan since the fall of the Assad regime.
The new bases have come alongside the detention of at least 240 Syrian citizens, 46 of them still in Israeli custody as of August 2026. Thirty-six Syrians have been killed by the Israeli military in southwestern Syria, most of them during ground incursions: 13 in Beit Jinn, nine in Nawa, and seven in Kuwayya.
In a speech before the United Nations General Assembly on Wednesday, Syrian president Ahmed al-Sharaa accused Israel of violating Syria's sovereignty and called for Israeli troops to withdraw from Syrian territory to the lines set under a 1974 disengagement agreement. Al-Sharaa said since December 2024, Israel had carried out nearly 500 air and artillery strikes, conducted more than 1,200 incursions into Syria, and detained around 300 people. "We reject the permanent Israeli attempts to impose a fait accompli in Syria," Al-Sharaa said, referring to the Israeli occupation of Syrian territory in the Golan Heights and beyond.
However, residents in southwestern Syria confronting Israeli forces on the ground say the government in Damascus has done little to come to their aid.
## **Localized Resistance**
Back in Nawa, Muhammad Khair Al-Batal said that the Israeli helicopter gunships arrived after the initial skirmishes began that night in April. "Half an hour later, we saw five or six [Israeli] helicopters arrive. As soon as they located someone, they struck him."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9563f1d0-7084-4f67-8efe-e8b7c3ee8fd3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Muhammad Khair Al-Batal, 27, a local resident who joined the battle of Nawa against the Israeli military in Nawa, Daraa, southwestern Syria on June 10, 2025. Photo by Sam Kimball.
Among the casualties were two brothers from the Batha family: "Hashim was killed and Abdullah was wounded," Al-Saqr said. "A missile landed in front of Muhammad al-Rifai and killed him."
"We believed the small drones were filming us and transmitting our coordinates to the helicopters so they could strike," he added. "The missiles were fired from a safe distance from their soldiers so that they would not be harmed."
Choking back his tears, Abdullah al-Saqr pointed to photos on a battered smartphone: the corpses of young men killed in the clash that night, one of them his son. "His name was Issa al-Saqr," he said, his eyes red and voice cracking. "He was married and had four children."
By all accounts, the resistance was spontaneous rather than planned. "Everything happened suddenly," Muhammad al-Saqr said. "We never expected them to enter in the first place."
Residents also suspected that Israel had manipulated the local telecommunications network. "At first, phone coverage was unusually strong--in this area, it is normally weak," he said. "They strengthened the network, and then they began striking us," he said, adding that he believed the Israelis strengthened mobile coverage to allow for better communication and precise targeting through the network signal.
No support arrived from the government in Damascus. "We asked the new government for help, but no help came," said Jihad Tayasni, a local resident in Nawa. He said requests for military support and emergency rescue workers went unanswered. "They did not even allow an ambulance to reach us. Civilian cars were the ones that went in and evacuated the wounded."
Outmanned and outgunned, the local residents of Nawa suffered losses but they did manage to prevent the advancing Israeli troops from entering the town or occupying Tal Al-Jumoua, a strategic Assad-era military position atop a nearby mountain. Israeli forces have occupied hilltops throughout southwestern Syria where they have built or reinforced military bases with sweeping views over the region. However, these acts of localized resistance seem to have acted as a deterrent. The Israeli military used to enter that stretch of the mountain on an almost daily basis, according to residents. "Since the battle," al-Saqr said, "it has not returned."
The same can be said about the village of Kuwayya, which lies some 16 miles to the south of Nawa and overlooks the Yarmouk River, which forms part of Syria's border with Jordan. Last year, Israeli ground troops advanced on the town only to be met with bullets
"It was the first and last intervention," said Hamada Msallam, a farmer who only offered a pseudonym out of fear of reprisals. He spoke to Drop Site from his home perched on a hill above the river.
On March 25, 2025, he found Israeli soldiers spread through the fields as he walked to his agricultural land below the village. When he and other farmers refused to let them into the village, the soldiers fired warning shots.
"Men from the village grabbed weapons from their homes and went and stood against the Israelis," Msallam said. "It wasn't small arms against small arms. The moment we fired, they struck us with explosives."
According to Msallam, the Israelis sent surveillance drones over the village and later sent armed drones which fired missiles. In the battle, local resistance won out, and the Israelis withdrew, leaving six local men dead. He said that after the battle, the Israeli forces never came back.
When asked why resistance broke out in Kuwayya and not other villages facing the same patrols, Msallam only said it was a spontaneous act in the moment. "If the Israelis had come in on a different road, or caught us off guard, perhaps there would have been no resistance, or no blood spilled," he said. "But there was fire in all the men's hearts in the village."
Msallam had heard rumors of soldiers in other villages dragging residents-including women-out of their homes at night. "I, my brother, my son, will die fighting before they ever enter our homes and touch our women," he said. "Our home is our dignity."
Other forms of quieter resistance have sprung up in nearby communities, with neighboring villages piling stones and earth to build barriers across roads in order to block Israeli patrols.
On June 28, 2026, residents of Abdeen, a village just two and a half miles to the north of Kuwayya, hurled stones at an Israeli patrol that answered with warning shots and artillery fire, prompting most of the village to flee the area. During one such confrontation near Abdeen, an Israeli soldier dropped a military-issue phone that ended up in a local's hands, marked "Olar"--the Israeli military's name for [Orion](https://substack.com/redirect/5287930e-2490-44a8-8033-a63cdfb0b967?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), a battlefield-mapping and terrain-analysis system.
At the Al-Jazeera base, an old Assad-era military barracks taken over by the Israelis, Israeli forces have demanded that residents of nearby Kuwayya hand over their weapons, and conducted routine searches of their homes. "People here genuinely believe they are left to their own fate," one farmer said.
The newly occupied bases have become launching points for Israeli patrols and military operations against locals. On August 24, an Israeli patrol [launched a raid](https://substack.com/redirect/347f1a88-8601-4984-8792-35323107eea5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from Al-Jazeera base with ground troops and vehicles backed by drones into Ma'ariya, a village just over a mile west of Kuwayya.
Beit Jinn, an isolated farming community 40 miles to the north of Kuwayya, in the mountains near the Israel-Lebanon-Syria border nestled among water channels and tree cover, has been subject to multiple Israeli incursions over the years.
On June 12, 2025, Israeli troops entered the village and abducted several young men from their homes. "We were at home, sleeping. At 3 a.m. they came, terrorizing the boys and women," said Fatima Mohamed Safadi, a local resident.
"They let their dogs into the house and then entered themselves. They pulled young men out of their homes, beat them up, and took them in their cars," she said, sitting at a plastic table in the shade of Beit Jinn's trees.
Two of Safadi's sons were taken in the raid. She said one of them had been a fighter in the Free Syrian Army years before. The Israeli military branded both of them as terrorists. For seven months she didn't know if they were alive, until she saw a YouTube [video](https://substack.com/redirect/52a1da04-d27d-4fae-8a5a-9e7441e84400?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of a fellow prisoner in Israel naming the men held alongside him. "That is how we found them," she said.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fe877351-8519-43b0-a0e3-dacdc2dc8a7f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Fatima Mohamed Safadi holds up a video of a former Palestinian where he mentions the names of her two sons who were imprisoned with him in Ofer Prison in Israel. Beit Jinn, southerwestern Syria. June 14, 2026. Photo by Safaa Al Safadi.
"No one fought back" that night, she said. "We lived next to them like neighbors. When they came in before, they never talked to us." During the civil war, factions from Beit Jinn even received military support from Israel in their battle against the Assad government. Residents believed that history would protect them.
June 12, 2025 changed that. Israeli forces killed a local resident, Mohammed Hamada, and arrested seven others, including Safadi's sons. Locals blamed informants for giving up their names. Safaa Safadi, a computer engineer and activist from the village, said the detainees were transferred to Israel and accused of belonging to Hamas, an allegation their families deny.
When the next Israeli raid came in late November, some in the village decided to resist. The response was fierce but unorganized.
Villagers rained bullets on the Israeli military unit from the streets and homes of Beit Jinn. During the firefight, "My neighbors told me that a local fighter was knocking on doors asking for ammunition," Safaa said. "But neighbors were too afraid to assist him for fear that they would be the next target. The situation was chaotic and no one knew what was happening. People chose to stay out of it."
"The guys resisting shot at an Israeli Humvee," said Mohammed Abderrazzaq Al-Saadi, the mokhtar, or community leader, of Beit Jinn. "One of [the fighters firing at the Humvee] was Hassan, my son, a martyr. It was supposed to be his wedding day," Al-Saadi said somberly. Israeli soldiers abandoned the Humvee. "When they could not retrieve it, they targeted it from the air with two missiles," Al-Saadi said.
Israel called in air support: warplanes, artillery, tank fire, drones, and helicopters through the night, while ambulances were kept out for hours. "The shelling began by all possible means--from warplanes, to artillery shelling from Jabal al-Sheikh [Mount Hermon], to direct tank shelling on every location," Safaa said.
Thirteen people were killed and as many as 35 wounded--five from the Hamada family alone, including four-year-old Shahad. The Israeli military later [said](https://substack.com/redirect/463f7216-7a3b-4222-80aa-545df6bcf81d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) six Israeli soldiers were wounded in the operation. The attack forced nearly all the 2,500 residents of the village to flee. Only a handful have been able to return.
"We did not initiate any attack on them, not even a stone, we were shocked that they were attacking us," Safaa said. "We are the same people, before and after the fall of Assad... why would they change their intentions towards us? We live in fear of a repetition of what happened."
Since the raids, residents have made repeated trips to Damascus to demand that the government press for their relatives' release, including holding a [street protest ](https://substack.com/redirect/c364024c-afbe-4006-9fa5-884ffcb0487b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)in front of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on April 26, 2025. The ministry [said](https://substack.com/redirect/e6cbc77f-d928-4a76-a3f9-7c3cc6bf6349?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) it "condemns in the strongest possible terms the criminal attack perpetrated by a patrol of the Israeli occupation forces that infiltrated the town of Beit Jinn," describing the subsequent deliberate bombardment of civilian homes as "a fully fledged war crime," and held Israel "fully responsible for this grave aggression." The government only told residents that negotiations are ongoing and that family members should wait for the results.
## **The Proclamations of Uli Al-Ba 'as**
There have been claims of more organized resistance to the Israeli occupation of southwestern Syria, though the veracity of those claims remains dubious. An Iran-linked group calling itself Uli al-Ba'as--Possessors of Might, formally the Islamic Resistance Front in Syria--has claimed credit on the internet for several clashes with Israeli forces, mostly in southwestern Syria.
The group announced itself in January 2025 under a different name, Jabhat Tahrir al-Janoub, the "South Liberation Front," which appeared on paper leaflets circulated across the Syrian south before it rebranded as Uli al-Ba'as. In a written statement sent to Drop Site on Telegram, the Uli al-Ba'as media office described the group as taking pride in belonging to "the Axis of Resistance extending from Tehran to Beirut and Palestine," drawing on inspiration from "the experiences of Hezbollah and Hamas" and their "history full of victories and jihad against Zionism."
The statement said Uli al-Ba'as operates as "an inseparable part of the joint operations rooms of the cross-border Axis of Resistance," exchanging intelligence and logistics with allies like Hezbollah. The statement claims rocket strikes on Israeli positions at Tal al-Ahmar and the Al-Jazeera base, among others.
It also claimed a parallel campaign against Syria's own transitional government, whose security services it brands as "tools of the Zionist enemy."
Uli al-Ba'as special security groups, the statement says, have carried out "a series of silent strikes and hit-and-run attacks" against government security offices in Dara'a and Rif Dimashq, ranging from assassinating officers to foiling attempts to locate its rocket batteries.
However, researchers who track the group remain skeptical that its rhetoric matches its actions on the ground. Analyst Wail Olwan from Jusoor Research Center said Uli al-Ba'as messaging consistently outpaces independently verifiable attacks.
Syria-based researcher Aymenn al-Tamimi notes the group is itself split into two rival factions that accuse each other of being infiltrated, and that one faction's claim that two of its fighters died fighting in Abdeen appears to be fabricated, as he found no evidence either man died there at all.
In contrast to the proclamations of Uli al-Ba'as, what resistance there is in Syria appears to be ad hoc, organic, and reactive.

Graffiti on a bus stop at the entrance of of Jubbatha Al Khashab in southwestern Syria declares that the village "refuses Israeli incursions." June 13, 2026. Photo by Sam Kimball.
On December 9, 2025, an Israeli patrol of seven vehicles set up an unexpected checkpoint inside Khan Arnabeh-the main market and administrative town in Quneitra province, hugging the UN buffer zone. It was the first time Israeli forces had established a direct presence in the town.
Villagers gathered to confront them. When an officer shouted in Arabic demanding they fall back, the mukhtar approached the Israelis while the crowd held its ground through a volley of warning shots.
"This is my land. When you're the owner of the land, you don't need someone to encourage you to resist," Mohammad Debbek, a young Syrian from Khan Arnabeh, said, wearing an AK-47 pendant around his neck as he spoke.
During the confrontation, villagers threw rocks to force the patrol out. As troops opened fire, a round struck the back of Debbek's leg. Months later, he walks with crutches and is still receiving treatment.
The standoff in Khan Arnabeh was an early example of unarmed civilian pushback. By April 2026, that localized defiance had grown into organized demonstrations across Quneitra, coordinated over Facebook and WhatsApp.
24-year-old organizer Ilaf Obeid, of the group Syrians for Palestine, helped drive a motorcycle rally near the neighboring village of Al-Rafeed and a flag-burning at Khan Arnabeh's roundabout to protest the Israeli presence. For Obeid, non-violent action is both principled and necessary.
"Syria cannot bear armed conflict right now," she said. "But when [the Israelis] see resistance, they think twice about advancing." Patrols, she said, have visibly backed off wherever demonstrations took place.
