June 10, 2025. Photo by Sam Kimball. NAWA, Syria--"The Israelis passed through five other villages to get to us," Abdullah Al-Saqr said. The septuagenarian was sitting on an embroidered cushion in a darkened room surrounded by other men from Nawa, a small town in southwestern Syria with houses built of concrete and basalt--the signature black volcanic rock pulled from the earth of Daraa province. Al-Saqr recounted in detail what happened on April 3, 2025, when the Israeli military that has come to occupy a large swathe of southwestern Syria over the past two years, conducted a violent raid on Nawa. That night, the local residents fought back. Israeli troops reached the village of Jubaylia, six kilometers (3.7 miles) away, before guards hired to look after vacant farmland spotted the advance and called in young men from Nawa. "Everyone was armed," Al-Saqr said. "They went out with hunting rifles, army rifles--whatever weapons they had--to stop the Israeli advance." The first groups raced to the location on motorbikes and engaged the soldiers with small arms. The Israelis called in reinforcements, and the young men of Nawa did the same, calling on their cousins and neighbors; the battle grew as more people arrived in waves. Israeli drones and helicopter gunships struck overhead, targeting locals on the ground. A contingent of Israeli troops hid themselves in a position behind the locals and first responders arriving at the scene, "effectively setting a trap" for those arriving to help the wounded, Al-Saqr said. Israeli artillery positioned in the far distance targeted the road leading to the battle. In all, nine men from Nawa were killed and 12 wounded. Despite the losses, they managed to turn back the advancing Israeli troops. The battle was just one of several incidents over the past 18 months when local residents in towns and villages across southwestern Syria fought back against occupying Israeli forces. In that time, resistance to Israeli occupation in Syria has stayed largely local and spontaneous--young men grabbing arms and confronting soldiers during raids in places like Nawa, Kuwayya, and Beit Jinn--with no formal command structure and no government support. Yet it has produced a real deterrent: in every town that saw armed firefights, Israeli troops have reportedly not returned as of August 2026. Acts of unarmed resistance have been growing as well, with outraged families and residents launching impromptu street demonstrations to protest the Israeli military. Expanding Israeli Occupation Syria's entire political and security landscape was transformed on December 8, 2024 when, after nearly 14 years of revolution and war, a lightning offensive led by Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham (HTS), a former al-Qaeda affiliate, and toppled Bashar al-Assad's government. Within hours, Israeli troops crossed from the occupied Golan Heights into a UN-patrolled buffer zone and later advanced farther into southwestern Syria. Meanwhile, Israeli warplanes launched on Syrian bases, airfields, naval vessels, weapons depots, missiles and air-defense systems, decimating Syria's military capability. At first, Israel said the ground deployment was a temporary defensive measure and claimed the bombing was intended to prevent strategic weapons from reaching HTS or other groups it considered hostile. It subsequently abandoned any pretense of a limited military presence on the ground, with Defense Minister Israel Katz declaring that on Syrian Mount Hermon (Jabal al-Shaykh) indefinitely and later reaffirming the military would remain in Syria for an "." The Syrian government has repeatedly demanded the "immediate and unconditional withdrawal" of Israeli forces to the lines held before December 8, 2024, though it has done little more than issue statements. In southwestern Syria's Quneitra, Dara'a, and Rif Dimashq (Damascus Countryside) provinces, which abut the UN-patrolled buffer zone, Israeli incursions are almost daily, with night patrols, house raids, checkpoints, and drone flights overhead. To the north of Nawa, lies the Circassian village of Breiga, whose land spreads out over scenic hills inside the UN buffer zone. Just outside of the village, two locals on a motorcycle warned Drop Site about IDF checkpoints ahead. "Never turn around if you spot one. Just stay calm, or you'll be followed," the local men said. Under what the Israeli military calls the , troops are digging a continuous barrier of earthen walls and trenches four meters deep and four meters wide that passes less than a mile from Breiga. The barrier stretches from the northern Israeli-occupied Golan Heights, down to the southern border tripoint between the Israeli-occupied Golan Heights, Jordan, and Syria, with increased surveillance over the entire area. Hamza Ghadban, the head of Syria's Sijil Center, has tracked nine Israeli military bases established from Mount Hermon on the Syria-Lebanon border in the north to the Yarmouk River in the southern border with Jordan since the fall of the Assad regime. The new bases have come alongside the detention of at least 240 Syrian citizens, 46 of them still in Israeli custody as of August 2026. Thirty-six Syrians have been killed by the Israeli military in southwestern Syria, most of them during ground incursions: 13 in Beit Jinn, nine in Nawa, and seven in Kuwayya. In a speech before the United Nations General Assembly on Wednesday, Syrian president Ahmed al-Sharaa accused Israel of violating Syria's sovereignty and called for Israeli troops to withdraw from Syrian territory to the lines set under a 1974 disengagement agreement. Al-Sharaa said since December 2024, Israel had carried out nearly 500 air and artillery strikes, conducted more than 1,200 incursions into Syria, and detained around 300 people. "We reject the permanent Israeli attempts to impose a fait accompli in Syria," Al-Sharaa said, referring to the Israeli occupation of Syrian territory in the Golan Heights and beyond. However, residents in southwestern Syria confronting Israeli forces on the ground say the government in Damascus has done little to come to their aid. Localized Resistance Back in Nawa, Muhammad Khair Al-Batal said that the Israeli helicopter gunships arrived after the initial skirmishes began that night in April. "Half an hour later, we saw five or six [Israeli] helicopters arrive. As soon as they located someone, they struck him." | | ---|---|--- Muhammad Khair Al-Batal, 27, a local resident who joined the battle of Nawa against the Israeli military in Nawa, Daraa, southwestern Syria on June 10, 2025. Photo by Sam Kimball. Among the casualties were two brothers from the Batha family: "Hashim was killed and Abdullah was wounded," Al-Saqr said. "A missile landed in front of Muhammad al-Rifai and killed him." "We believed the small drones were filming us and transmitting our coordinates to the helicopters so they could strike," he added. "The missiles were fired from a safe distance from their soldiers so that they would not be harmed." Choking back his tears, Abdullah al-Saqr pointed to photos on a battered smartphone: the corpses of young men killed in the clash that night, one of them his son. "His name was Issa al-Saqr," he said, his eyes red and voice cracking. "He was married and had four children." By all accounts, the resistance was spontaneous rather than planned. "Everything happened suddenly," Muhammad al-Saqr said. "We never expected them to enter in the first place." Residents also suspected that Israel had manipulated the local telecommunications network. "At first, phone coverage was unusually strong--in this area, it is normally weak," he said. "They strengthened the network, and then they began striking us," he said, adding that he believed the Israelis strengthened mobile coverage to allow for better communication and precise targeting through the network signal. No support arrived from the government in Damascus. "We asked the new government for help, but no help came," said Jihad Tayasni, a local resident in Nawa. He said requests for military support and emergency rescue workers went unanswered. "They did not even allow an ambulance to reach us. Civilian cars were the ones that went in and evacuated the wounded." Outmanned and outgunned, the local residents of Nawa suffered losses but they did manage to prevent the advancing Israeli troops from entering the town or occupying Tal Al-Jumoua, a strategic Assad-era military position atop a nearby mountain. Israeli forces have occupied hilltops throughout southwestern Syria where they have built or reinforced military bases with sweeping views over the region. However, these acts of localized resistance seem to have acted as a deterrent. The Israeli military used to enter that stretch of the mountain on an almost daily basis, according to residents. "Since the battle," al-Saqr said, "it has not returned." The same can be said about the village of Kuwayya, which lies some 16 miles to the south of Nawa and overlooks the Yarmouk River, which forms part of Syria's border with Jordan. Last year, Israeli ground troops advanced on the town only to be met with bullets "It was the first and last intervention," said Hamada Msallam, a farmer who only offered a pseudonym out of fear of reprisals. He spoke to Drop Site from his home perched on a hill above the river. On March 25, 2025, he found Israeli soldiers spread through the fields as he walked to his agricultural land below the village. When he and other farmers refused to let them into the village, the soldiers fired warning shots. "Men from the village grabbed weapons from their homes and went and stood against the Israelis," Msallam said. "It wasn't small arms against small arms. The moment we fired, they struck us with explosives." According to Msallam, the Israelis sent surveillance drones over the village and later sent armed drones which fired missiles. In the battle, local resistance won out, and the Israelis withdrew, leaving six local men dead. He said that after the battle, the Israeli forces never came back. When asked why resistance broke out in Kuwayya and not other villages facing the same patrols, Msallam only said it was a spontaneous act in the moment. "If the Israelis had come in on a different road, or caught us off guard, perhaps there would have been no resistance, or no blood spilled," he said. "But there was fire in all the men's hearts in the village." Msallam had heard rumors of soldiers in other villages dragging residents-including women-out of their homes at night. "I, my brother, my son, will die fighting before they ever enter our homes and touch our women," he said. "Our home is our dignity." Other forms of quieter resistance have sprung up in nearby communities, with neighboring villages piling stones and earth to build barriers across roads in order to block Israeli patrols. On June 28, 2026, residents of Abdeen, a village just two and a half miles to the north of Kuwayya, hurled stones at an Israeli patrol that answered with warning shots and artillery fire, prompting most of the village to flee the area. During one such confrontation near Abdeen, an Israeli soldier dropped a military-issue phone that ended up in a local's hands, marked "Olar"--the Israeli military's name for , a battlefield-mapping and terrain-analysis system. At the Al-Jazeera base, an old Assad-era military barracks taken over by the Israelis, Israeli forces have demanded that residents of nearby Kuwayya hand over their weapons, and conducted routine searches of their homes. "People here genuinely believe they are left to their own fate," one farmer said. The newly occupied bases have become launching points for Israeli patrols and military operations against locals. On August 24, an Israeli patrol from Al-Jazeera base with ground troops and vehicles backed by drones into Ma'ariya, a village just over a mile west of Kuwayya. Beit Jinn, an isolated farming community 40 miles to the north of Kuwayya, in the mountains near the Israel-Lebanon-Syria border nestled among water channels and tree cover, has been subject to multiple Israeli incursions over the years. On June 12, 2025, Israeli troops entered the village and abducted several young men from their homes. "We were at home, sleeping. At 3 a.m. they came, terrorizing the boys and women," said Fatima Mohamed Safadi, a local resident. "They let their dogs into the house and then entered themselves. They pulled young men out of their homes, beat them up, and took them in their cars," she said, sitting at a plastic table in the shade of Beit Jinn's trees. Two of Safadi's sons were taken in the raid. She said one of them had been a fighter in the Free Syrian Army years before. The Israeli military branded both of them as terrorists. For seven months she didn't know if they were alive, until she saw a YouTube of a fellow prisoner in Israel naming the men held alongside him. "That is how we found them," she said. | | ---|---|--- Fatima Mohamed Safadi holds up a video of a former Palestinian where he mentions the names of her two sons who were imprisoned with him in Ofer Prison in Israel. Beit Jinn, southerwestern Syria. June 14, 2026. Photo by Safaa Al Safadi. "No one fought back" that night, she said. "We lived next to them like neighbors. When they came in before, they never talked to us." During the civil war, factions from Beit Jinn even received military support from Israel in their battle against the Assad government. Residents believed that history would protect them. June 12, 2025 changed that. Israeli forces killed a local resident, Mohammed Hamada, and arrested seven others, including Safadi's sons. Locals blamed informants for giving up their names. Safaa Safadi, a computer engineer and activist from the village, said the detainees were transferred to Israel and accused of belonging to Hamas, an allegation their families deny. When the next Israeli raid came in late November, some in the village decided to resist. The response was fierce but unorganized. Villagers rained bullets on the Israeli military unit from the streets and homes of Beit Jinn. During the firefight, "My neighbors told me that a local fighter was knocking on doors asking for ammunition," Safaa said. "But neighbors were too afraid to assist him for fear that they would be the next target. The situation was chaotic and no one knew what was happening. People chose to stay out of it." "The guys resisting shot at an Israeli Humvee," said Mohammed Abderrazzaq Al-Saadi, the mokhtar, or community leader, of Beit Jinn. "One of [the fighters firing at the Humvee] was Hassan, my son, a martyr. It was supposed to be his wedding day," Al-Saadi said somberly. Israeli soldiers abandoned the Humvee. "When they could not retrieve it, they targeted it from the air with two missiles," Al-Saadi said. Israel called in air support: warplanes, artillery, tank fire, drones, and helicopters through the night, while ambulances were kept out for hours. "The shelling began by all possible means--from warplanes, to artillery shelling from Jabal al-Sheikh [Mount Hermon], to direct tank shelling on every location," Safaa said. Thirteen people were killed and as many as 35 wounded--five from the Hamada family alone, including four-year-old Shahad. The Israeli military later six Israeli soldiers were wounded in the operation. The attack forced nearly all the 2,500 residents of the village to flee. Only a handful have been able to return. "We did not initiate any attack on them, not even a stone, we were shocked that they were attacking us," Safaa said. "We are the same people, before and after the fall of Assad... why would they change their intentions towards us? We live in fear of a repetition of what happened." Since the raids, residents have made repeated trips to Damascus to demand that the government press for their relatives' release, including holding a front of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on April 26, 2025. The ministry it "condemns in the strongest possible terms the criminal attack perpetrated by a patrol of the Israeli occupation forces that infiltrated the town of Beit Jinn," describing the subsequent deliberate bombardment of civilian homes as "a fully fledged war crime," and held Israel "fully responsible for this grave aggression." The government only told residents that negotiations are ongoing and that family members should wait for the results. The Proclamations of Uli Al-Ba 'as There have been claims of more organized resistance to the Israeli occupation of southwestern Syria, though the veracity of those claims remains dubious. An Iran-linked group calling itself Uli al-Ba'as--Possessors of Might, formally the Islamic Resistance Front in Syria--has claimed credit on the internet for several clashes with Israeli forces, mostly in southwestern Syria. The group announced itself in January 2025 under a different name, Jabhat Tahrir al-Janoub, the "South Liberation Front," which appeared on paper leaflets circulated across the Syrian south before it rebranded as Uli al-Ba'as. In a written statement sent to Drop Site on Telegram, the Uli al-Ba'as media office described the group as taking pride in belonging to "the Axis of Resistance extending from Tehran to Beirut and Palestine," drawing on inspiration from "the experiences of Hezbollah and Hamas" and their "history full of victories and jihad against Zionism." The statement said Uli al-Ba'as operates as "an inseparable part of the joint operations rooms of the cross-border Axis of Resistance," exchanging intelligence and logistics with allies like Hezbollah. The statement claims rocket strikes on Israeli positions at Tal al-Ahmar and the Al-Jazeera base, among others. It also claimed a parallel campaign against Syria's own transitional government, whose security services it brands as "tools of the Zionist enemy." Uli al-Ba'as special security groups, the statement says, have carried out "a series of silent strikes and hit-and-run attacks" against government security offices in Dara'a and Rif Dimashq, ranging from assassinating officers to foiling attempts to locate its rocket batteries. However, researchers who track the group remain skeptical that its rhetoric matches its actions on the ground. Analyst Wail Olwan from Jusoor Research Center said Uli al-Ba'as messaging consistently outpaces independently verifiable attacks. Syria-based researcher Aymenn al-Tamimi notes the group is itself split into two rival factions that accuse each other of being infiltrated, and that one faction's claim that two of its fighters died fighting in Abdeen appears to be fabricated, as he found no evidence either man died there at all. In contrast to the proclamations of Uli al-Ba'as, what resistance there is in Syria appears to be ad hoc, organic, and reactive. | | ---|---|--- Graffiti on a bus stop at the entrance of of Jubbatha Al Khashab in southwestern Syria declares that the village "refuses Israeli incursions." June 13, 2026. Photo by Sam Kimball. On December 9, 2025, an Israeli patrol of seven vehicles set up an unexpected checkpoint inside Khan Arnabeh-the main market and administrative town in Quneitra province, hugging the UN buffer zone. It was the first time Israeli forces had established a direct presence in the town. Villagers gathered to confront them. When an officer shouted in Arabic demanding they fall back, the mukhtar approached the Israelis while the crowd held its ground through a volley of warning shots. "This is my land. When you're the owner of the land, you don't need someone to encourage you to resist," Mohammad Debbek, a young Syrian from Khan Arnabeh, said, wearing an AK-47 pendant around his neck as he spoke. During the confrontation, villagers threw rocks to force the patrol out. As troops opened fire, a round struck the back of Debbek's leg. Months later, he walks with crutches and is still receiving treatment. The standoff in Khan Arnabeh was an early example of unarmed civilian pushback. By April 2026, that localized defiance had grown into organized demonstrations across Quneitra, coordinated over Facebook and WhatsApp. 24-year-old organizer Ilaf Obeid, of the group Syrians for Palestine, helped drive a motorcycle rally near the neighboring village of Al-Rafeed and a flag-burning at Khan Arnabeh's roundabout to protest the Israeli presence. For Obeid, non-violent action is both principled and necessary. "Syria cannot bear armed conflict right now," she said. "But when [the Israelis] see resistance, they think twice about advancing." Patrols, she said, have visibly backed off wherever demonstrations took place. Ohio is the only state they are targeting, and it’s with a historic amount in the final stretch of our race. These attacks are imminent, and our response window is closing fast. There's a lot of moving pieces, but here's what I know right now: Before this, the Republican establishment was already spending $14 million each week against us. That includes Jon Husted's super PAC, Elon Musk's contributions, Peter Thiel's dark money, and Donald Trump's multi-million dollar investment. Every single week. With crypto jumping in, that weekly amount is skyrocketing. For reference, our campaign is currently spending about $2 million on TV ads each week. Combined Republican spending is now at $238 million against me this cycle. I'm never one to say the sky is falling or sound the alarm unnecessarily. But, Peter, this is not one of those times. Crypto's new spending could bury us. They're doing it because Jon Husted is extremely vulnerable and the GOP has seen this tactic work before. In my 2024 race, when crypto started spending against me and we weren't able to respond, the polls started turning in Republicans' favor. We lost that race. A few weeks ago, Senate Republicans put out a call for outside groups like data centers and AI to bail Husted out with enormous cash infusions in the Ohio Senate race. And Peter, this is them answering the call. We had no choice but to raise our fundraising goals so we could mount a response to these attacks from Big Tech. We had terrific responses overall with very few surprises - government accountability, cost of living, the economy, and access to health care are the top federal issues on everyone’s minds. **Gabe Vasquez (NM-02)** is laser focused on lowering costs, securing better paying jobs and making Southern New Mexico communities safer in this district Trump won in 2024.

**Marcy Kaptur (OH-09)** is the longest serving woman in Congress and a fighter for Northeast Ohio. Republicans couldn’t beat her in 2024, so they re-drew the congressional map in a desperate attempt to try and flip this seat.

**Henry Cuellar (TX-28) and Vicente Gonzalez (TX-34)** have a proven record of delivering for South Texas. Across Texas and the country, a wave of Latino voters are ready to reject Republicans at the ballot box.

**Bill Hill (AK-AL)** is a commercial fisherman, union construction worker and educator of nearly 25 years. Bill understands the economic pressures Alaskans are facing right now. He is running to make government work for hardworking families, because he is one.

As a teen, **Manny Rutinel (CO-08)** worked at McDonalds, tutored kids and even sold plasma to help pay the bills after the bank foreclosed on his family home. Manny is running for Congress to fight for working families, create good paying jobs and fix our broken healthcare system.

**Shannon Taylor (VA-01)** is a career prosecutor with a 90% homicide conviction rate. In 2011, Shannon became the first Democrat in nearly 40 years and first woman ever to win the office of Henrico Commonwealth’s Attorney. She’s ready to flip Virginia’s First Congressional District blue.

DCCC Red Alert Round #2 Frontline Members: Gabe Vasquez (NM-02) Tom Suozzi (NY-03) Marcy Kaptur (OH-09) Henry Cuellar (TX-28) Vicente Gonzalez (TX-34) Red to Blue Candidates: Bill Hill (AK-AL) Manny Rutinel (CO-08) Will Lawrence (MI-07) Shannon Taylor (VA-01) Mitch Berman (WI-01) Gabe Vasquez (NM-02) is laser focused on lowering costs, securing better paying jobs and making Southern New Mexico communities safer in this district Trump won in 2024. Donald Trump’s Super PAC is spending millions against Tom Suozzi (NY-03), a bipartisan leader, because they know he won’t be easy to beat. Marcy Kaptur (OH-09) is the longest serving woman in Congress and a fighter for Northeast Ohio. Republicans couldn’t beat her in 2024, so they re-drew the congressional map in a desperate attempt to try and flip this seat. Henry Cuellar (TX-28) and Vicente Gonzalez (TX-34) have a proven record of delivering for South Texas. Across Texas and the country, a wave of Latino voters are ready to reject Republicans at the ballot box. Bill Hill (AK-AL) is a commercial fisherman, union construction worker and educator of nearly 25 years. Bill understands the economic pressures Alaskans are facing right now. He is running to make government work for hardworking families, because he is one. As a teen, Manny Rutinel (CO-08) worked at McDonalds, tutored kids and even sold plasma to help pay the bills after the bank foreclosed on his family home. Manny is running for Congress to fight for working families, create good paying jobs and fix our broken healthcare system. Will Lawrence (MI-07) is ready to serve Mid-Michiganders. He has a proven track record of protecting manufacturing jobs and leading the fight for affordable housing. He was one of the top vote getters in the primary, and has shown his campaign has the momentum, enthusiasm and organization to win this critical seat in November. Shannon Taylor (VA-01) is a career prosecutor with a 90% homicide conviction rate. In 2011, Shannon became the first Democrat in nearly 40 years and first woman ever to win the office of Henrico Commonwealth’s Attorney. She’s ready to flip Virginia’s First Congressional District blue. Wisconsinites know what hard work is, and Mitch Berman (WI-01) is a registered nurse and father who has dedicated his career to fighting for his community. Raised in a one-stoplight town, Mitch was brought up on the rural values that corrupt career politicians like his opponent Rep. Bryan Steil have long forgotten. = Thanks for your support. With your help, Democrats will take back the House in 2026. Be well, Rep. Peter,
---
We've looked at the polling in every swing state and swing race in the country. It's margin of error, either way, almost everywhere.

At this point, it's not about winning anybody over. _It's about who actually shows up._

If conservatives turn out in November, we'll win every critical battleground and lay the groundwork for victory in 2028 and beyond.

That's why Turning Point Action is focusing all our efforts on three key states: Arizona, Nevada, and New Hampshire.

**We call these states the new RED WALL.**

_Let me explain why they matter so much... _

After 2024, Charlie looked at the numbers, looked at the maps, and told our team something simple. If we lock down Arizona, Nevada, and New Hampshire, the Left's entire strategy falls apart. Their map collapses. Their path back to power disappears.

Here's why... Winning the presidency comes down to 270 electoral votes. Lose Arizona and most of the realistic paths to the White House in 2028 are gone. Lose Nevada and New Hampshire and the Left rebuilds the Blue Wall they lost in 2024.

Whoever wins in 2028 controls the 2030 Census. The Census drives redistricting. Redistricting sets the congressional map for the next ten years.

This midterm decides which way that goes.

# Is there a Hull sign in your yard?
# Show me.

|

| | | | | | Friend,
If there's a Hull for Governor sign in front of your home right now, thank you. I mean that.
Every sign in a yard tells your neighbors something a TV ad never can: someone they know and trust is ready for new leadership in Santa Fe. That kind of support is contagious, and I want the whole state to see it.
So here's my ask. Step outside, snap a photo of your yard sign, and post it on Facebook, Instagram, or X. Tag us at @GreggHullforNM on [Instagram](https://us.list-manage.com/12oz1yisSj_?e=530e36cac1&c2id=62f28c177cd28b25da81790396be4810) and [X](https://us.list-manage.com/19GKwHUSHPL?e=530e36cac1&c2id=62f28c177cd28b25da81790396be4810), or [@GreggHullforNewMexico on Facebook](https://us.list-manage.com/yDPQqquHRzg?e=530e36cac1&c2id=62f28c177cd28b25da81790396be4810) with the hashtags #GreggHullforNM #ProvenLeadership so we can share it. Get creative. Put your dog in the shot, your kids, your truck, the Sandias in the background. Show New Mexico what this movement looks like on your street.
Now, the hard truth is... we can't keep up with the demand. Requests for signs are coming in from Farmington to Hobbs, from Gallup to Clovis, and I want every one of those families to have one. A chip in of $25 puts more signs in more yards. $50 helps us reach towns we haven't covered yet. And $100 helps us blanket entire neighborhoods before Election Day on November 3rd.
Chip in now to get more Hull signs across New Mexico:

Thank you for standing with me,

The Los Angeles nonprofit backing DSA mayoral candidate Nithya Raman "Streets For All" recently unveiled its newest campaign: "Palm Trees Are A Scam."
In a recently **[released video](https://substack.com/redirect/e811549d-dc38-49a8-94a9-e35323f7fae4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) ,** they criticized the city's tens of thousands of palm trees, saying they use too much water and don't provide enough shade. They also go out of their way to mention that they are highly flammable, a touchy subject for L.A. residents who saw the Palisades fires destroy 37 square miles and kill 12 individuals in January 2025. Criticizing the palm trees seems like an attempt to shift the blame for the fires from negligent Democrat policies onto palm trees, but it tracks with the group's insistence that "climate change threatens our very existence."
"Streets For All" sounds friendly, but the policies behind its mission to start a "transportation revolution in Los Angeles" reveal why it's tied to DSA candidates like Raman.
One of the organization's primary concerns is speed enforcement, which they claim is "costly," "inefficient," and "especially detrimental to Black and Brown members of our community, who are often targeted by police." The group believes that police officers should be removed from traffic stops entirely, while the city relies on cameras that automatically issue tickets. Speeding tickets would be adjusted according to income, giving "heavily reduced" speeding tickets to those making minimum wage.

In 2024, the group's founder and CEO, Michael Schneider, co-sponsored Senate Bill **[961](https://substack.com/redirect/75b77017-563d-4c76-9403-7e257e260f33?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , introduced by Senator Scott Weiner. The bill would have required all new cars in California to install speed governors equipped with GPS trackers and cameras to limit their vehicles' maximum speed. Schneider **[argued](https://substack.com/redirect/06de8c61-88e0-47e6-ac89-f4f5a4c0e7f4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** that the speed limiters would help alleviate the city's twenty-year high of pedestrian deaths in L.A., although many critics claimed the rising number of incidents was a long-term consequence of defunding the LAPD. The bill was too radical for liberal Governor Gavin Newsom, who vetoed it, much to the dismay of "Streets For All."
The nonprofit has taken issue with Gov. Newsom several times, including in early August, 2026, when they labelled him a 'hypocrite.' When he supported measures cutting $2 billion from one of California's public transit programs, the nonprofit **[lashed out](https://substack.com/redirect/951c51a7-e8be-4a70-a9e0-3a17ad6c60d8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** at him for investing into "Big Oil and other polluters." The state of California currently has a transportation budget of about **[$30.9 billion](https://substack.com/redirect/3a84548b-8e7b-42d1-9666-16eaca3c25c2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , with the L.A. metro alone costing over **[$9 billion](https://substack.com/redirect/d216b112-f474-4864-8e5a-21e6549829f0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , meaning that Newsom's cuts accounted for just a fraction of the state's investment into transportation.

* * *

* * *
* * *
"Streets For All" has taken radical positions on other issues, such as congestion pricing. This would force drivers to pay tolls to use busy roads and freeways, especially in downtown areas. However, these tolls wouldn't apply to those making minimum wage. The explicit goal of congestion pricing is to take people off of roads and force them to use public transit. The group has asked that a majority of major streets are rebuilt with full 24x7 bus lanes by removing public traffic lanes. Further, congestion pricing would eliminate all 'free' parking on city streets. The group has called for the end of parking minimums, labelling them a "pseudoscience" and an easy way to "combat high rents."
Additionally, they have advocated for reinforcing bus lanes with concrete curbs so that they can't be used by vehicles.
"Streets For All" is trying to do everything it can to convince people to give up their cars and rely on public transportation, similar to how the Soviet Union under Khrushchev argued against private car ownership. It comes as no surprise that the group has tied itself to DSA candidates like Nithya Raman, Hugo Soto Martinez, and Eunisses Hernandez. Despite their reverence for socialist candidates, "Streets For All" still sells merchandise, including a $40 sweatshirt that says "BDSM" in large print, with "Buses Do So Much" in small print beneath it.

This would force drivers to pay tolls to use busy roads and freeways, especially in downtown areas. However, these tolls wouldn't apply to those making minimum wage. The explicit goal of congestion pricing is to take people off of roads and force them to use public transit. The group has asked that a majority of major streets are rebuilt with full 24x7 bus lanes by removing public traffic lanes. Further, congestion pricing would eliminate all 'free' parking on city streets. | | | | JoCasta Zamarripa is a lifelong Milwaukeean, a proud daughter of the city’s south side, and a dedicated public servant who’s never stopped fighting for working people. Born and raised in the very neighborhoods she now represents, JoCasta has spent her life pushing for progress that reflects the realities of everyday Wisconsinites.

[ ](https://us.list-manage.com/5r1WNlO28ge?e=8d919f2092&c2id=0bdcb6d83cbc8b2aaf05afb952b88bb7)

She made history as the first Latina and first openly bi member of both the Wisconsin State Legislature and the Milwaukee Common Council. But JoCasta’s leadership is defined by more than her historic firsts—it's grounded in results. She served ten years in the State Assembly and is now in her second term as Alderperson for Milwaukee’s 8th District, where she’s led major efforts on affordable housing, small business licensing reform, and community development.

In 2025, she was the lead sponsor of the Housing Element Plan, a key step in addressing Milwaukee’s housing crisis by expanding affordable options and preventing displacement. Her approach is practical and persistent—building coalitions, navigating political challenges, and staying rooted in the neighborhoods she serves.

Now, JoCasta is running as a Democrat for Wisconsin Secretary of State to use the platform to fight for what matters: more funding for our schools so families aren’t forced into referenda every election, real housing relief for working people, and affordable child care that lets parents breathe.

We’re already getting pummelled. It’s about to get worse.
| Please don't look away.

I just learned that crypto is dumping $30 million into defeating our campaign. Ohio is the only state they are targeting, and it’s with a historic amount in the final stretch of our race. **These attacks are imminent, and our response window is closing fast.**[Please rush a split contribution between my campaign and the Voter Protection Project to help fend off these attacks.](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/132415?t=6&akid=29064%2E878179%2EKLFMhc) | [Rush $10 »](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/132415?t=7&akid=29064%2E878179%2EKLFMhc)

There's a lot of moving pieces, but here's what I know right now:

Before this, the Republican establishment was already spending $14 million each week against us. That includes Jon Husted's super PAC, Elon Musk's contributions, Peter Thiel's dark money, and Donald Trump's multi-million dollar investment. _Every single week._

**With crypto jumping in, that weekly amount is skyrocketing.**

For reference, our campaign is currently spending about $2 million on TV ads each week.

Combined Republican spending is now at $238 million against me this cycle.

I'm never one to say the sky is falling or sound the alarm unnecessarily. But, unfortunately, this is not one of those times. **Crypto's new spending could bury us.**

They're doing it because Jon Husted is _extremely_ vulnerable and the GOP has seen this tactic work before. In my 2024 race, when crypto started spending against me and we weren't able to respond, the polls started turning in Republicans' favor. _We lost that race._

A few weeks ago, Senate Republicans put out a call for outside groups like data centers and AI to bail Husted out with enormous cash infusions in the Ohio Senate race. **And this is them answering the call.**

**We had no choice but to raise our fundraising goals so we could mount a response to these attacks from Big Tech. My team and I did the math and we need to raise $1 million so we can scale up our program _immediately_.**

[We have less than 24 hours to fend off their attacks and fundraise for our response. Right now is the single most important time for you to get involved. I cannot stress this enough – I need you to split $10 between my campaign and the Voter Protection Project right now. #### **Forward Party Endorses Diana DiZoglio for Massachusetts State Auditor**
**_Washington D.C. –_**** _September 23, 2026_** _–_ The Forward Party recently announced its endorsement of Massachusetts State Auditor Diana DiZoglio, who is running for re-election in November, continuing the party's commitment to supporting officials who fight for transparency and accountability regardless of party. DiZoglio has built her career on holding Beacon Hill accountable to the people it serves, a mission she has pursued relentlessly since taking office as the Commonwealth's chief accountability officer in 2023.

"Diana DiZoglio has shown what it looks like to actually fight for transparency instead of just talking about it. She took on entrenched interests in her own party in pursuit of an audit of the Legislature that voters overwhelmingly demanded, and she hasn't backed down since. That kind of independence and accountability to the public rather than to political insiders is exactly what Forward stands for." \- Lindsey Drath, CEO, Forward Party [_Read the full press announcement_](https://www.forwardparty.com/media/press_release/forward-party-endorses-diana-dizoglio-for-massachusetts-state-auditor/?e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_123a&n=1)

It's time to hit the pavement in Rapid City! **This Saturday**! Our affiliate partner and friend, Moving America Forward, will be canvassing to connect with independent voters. Join them and get out into your community to have real conversations about real solutions. Whether your first time canvassing or you're a seasoned veteran, all experience levels are needed! Training and materials will be provided. There will be a morning deployment from 8:30 AM to 12:00 PM and an afternoon deployment from 12:30 PM to 4:00 PM. Additionally, Moving America Forward will be hosting a multi-partner coalition dinner (5:30 PM - 8:00 PM) for participating volunteers and partner organizations, featuring special guest speaker and U.S. Senate candidate Brian Bengs. Hope to see you there! Sign up at the link above.
### [Meet the Forward Candidates 2026 - Round 2](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=UeDLqzdowGDpJNWAIB-bbDrU-YEOo41rQin1hqsEU9A&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_123a&n=3)
In Round 2 of our Meet the Forwardists series, we will be focusing on Independent Congressional candidates from many states! **Andrew Yang** will host and will be discussing the Fulcrum Strategy to change the way things are done in Congress. Sign up to attend TOMORROW's event!

*|MC_PREVIEW_TEXT|* | | |

Friend,

My husband, Colton, was a sheriff's deputy. He served his community proudly and built his life around serving others.

Then, January 6 changed everything.

Colton was swept into the federal investigation surrounding January 6. He lost his career, his freedom, and important civil rights, including his ability to vote and possess firearms. These consequences followed him long after his time behind bars, as he had figured out how to rebuild a life that had been turned upside down.

Then, on January 20, 2025, President Trump pardoned Colton and the other January 6 defendants. That was an incredible moment for us.

But here's something we learned the hard way: a pardon doesn't automatically put your life back together the way it was before.

Getting those rights restored can be a long and complicated process. Even after you've received a pardon, there can still be paperwork, records, applications, legal hurdles, and costs standing between you and the rights you once took for granted.

I've watched my husband fight to rebuild his life after losing so much, and I don't want other Americans who have earned a second chance to face that process alone.

**GOOD NEWS:** We live in a republic governed by the U.S. Constitution.

This Constitution Week, we celebrate the anniversary of the day our Founding Fathers signed that document and set in motion the greatest experiment in self-government the world has ever known.

The Constitution is supposed to protect our God-given rights from government overreach, including the right to keep and bear arms.

**BAD NEWS** : Sometimes those rights get lost, ignored, or outright disregarded.

And when that happens, somebody has to stand up and fight to restore them.

**That's why I’m excited to introduce Operation Proof Mark, Stand in the Gap Foundation’s new effort to help eligible Americans pursue restoration of their federal firearm rights.**
[Support Operation Proof Mark](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckE2KhDAUhE8Td0r-jGaRxUDjrmc7y_DyowY0CSbazO0HG-YCvXu8Kqo-6uepnxC2EJdv2L2yV9BH0TGZ5H5fcETvzgImnbWuoWTQFFPRYtlSpsHWcHnNoXHKOsFo4xUZJCYSy542q5Km53hwsxB-FH4YjWFcjIBHjKUBQZqg7jgsKSOS9LzvCOesJ5QNxs3zzGbE8ZkdVF86m2LxxwV3Z4gx3VeKnU17s6m11lwQ-0J0QnQq3p6H7yB6l-rtuH8VomtDbOvq2wUyolOGNuUdsemsu7awZwhLROzxz4SoeCspVh8rYg97heZQLr_CtoUiBsTxskPY3hD1w-0uRf8CAAD__58Ef-g)
A federal firearms prohibition doesn't automatically disappear when someone finishes their sentence. A conviction from 1994 can still prevent someone from exercising their Second Amendment rights in 2026.
* It can affect the jobs they can get.
* It can create problems for their family and their home.
* It can even prevent a father from passing a firearm down to his own children.

That's where Operation Proof Mark comes in.

Operation Proof Mark is helping eligible people build the evidence they need, obtain certified records and fingerprints, cover the costs, and coordinate with attorneys to get their applications filed properly.

And we don't charge applicants a dime.

I've seen firsthand how difficult it can be to rebuild your life after the government takes away your freedom and your rights. I've also seen how powerful a second chance can be.

Colton got his second chance. Now I want to help make sure other eligible Americans have a real opportunity to reclaim the rights they lost, too.

But that work costs money, and that's why I'm asking you to stand with me today.

name: Rep. Ilhan Omar
subject: Medical debt.
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY ILHAN FOR CONGRESS
body:
Last week I introduced a new bill that would provide a simple and much-needed protection for Americans
# [](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/35?t=1&akid=2483%2E791427%2EcTIpba)
[](https://act.ilhanomar.com/signup/em_endorse_medical_debt_bill_sep/?refcode=em260923-1-180&akid=2483%2E791427%2EcTIpba)
Friend, last week I introduced a new bill that would provide a simple and much-needed protection for Americans: banning wage garnishment for medical debt.
Just imagine suffering a major illness or injury, going into extreme debt in order to see the doctor you need, and then having a portion of your hard-earned paycheck taken from you by debt collectors before it even reaches your hands. It’s wrong, and it only makes the cycle of poverty and debt worse.
[**If you agree that we must protect working Americans from the medical debt crisis, add your name to endorse our bill today >>**](https://act.ilhanomar.com/signup/em_endorse_medical_debt_bill_sep/?source=em260923-1-180&refcode2=2483.791427.cTIpba&akid=2483%2E791427%2EcTIpba)
**[ADD YOUR NAME](https://act.ilhanomar.com/signup/em_endorse_medical_debt_bill_sep/?source=em260923-1-180&refcode2=2483.791427.cTIpba&akid=2483%2E791427%2EcTIpba)**
Let me be completely clear — **in a just system, medical debt would not exist.**
That’s why I’m an advocate for Medicare-for-All, a single-payer healthcare system that would provide each and every American with the care they need and remove the very idea of medical debt from the equation.
For too long we have accepted an unworkable status quo, where the health and well-being of Americans is treated like a profit opportunity by the private insurance industry. We get sick, they get rich.
And this is a problem that every other developed nation has solved. In fact, about 66% of all bankruptcies in America are due to medical debt — **_in most countries, that number is 0%._**
It’s time to end this unfair nonsense and deliver a sensible system that treats healthcare like any other public good, whether it’s the schools our kids go to or the roads we drive on.
[**So please: If you believe in Medicare-for-All, and if you believe we need to tackle the medical debt crisis, sign on to endorse our bill today. It’s a small step, but a necessary one that will move America in a more just and fair direction.**](https://act.ilhanomar.com/signup/em_endorse_medical_debt_bill_sep/?source=em260923-1-180&refcode2=2483.791427.cTIpba&akid=2483%2E791427%2EcTIpba)
**[ADD YOUR NAME](https://act.ilhanomar.com/signup/em_endorse_medical_debt_bill_sep/?source=em260923-1-180&refcode2=2483.791427.cTIpba&akid=2483%2E791427%2EcTIpba)**
Thank you in advance for helping me show a groundswell of support for this important legislation.
In solidarity,
Rep. Ilhan Omar

Tuesday delivered the clearest single piece of evidence yet on which of Trump's three stated Iran options is actually in play — and it wasn't the diplomatic one this newsletter flagged markets as betting on. **Verified fact:** addressing the UN General Assembly, Trump told Iran: “Will a deal be made with Iran that lets them rebuild... or do I annihilate the Islamic Republic, and do it quickly,” adding that he expected a deal to materialize “right after the election” and that his central concern remained that “Iran will never have a nuclear weapon.” Iran's delegation staged a walkout during the remarks on military operations against Iran. Oil fell further regardless — WTI down 3.19% to $89.42, Brent down 2.69% to $97.64 — while the Nasdaq closed at a fresh record on an unrelated rally in Meta shares.
| | Regime Signal 01 — The Election Timeline Just Reappeared, and It Undercuts the Diplomatic Read
---|---
**Our interpretation:** this newsletter flagged weeks ago that Trump's public framing has repeatedly tied the war's resolution to the midterm election calendar rather than to a negotiating timeline. Tuesday's “right after the election” comment is the clearest recent restatement of that link. **What remains unknown** is why markets continue pricing an imminent diplomatic resolution when the president's own words point to a deal, if it comes, arriving on a political timeline weeks or months away — not this week's General Assembly.
| | Regime Signal 02 — A Walkout Is a Harder Data Point Than Any Rhetoric
---|---
**Verified fact:** Iran's delegation walked out during Trump's remarks on military operations against Iran, a concrete diplomatic rupture rather than an ambiguous statement open to interpretation. **Our interpretation:** a formal walkout at the UN is a harder, more legible signal of diplomatic distance than any single quote from either side — and it occurred on the same day markets rallied further on hopes of exactly the kind of engagement a walkout makes less, not more, likely in the near term.
| | Regime Signal 03 — Markets and the War's Actual Trajectory Are Now Visibly Diverging
---|---
**Current classification: Markets show CONFIRMATION of de-escalation; the diplomatic record shows PRESSURE, if not regression.** Oil's continued decline and the Nasdaq's record close reflect a market pricing improving conditions; Tuesday's ultimatum and walkout are the opposite kind of evidence. This is the widest gap this newsletter has observed all month between market pricing and the underlying diplomatic record.
| | Today’s Confirmation Point
---|---
Watch for any further Trump or Pezeshkian remarks as the General Assembly continues this week, and whether markets begin to reprice once the walkout and the “right after the election” timeline are more fully absorbed.

Peter, There is a covenant at the center of military service, one as old as the republic itself. A young American raises a right hand and promises this country everything, even their own life. In return the nation swears that if the worst comes, the family left behind will want for nothing. I kissed my family goodbye before every deployment of my career because I believed that promise. This administration looked a grieving widow in the eye and broke that promise over wordplay. I struggle to think of anything lower. [**Send a combat veteran to Congress who will end this disrespect to the families of our fallen.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqs6gc2C5hUDUAX_oNaSPVDobFeqfVfzIW2x4J26hzyt88MYO7P3oH_gDdBcq7FnI4b1QqrM1szBuTH1U55AjYgWLughSKxY0WCB8n4-flgeKhbhMgIuuOBnFwdXM-6Zj-sZkSoVk-h6AoJ_Ay7WjrJruvHBrR7cj6tjOQORiqO8MegKGMmIJXIe3W0PCHvmwa562vNBoi1APPEpK4pG7ZsujQQmmkPcRGxS9CG7Jw2pHgXERCoSHbB_RhbYwBUWnL50rOpU3wPL0QicauZu22ra3lr4ZCVhOcoFtCfEaAcCFIbnjOo0xmOxLZRMWo0oPoVRsudG9jpLAPRG1fO_ISyEOKrLjOocSvgQ6nklchbuUFGl1DUbhDQqCfX6daKnEra9yUGkrv0D94WVT5G5LFis0dJwAGlZY6HkOKKYEJkU8x--XapM4VCg2lCAlLd_F78/4ua/MAYib7rOSvOkTEwhNT-JAQ/h1/h001.sotjtIJUspTYnJe17SiwZ3KJuWgVh3v5-n3da7DCVV8) Major Alex Klinner was 33 when his refueling aircraft went down in western Iraq supporting strikes on Iran, one of six crew members lost. His widow Libby is raising their three children alone. **_She was told she was ineligible for benefits because Congress never formally declared war._** Not only has she lost her husband, she had to fight the government for straight answers while planning his funeral. Officials later admitted feeding her inaccurate information. No Gold Star family should have to become an expert in government language to learn what they are owed. And now the Pentagon is going even further in its disgrace, intentionally hiding our war dead from the record. [**If our covenant with the men and women who serve still means something to you, help us put a combat veteran in Congress who will defend it.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqs6gc2C5hUDUAX_oNaSPVDobFeqfVfzIW2x4J26hzyt88MYO7P3oH_gDdBcq7FnI4b1QqrM1szBuTH1U55AjYgWAng0l85KIzlH58jCki19afjy9IrI6kckCos3irFOjOmqRPmhSctTdDGXOtSfFUAqZ9ziZtPcrdVdOQxIUSJyXR4qQK3-5MCb9i6v4_HKPvfB8UAZDsRAciKYZY3ub3G6DBSTYEWUTbxQ75ZcY3OxrStlso-2fCIMRXysqTNY645W2RLSD6V4v0PoaugvNtF6UL3WQFea-ECYR58ils_PBelPDOzyZjd8rI---unB0aLYQhuZb7WU4afP6oXm3JafOr9EhCJKTaMz-0gXE_JERXmZRAu5VxUbd2aCXM_ifSr7vbIxXgiIfpAcxFoL9vY0tXO2o5Cgce0D7E5oi-vH7TiVqL87eYT6gviDXZOkiYM/4ua/MAYib7rOSvOkTEwhNT-JAQ/h2/h001.W2DAe7fejj8-DRaqbRifl_RPmnJHw1eMz8fIg3ZkUyQ) I served as a Master Air Attack Plans Chief at the Combined Air Operations Center in Qatar, helping run the daily air war over Iraq and Afghanistan. Every serious military planner understood what escalation with Iran meant. We had Iran contained and sanctioned, the one strategic call America got right after two decades of conflict in that global theater. This administration threw it away and tripped us into attrition with no exit. **And through it all, their corruption and incompetence have treated our troops as an afterthought, undefended on their bases, uncounted in death, and unsupported in grief.** Congress holds the power to end this. Three times this year the House has voted to halt these unauthorized hostilities, most recently last week, when a record 7 Republicans found the spine to cross over. **Keith Self refused every single time. ** A retired lieutenant colonel had three chances to vote against the war that is killing our troops and shortchanging their widows, and three times he chose Trump over them. [**The full accounting of this war is coming, and a reckoning rides with it. clean_body: And still Keith Self stands by this illegal war. | | Peter, There is a covenant at the center of military service, one as old as the republic itself. A young American raises a right hand and promises this country everything, even their own life. In return the nation swears that if the worst comes, the family left behind will want for nothing. I kissed my family goodbye before every deployment of my career because I believed that promise. This administration looked a grieving widow in the eye and broke that promise over wordplay. I struggle to think of anything lower. Major Alex Klinner was 33 when his refueling aircraft went down in western Iraq supporting strikes on Iran, one of six crew members lost. His widow Libby is raising their three children alone. She was told she was ineligible for benefits because Congress never formally declared war. Not only has she lost her husband, she had to fight the government for straight answers while planning his funeral. Officials later admitted feeding her inaccurate information. No Gold Star family should have to become an expert in government language to learn what they are owed. And now the Pentagon is going even further in its disgrace, intentionally hiding our war dead from the record. I served as a Master Air Attack Plans Chief at the Combined Air Operations Center in Qatar, helping run the daily air war over Iraq and Afghanistan. Every serious military planner understood what escalation with Iran meant. We had Iran contained and sanctioned, the one strategic call America got right after two decades of conflict in that global theater. This administration threw it away and tripped us into attrition with no exit. And through it all, their corruption and incompetence have treated our troops as an afterthought, undefended on their bases, uncounted in death, and unsupported in grief. Congress holds the power to end this. Three times this year the House has voted to halt these unauthorized hostilities, most recently last week, when a record 7 Republicans found the spine to cross over. Keith Self refused every single time. A retired lieutenant colonel had three chances to vote against the war that is killing our troops and shortchanging their widows, and three times he chose Trump over them. name: Molly Gray
subject: From the Backroads: Join us this Saturday!
body:
Dear Peter, Last week, I had the opportunity to join members of [Rural Vermont Rising](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139814462/648592119/-2074214895?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MDg5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwMDAyNTM4OS04NWI3LWYxMTEtYTZhOS0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=q62Hh2eIeAZD_Y0vwrdFWvbDKgmQj6c3vgj1Hkg9GWM=&emci=a38aa5c6-83b7-f111-a6a9-0022482a933b&emdi=00025389-85b7-f111-a6a9-0022482a933b&ceid=43402276), and others for[ a conversation at the Tunbridge World’s Fair](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139814463/648592120/1864362931?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MDg5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwMDAyNTM4OS04NWI3LWYxMTEtYTZhOS0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=q62Hh2eIeAZD_Y0vwrdFWvbDKgmQj6c3vgj1Hkg9GWM=&emci=a38aa5c6-83b7-f111-a6a9-0022482a933b&emdi=00025389-85b7-f111-a6a9-0022482a933b&ceid=43402276) about working lands, land use, and the future of rural Vermont. It was a thoughtful conversation about the experiences of farmers, landowners, and rural communities and about the importance of making sure everyone has a seat at the table in Montpelier and in state policymaking. That conversation is continuing. Yesterday, I launched “**From the Backroads: Conversations on Working Lands, Land Use and Vermont’s Future** ,” a series of gatherings where I hope to hear directly from Vermont farmers, sugarers, loggers, landowners, families, and so many others. I want to hear from you. I want to hear your experiences, concerns, and ideas. The first gathering will be this Saturday in Fairfield, and I hope you’ll join us: **From the Backroads:**_Conversations on Working Lands, Land Use and Vermont’s Future_
**Saturday, September 26, 2026
10:00–11:00 a.m.**
Heart and Soil Farm
Fairfield, Vermont
**[RSVP here](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139814464/648592122/-1442509982?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MDg5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwMDAyNTM4OS04NWI3LWYxMTEtYTZhOS0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=q62Hh2eIeAZD_Y0vwrdFWvbDKgmQj6c3vgj1Hkg9GWM=)** **[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139814465/648592124/-1442509982?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MDg5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwMDAyNTM4OS04NWI3LWYxMTEtYTZhOS0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=q62Hh2eIeAZD_Y0vwrdFWvbDKgmQj6c3vgj1Hkg9GWM=)** We’ll talk about working lands, land use, agriculture, and what changes to legislative policy (and process) could help rural communities and farms remain viable, and ensure voices are heard. As we gear up for these conversations, we’ll be considering some of the policy priorities put forward in the [Grow What's Good Here](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139814466/648592126/-1257994077?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MDg5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwMDAyNTM4OS04NWI3LWYxMTEtYTZhOS0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=q62Hh2eIeAZD_Y0vwrdFWvbDKgmQj6c3vgj1Hkg9GWM=&emci=a38aa5c6-83b7-f111-a6a9-0022482a933b&emdi=00025389-85b7-f111-a6a9-0022482a933b&ceid=43402276) platform. Finally, these conversations are aimed at positive, civil, non-partisan discourse, focused on idea generation. All are welcome! **To RSVP,[click here](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139814467/648592128/-1442509982?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MDg5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwMDAyNTM4OS04NWI3LWYxMTEtYTZhOS0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=q62Hh2eIeAZD_Y0vwrdFWvbDKgmQj6c3vgj1Hkg9GWM=) **or email Erin at _erin@mollyforvt.com._ If you have feedback, ideas, concerns, or questions but can’t make Saturday’s gathering, please reach out at info@mollyforvt.com. I want to hear from you. I hope to see you on Saturday! _Molly Gray_

Trump's war with Iran isn't just costing lives and driving up gas prices. It's draining the actual weapons America needs to deter a far more dangerous conflict — with China. Here's what I laid out. The United States has reportedly burned through almost half of its global supply of Tomahawk cruise missiles. We've used "virtually all" of our Army Tactical Missile Systems and Precision Strike Missiles. Patriot missile stockpiles are down by two-thirds. THAAD interceptors are down by half. Defense planners call this "magazine depth" — and ours is disappearing faster than we can rebuild it. **Why does that matter beyond Iran?** Because America's entire strategy for preventing war with China depends on Beijing believing that aggression will fail. That deterrence only works if our military capability, our alliances, and our resolve are visibly intact. Every missile we burn through in an open-ended, strategy-free war with Iran is a missile we don't have if a real crisis erupts in the Pacific. I made the case plainly: We are sliding toward a war we are not prepared for, while distracted by one we never needed to fight this way. Here's the thing, though. Writing the op-ed matters. Getting the argument right matters. But none of it changes anything by itself. What actually changes this is electing Democrats who will demand accountability, follow through on real oversight, and have the backbone to stand up to reckless, strategy-free warmongering — not just write about it, but do something about it in Washington. That's exactly why I built Equal Opportunity Now. We need leaders in office who understand that real strength means knowing when to stop, not just how to escalate. **[Writing about the danger isn't enough — we need people in power who'll act on it. $25 or $50, right now.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139814810/648593276/1090555623?amount=25&refcode=260923_hillopedrs&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDUvMS83MzE2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3N2IyNzdmYi04NmI3LWYxMTEtYTZhOS0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=dutjtlp_tkWEoaFfa_aF72h8DC-aj4BWsp7Yl4sWPMg=)**

| | Hi friend, After 2016, I made a promise to myself: I don’t want to wake up the morning after Election Day ever again wishing that I had done more. No more wishing I had knocked more doors, raised more money, or done more to support quality candidates up and down the ballot. I’m sure many of you remember waking up nearly 10 years ago with that same feeling. That feeling is why I raised my hand to run for the Maryland Senate before the age of 30. It’s why I ran for Congress. And it’s why I’m always giving our community everything that I’ve got. My mentor and friend, Senator Barbara Mikulski, has a saying: “We cannot always guarantee an outcome, but we can guarantee an effort.” Those words have carried me through some of the tougher days in Washington. name: Jeff Bridges
subject: Weiser, walking, and wine on the Western Slope
body:
We started in the best way possible, with a canvass launch and hearing from voters about what’s making it harder to earn a good life in Colorado.

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/b97eb25dffb4/get-more-smarter-on-colorados-budget-10378993?e=b48bb2b4f4)
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/19XfulZygSJ?e=b48bb2b4f4&c2id=bbe572662fdb5fed2d0855c1bcb00da8)
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Hi there,
Saturday started with door knocking in Grand Junction and ended with dinner in Montrose. In between we met with local small business owners, had a debate, and of course lots of driving.
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/11EFrJoJ6Y6?e=b48bb2b4f4&c2id=bbe572662fdb5fed2d0855c1bcb00da8)
| |
We started in the best way possible, with a canvass launch to knock doors and hear directly from voters about what’s making it harder to earn a good life in Colorado.
We had pretty good company! My friend and our next governor Phil Weiser joined us for the morning.

From there, we headed to Club 20 for a debate with my opponent, Kevin Grantham. Club 20 represents Colorado's 22 western counties, and I've hoped for a chance to debate on their stage for more than a decade.
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/iWdvs5Gdep4?e=b48bb2b4f4&c2id=bbe572662fdb5fed2d0855c1bcb00da8)
| | Kevin and I actually agree that Colorado has gotten too expensive. We also really respect each other, and it was a very cordial debate.
Where we disagree, pretty dramatically, is on what the Treasurer should do about our cost of living crisis.
Colorado's Treasurer manages billions of dollars on behalf of Colorado. I think anyone holding public office right now should pull every lever they have to lower the cost of living.
**For the Treasurer, that means putting more Colorado dollars to work here in Colorado.**
Housing working people can actually afford. Renewable energy to lower bills and fight global warming. Good-paying jobs across our state. All while protecting taxpayer dollars and earning a good return.
Kevin has a different vision for the office. "Less is more."
That’s what elections are for, and I'm grateful to Club 20 for offering us the chance to share those differences together on stage.
---
| | | | | | | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/14Y7rvxtLNX?e=b48bb2b4f4&c2id=bbe572662fdb5fed2d0855c1bcb00da8)
| | After the debate, I headed south toward Montrose, with a stop in Delta County to visit the team at Aquila Wineries in the North Fork Valley.
This is one of my favorite parts of traveling the state.
Aquila is building a business around something distinctly Colorado. Local agriculture, local craftsmanship, and a landscape you simply can’t recreate anywhere else.
And delicious wine.
When we talk about investing Colorado dollars in Colorado, this is part of what I mean. Strong local economies don’t appear by accident. They grow because people take risks, build businesses, create jobs, and invest in the places they call home.
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/CcVakJlsJ6n?e=b48bb2b4f4&c2id=bbe572662fdb5fed2d0855c1bcb00da8)
| | My last stop was the Montrose County Blue Tsunami dinner.
I've been to Democratic dinners in counties many times the size of Montrose with smaller crowds and a lot less energy. This room was packed.
Keep an eye on Montrose. Something is happening there.
Whether I’m knocking doors, debating the role of the Treasurer, visiting a local business, or talking with a packed room in Montrose, I keep hearing the same basic question:
**How do we make it a little easier to earn a good life in Colorado?**
For me, the answer's in the Treasurer's office. Still many more miles ahead before we get there. Thanks for being part of the journey.
---
| | Talk soon,
---
| | P.S. The peach cobbler at the Club 20 steak fry... chef's kiss. And little known fact: every member of the Mesa University board gets to design a cocktail for the restaurant at the Maverick Hotel!
---

A free press exists so journalists can question powerful people, investigate the government, and report things those in power may not want reported. Presidents should not be able to turn White House press credentials into rewards for favorable coverage. subject: My resources are running low, and the fight isn't over
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Friends of Mike Lee, Inc
body:
This is the most important fundraising deadline of the quarter.
This is the most important fundraising deadline of the quarter.
| | United States Senate MIKE LEE
---

Friend,
I'll be blunt with you. I am in the fight of my life to pass the SAVE America Act -- a bill that says only U.S. citizens can vote in U.S. elections. Full stop. I've been on the Senate floor. I've made the case. I've pushed and pushed and pushed. And I am not done pushing.
|
---
But here's the truth: fighting costs money.

---
It costs money to reach voters like you. It costs money to keep the pressure on. It costs money to make sure the American people know what's at stake -- and who is standing in the way.
| Right now, my end-of-quarter deadline is days away.
---
Every quarter, my campaign has to report exactly how much money we raised and how much we have left to fight with. When those numbers are strong, it sends a message: Mike Lee has the backing of the American people, and he's not going anywhere. When those numbers are weak? It sends the opposite message. Fellow Conservative: As we race toward the midterm elections, there are two things Americans must know. **1) U.S. Senate races are _NATIONAL_ elections that impact ALL AMERICANS regardless of where you live.** **2) Electing strong _CONSERVATIVES_ is what matters, because another spineless Republican majority will not save our country.** Let's break these down... First, we often hear people say they don't really care about elections outside their home state. They can't vote for the candidates, so why bother? The reason is simple: _U.S. Senators make national policies that impact the lives of ALL Americans._ So while you may not be able to vote for them, their votes in Washington affect you and your family. **This is why conservatives in all 50 states must use their Constitutionally protected freedom of speech to influence the outcomes of Senate races around the country.** But if the entire Senate map is important to every American, which candidates matter most? The answer: _Conservatives_. Notice that it's not Republicans because many Republicans will not fight for our priorities when it matters. We've all painfully watched the current Senate Republican majority squander its mandate and fail to pass even the most popular policies like voter ID. Meanwhile, it has worked with the Democrats to spend so much that our national debt now exceeds $40 trillion. **The bottom line is that electing more moderate, pro-establishment Republicans is not worth our time and money.** That's why the Senate Conservatives Fund has selected eight conservative candidates across the nation who deserve our votes _AND_ our financial support.

Hey folks,
This one is wild. We're digging into new reporting about Sen. Susan Collins, an FBI bribery inquiry that investigators reportedly sought to open, and the questions surrounding a defense contractor, political donations, and millions of dollars in federal contracts.
And the timing could hardly be more consequential. Maine has a major Senate race underway, Democrats are already seizing on the reporting, and this story raises much bigger questions about money, power, accountability, and trust in government.
* [**00:01:49**] I break down the timeline at the center of the ProPublica reporting--from an $8 million Navy contract to a $150,000 contribution to a pro-Collins super PAC.
* [**00:04:26**] The episode gets into some of the most striking details reported in the story, including communications surrounding the donation and Collins' office later supporting millions of dollars in additional projects.
* [**00:06:12**] Democratic Senate candidate Troy Jackson responds to the reporting and calls for answers about Collins' dealings with the contractor and donor.
* [**00:08:29**] Matt Dunlap talks about why allegations involving public money can do lasting damage to people's trust in government--and shares a very different story involving a $36 reimbursement check.
* [**00:10:09**] I zoom out to the political stakes: the Maine Senate contest, changing race ratings elsewhere around the country, and the questions Republican candidates could face as this story develops.

There's a lot here, and these allegations deserve to be taken seriously while the facts and legal process play out. But the bigger questions about political donations, government contracts, and public trust aren't going away. Our lead in Kansas is growing. **An independent poll shows me leading Sen. Roger Marshall — this time by TWO points (45% to 43%)!**
This is proof that our message is resonating with voters and a true testament to the power of the grassroots movement we’ve built. _Thank you to everyone who has helped us get to this point._

subject: Taxpayer-Funded Health Care Programs Hit With $17.5 Billion in Fraud in One Year
body:
Fraud in taxpayer-funded health care programs like Medicare and
Medicaid is so pervasive that the government identified a breathtaking
$17.5 billion in scams in just one year, according to an analysis
conducted by the U.S. Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement
Network (FinCEN), the agency bureau charged with safeguarding the
nation’s financial system form illicit activity, money laundering
and the financing of terrorism.

[alt_text]

[*****]
September 23, 2026

[article-image]
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=85577&L=38708&F=T&&hash=0cfc6f06bdffc9e23ac651c08f58e633fdd378889fef8a4393a5831e00a1ba88]

Fraud in taxpayer-funded health care programs like Medicare and
Medicaid is so pervasive that the government identified a breathtaking
$17.5 billion in scams in just one year, according to an analysis
conducted by the U.S. Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement
Network (FinCEN), the agency bureau charged with safeguarding the
nation’s financial system form illicit activity, money laundering
and the financing of terrorism. The crimes occurred in all 50 states,
as well as Washington D.C, and U.S. territories including Guam, Puerto
Rico and the Virgin Islands. A lengthy report
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=85577&L=38709&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZmluY2VuLmdvdi9zeXN0ZW0vZmlsZXMvMjAyNi0wOS9GVEEtSGVhbHRoLUNhcmUtRnJhdWQucGRmP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249Y29ycnVwdGlvbitjaHJvbmljbGVzJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnMmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9Q01qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNE&hash=763dae34f471a73f2e1b2bb09da52f2f1d2144fbf08b5a6c2a8765debe0bf8b1]
made public this month identifies the largest number of offenders in
California (3,141), followed by Florida (1,378), New York (989) and
Minnesota (946) with some of the scams involving criminal networks
connected to foreign entities.

# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
When you look at what Greg Abbott has done as Governor of Texas, none of it makes sense until you follow the money.
Letting property taxes increase 85% during his time as governor doesn't make sense. Starving our public schools to force through private school vouchers doesn’t make sense. Skyrocketing electricity bills and handing our grid over to massive data centers _definitely_ doesn’t make sense.
**None of it makes sense for hardworking, everyday Texans.**
It only makes sense when you see who is profiting from it. Greg Abbott and his wealthy donors.
This is what the fight in Texas is all about, Peter. Every single day, people in this state work harder and get less. Meanwhile, about 15 billionaires at the top are trying to run the show, and we’re left paying more for quite literally — everything.
All because politicians like Greg Abbott have enabled it.
This November, we have a chance to take back Texas and elect a leader who answers to the people, not out-of-touch billionaires.
