It is election season, and you are probably wondering why you are seeing certain advertisements, receiving certain mailers and getting certain text messages while your neighbor is seeing something completely different.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/56ed464b-a2d9-4679-8313-09cfa303173f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
A Democratic candidate may show up at your door. Republican Senate advertisements may follow you around social media. You may receive five pieces of campaign mail while your neighbor receives only one, or none at all.
That is not random.
Political campaigns have ways of estimating who you are, how likely you are to vote and how you might vote. They assign voters different scores based primarily on two variables: support and turnout. Those scores are then combined with voter records, donation history, consumer data and whatever other concoction of information the campaigns and their data brokers put into their algorithms.
Out comes a score telling campaigns how good of a Democrat or Republican they think you are, how likely you are to vote, how they might be able to use you and whether you are worth targeting at all.
Let's get into what that actually means.
* * *
## The Tools Used to Score You
I ran as a Democrat and have been involved in Democratic campaigns and political circles, so I know more about the Democratic side than the Republican side.
For Democrats, the primary system is NGP VAN's VoteBuilder. Other political-data companies exist, including nonpartisan vendors such as[ L2 that sell voter data to ](https://substack.com/redirect/341e2724-6670-47d8-83c0-3d35bf2ec7c3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)Democrats, Republicans and independent campaigns.
The basic information starts with voter-registration records.
Campaigns cannot see whom you voted for. Your ballot is private. But they can see whether you showed up.
They can see whether you voted in a Democratic or Republican primary. They can see whether you participated in a general election, special election or ballot-issue election. They can see how consistently you vote and which elections you skip.
They can also see your publicly reported campaign contributions. Federal contributions are disclosed through the Federal Election Commission, while Ohio state and local contributions are reported through the state's campaign-finance system. Campaigns can see which candidates or political committees received your money, how much you gave, how often you donated and whether your contributions generally went to Democrats or Republicans.
That information becomes the foundation of your score.
Campaigns and political-data companies can then combine it with modeled information and commercially available consumer data. VoteBuilder provides campaigns with voter-file information, score modeling and consumer data designed to help them target the people they want to reach.
The exact formula is not public. Campaigns are not handing voters a recipe showing exactly which data points are used or how heavily each one is weighted.
Consumer data could include assumptions drawn from the stores where people shop, the media they consume and the demographic categories into which data brokers place them.
Are you more likely to shop at Aldi, Costco or Tractor Supply?
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d4becacd-1e07-46fb-b6d7-3658bf03ab13?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
What categories of shows do you watch on YouTube, Netflix or other platforms?
What does your neighborhood, income, age or consumer profile suggest about you?
These are examples of the kinds of categories consumer models could use. I am not claiming that VoteBuilder contains your raw Netflix history, a list of every YouTube video you have watched or an itemized receipt from Tractor Supply.
I am saying that data companies use consumer patterns, interest categories, demographic information and other commercially available data to build models about people.
Buying something at Tractor Supply does not automatically make you a Republican, and shopping at Aldi does not make you a Democrat. But these systems can take enormous amounts of information, run it through algorithms and use the result to estimate what kind of voter you are.
These are assumptions. Sometimes they are right. Sometimes they are wrong. But campaigns make real decisions and spend real money based on them.
* * *
## How Campaigns Categorize You
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/99d09b71-e9e5-4e9b-a370-8b58f6718e0f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
A voter with a Democratic-support score of 90 to 100 would generally be considered a strong Democratic voter.
If that person also has a high turnout score, a Democratic campaign may not spend much money persuading them. The campaign already believes that person supports Democrats and will show up. It might ask for a donation, recruit the person as a volunteer or send a basic reminder, but there is little reason to waste money repeatedly convincing someone who is already voting for you.
If someone has high Democratic support but low turnout, that person becomes a get-out-the-vote target.
That is when the mailers, calls and text messages start saying, "This is the most important election of our lifetime." The campaign believes the person supports Democrats, but it is not confident that the person will actually vote.
Someone scoring between roughly 75 and 90 may still lean Democratic, but there may be something in the data suggesting that the person does not always support the party or may sit out an election.
Maybe there is an inkling of independence or free thinking. Maybe that person has not completely drunk the Kool-Aid. Depending on the turnout and support scores, that voter may become a persuasion target.
The campaign wants to convince that person that its candidate is the right choice and then make sure the person votes.
Someone around 50 or 60 could fall closer to the middle. That voter might be worth persuading, or the campaign might decide the score is too low and leave the person alone. If the voter has a high turnout score, both parties may fight for that vote.
A Democratic-support score of 20 would suggest someone who is probably a strong Republican. Democratic campaigns may leave that person alone while Republicans treat the same person as a reliable supporter.
These numbers are examples, not universal cutoffs. Each campaign decides where it draws the lines based on its race, district, budget and strategy.
But the basic system remains the same.
Campaigns want to know whether you support them, whether you vote, whether you donate, whether you volunteer and whether you can be persuaded. If your scores do not fit their campaign goals, they may completely ignore you.
* * *
## Then the Political Machine Starts Turning
Once campaigns have this information, the machine starts turning and the gears start running.

They call the printers. They call the advertising agencies. They call the media creators, consultants, designers, texting companies and canvassing operations. They begin creating literature, advertisements, videos, text messages and door-knocking lists designed around the voters they want to reach.
This is why you can open your mailbox and see completely different political advertisements than your neighbor.
Your social media feed may be filled with advertisements your relatives have never seen. One voter may receive messages about abortion. Another may receive messages about taxes. Another may receive messages about guns, immigration, crime or healthcare.
The campaign is not communicating one message to everybody. It is dividing voters into groups and telling each group what the campaign believes will move them.
This data is insanely valuable to a political campaign.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9b3e92dc-b5e9-40ef-bd30-2b5f26a16cc1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Without it, a campaign is throwing money into the air and hoping the right people see its message. With it, the campaign can decide which voters should receive mail, which doors should be knocked, which phones should be called and which people are not worth the campaign's time or money. **All this is called targeting.**
Campaigns also feed information back into these systems.
If a canvasser knocks on your door and you say you support a candidate, oppose a candidate, need more information, have moved or do not want to be contacted again, that response can be entered into the system. The same thing can happen when you answer a campaign phone call, complete a survey or respond to a text message.
That contact information can improve the voter file and help future Democratic campaigns make decisions about you.
That brings us to the political parties and the control they have over this information.
* * *
## In Ohio, It Is Pay to Play
NGP VAN licenses VoteBuilder access through Democratic Party organizations. In Ohio, the Ohio Democratic Party controls access to the Democratic voter file.
The party works with legislative caucuses and other Democratic organizations to determine how that access is distributed. It also charges candidates directly based on the office they are seeking.
For the 2023-2024 election cycle, a Democratic candidate for the United States House paid **$5,000 per year for VoteBuilder access.**
A State Senate candidate who did not receive free access through the legislative caucus paid $300.
A State House candidate who did not receive caucus access **paid $150.**
City and county council candidates paid between **$50 and $950** , depending on the number of registered voters in the district.
County Democratic parties received access at no cost, **but they were not permitted to extend that access to candidates who had not purchased their own campaign access.**
Countywide and municipal candidates could purchase access regardless of whether they had received the party's endorsement, provided they were self-identified Democrats in good standing.
For Ohio House and Senate races, the legislative caucuses could provide free access to incumbents and Democratic candidates whose campaigns they supported. Candidates who did not receive that support could still purchase access, but they had to pay for it themselves.
Sometimes a State House or Senate candidate did not personally have to pay because the legislative caucus supported the campaign and provided access at no cost. Candidates who did not receive that support had to purchase it.
Long story short, it is pay to play.
That surprises a lot of candidates when they begin running for office. They think they are joining a political party and will have access to the basic information necessary to contact Democratic voters. Then they learn that the voter file is a product, and the party controls the door.
A campaign can also hire a consultant to request and manage VoteBuilder access on its behalf. But the access still belongs to the campaign committee, is limited to the geography of that campaign and remains governed by the Ohio Democratic Party's user agreements.
The campaign is still paying someone.
You either pay the party, receive free access because a legislative caucus is supporting you or hire consultants to help manage the system for your campaign.
One way or another, access costs money or depends on the people controlling the system.
* * *
## It Is Also a Gatekeeping Tool
This is where the problem becomes larger than a software fee.
The Ohio Democratic Party and its staff reserve the right to grant, deny or terminate VoteBuilder access to any candidate or organization at their discretion.
**Read that again.**
The Ohio Democratic Party reserves the right to decide who receives access, who is denied access and whose access can be terminated.
A political party controlling an enormously valuable voter database can make life easier for the candidates it supports and more difficult for the candidates it does not.
The party can provide free access to supported legislative candidates. It can require other candidates to purchase access. It can deny access. It can terminate access.
That creates an obvious mechanism for compliance.
Do what the party wants, stay within its preferred messages and remain in the good graces of the people controlling the system. Otherwise, you may find yourself running without the same voter data, campaign-contact history and political infrastructure available to the party's preferred candidates.
The ability to gatekeep is built directly into the structure.
This is one of the ways political parties maintain control over candidates. It is not always through some dramatic public threat. Sometimes it is through access to the basic tools a candidate needs to run a competitive campaign.
You can run without the party's system. This is America. Private companies such as L2 will sell voter data, and some private vendors may have stronger data in certain categories.
But it is different data, and candidates must understand how to navigate and use it independently. They may not have access to the same years of Democratic campaign contacts, volunteer information, survey responses and party-specific models accumulated inside VoteBuilder.
So yes, alternatives exist. But pretending there is no advantage to receiving the party's data is ridiculous.

We should note: VoteBuilder access is not governed by one national Democratic Party rule.

NGP VAN says access is granted through each individual state Democratic Party, which means the rules vary considerably from state to state.

Delaware explicitly allows any Democratic candidate with an active campaign committee to purchase access, regardless of endorsement, and says that access will not be revoked or altered after an endorsement is made.

Kansas provides access to filed Democratic candidates at no direct charge, including legislative and congressional candidates, but still reserves the discretion to grant, deny or terminate access.

Other state parties have historically restricted access for certain primary challengers or required particular endorsements. **In other words, whether VoteBuilder is treated as a neutral resource available to every Democratic candidate or as a party-controlled resource with restrictions depends heavily on the rules and access policies adopted by each state party.**
* * *
## Wait Until We Talk About Political Mail
VoteBuilder is only part of this system.
Wait until we get into the mailing services available through the Democratic Party, how campaigns get political mail sent so cheaply and how much more candidates may pay if they do not run their mail through the established party infrastructure and play by their rules.
There are ways to work around that too, but that is a discussion for another time.
The larger point is that political campaigns are not simply candidates printing signs and asking people for votes. There is an entire political industry behind them, including data companies, consultants, printers, advertising agencies, mailing operations and party-controlled systems.
Access to that machinery costs money, and the people controlling it can decide who receives help and who does not.
* * *
## In Summary: Why You Receive the Political Ads You Receive
If you have ever wondered why you receive certain campaign mailers, advertisements or text messages while other people receive something completely different, this is why.
Campaigns have access to scoring systems that estimate what kind of Democrat or Republican you are.
They look at whether you vote, which elections you participate in, whether you donate, whom you donate to and what consumer or demographic patterns might provide an inkling of how you think.
They then decide whether you are a supporter, a turnout target, a persuasion target, a donor, a potential volunteer, a reliable opponent or someone who is not worth contacting at all.
So when the mail starts arriving, save it.
Send me pictures of the campaign literature you receive. Compare it with what your neighbors, relatives and friends are receiving. I think it will be extremely interesting to see how differently campaigns speak to different groups of voters. Might tell you a bit about who you are and how you are perceived by campaigns and candidates.
## **Stay Angry.**
P.S. The last time I checked, my Democratic-support score was 71. Take that for what you will.

So yes, alternatives exist. But pretending there is no advantage to receiving the party's data is ridiculous. We should note: VoteBuilder access is not governed by one national Democratic Party rule. NGP VAN says access is granted through each individual state Democratic Party, which means the rules vary considerably from state to state. Delaware explicitly allows any Democratic candidate with an active campaign committee to purchase access, regardless of endorsement, and says that access will not be revoked or altered after an endorsement is made. Kansas provides access to filed Democratic candidates at no direct charge, including legislative and congressional candidates, but still reserves the discretion to grant, deny or terminate access. Other state parties have historically restricted access for certain primary challengers or required particular endorsements. In other words, whether VoteBuilder is treated as a neutral resource available to every Democratic candidate or as a party-controlled resource with restrictions depends heavily on the rules and access policies adopted by each state party. Wait Until We Talk About Political Mail VoteBuilder is only part of this system. Wait until we get into the mailing services available through the Democratic Party, how campaigns get political mail sent so cheaply and how much more candidates may pay if they do not run their mail through the established party infrastructure and play by their rules. There are ways to work around that too, but that is a discussion for another time. The larger point is that political campaigns are not simply candidates printing signs and asking people for votes. There is an entire political industry behind them, including data companies, consultants, printers, advertising agencies, mailing operations and party-controlled systems. Access to that machinery costs money, and the people controlling it can decide who receives help and who does not. In Summary: Why You Receive the Political Ads You Receive If you have ever wondered why you receive certain campaign mailers, advertisements or text messages while other people receive something completely different, this is why. Campaigns have access to scoring systems that estimate what kind of Democrat or Republican you are. They look at whether you vote, which elections you participate in, whether you donate, whom you donate to and what consumer or demographic patterns might provide an inkling of how you think. They then decide whether you are a supporter, a turnout target, a persuasion target, a donor, a potential volunteer, a reliable opponent or someone who is not worth contacting at all. So when the mail starts arriving, save it. Send me pictures of the campaign literature you receive. Compare it with what your neighbors, relatives and friends are receiving. I think it will be extremely interesting to see how differently campaigns speak to different groups of voters. Might tell you a bit about who you are and how you are perceived by campaigns and candidates. Stay Angry. P.S. The last time I checked, my Democratic-support score was 71. Yesterday, I stood outside Houston ISD headquarters alongside parents, and educators to talk about something that should concern every Texas parent: **artificial intelligence is rapidly taking over our neighborhood schools.**
And once again, Greg Abbott and TEA Commissioner, Mike Morath, are at the center of a decision that does nothing to benefit our kids, but definitely pleases the billionaire donor class. Greg Abbott has received millions of dollars from MacKenzie Price, who owns and operates AI schools. These are schools where teachers are replaced by education guides, where kids spend hours in front of screens, and that is their education. This model threatens the development of our kids and attempts to replace teachers with robots.
Human connection is at the heart of most of our educational journeys. Hopefully, like me, you all can remember that one special teacher who saw something in you and made you believe in yourself. For me that was my middle school history teacher.
Abbott's AI slop could never replace the critical role of having actual qualified teachers in front of the classroom. Already we are seeing curriculum that's been created by AI be totally inaccurate for both math and social studies.
That's especially concerning in Houston, because the people making these decisions weren't chosen by Houston voters. Greg Abbott's Education Commissioner, Mike Morath, replaced HISD's elected school board with a state-appointed board of managers.
**When I am governor, I will give Houston ISD back to the people of Houston, so that there can be accountability again. Accountability from the parents, and accountability from the community. Because when there is accountability, this kind of nonsense doesn 't happen.**
Parents deserve a say in decisions about their children's education. Teachers deserve a seat at the table when decisions are made about their classrooms. And communities deserve accountability from the people spending their tax dollars.
If the goal is to see students succeed, we have to get back to the basics. That means having certified teachers at the front of the classroom and a fully funded neighborhood public school system. Abbott's $1 billion voucher scam is stealing money from our schools, and I'm running to put a stop to it.
Abbott and Morath plan to convert 100 schools to their AI model. They are experimenting on our kids. Their AI plan for Houston ISD alone costs $4.5 million! That's money we could use to increase teacher pay and hire more staff for our students.
Meanwhile, our neighborhood schools are struggling.
Schools are closing. More than 150 districts have moved to four-day school weeks. Teachers are leaving the profession. And instead of putting every available dollar toward fixing those problems, Abbott pushed through a voucher program that sends taxpayer dollars to private schools -- including schools built around an AI-driven education model.
**This is what I call the Greg Abbott Corruption Tax: Texans pay the price while politically connected donors and special interests benefit.**
Our children should never come second to a campaign donor or corporate interest.
And our taxpayer dollars should be going toward strengthening neighborhood public schools and putting great teachers in classrooms -- not subsidizing an experiment in replacing human instruction with algorithms.
**Let me be clear: There can be no American Dream without strong public schools.**
I believe the most important resource we can put in a classroom isn't a chatbot, algorithm, standardized test, or new piece of software.
It's a great teacher.
That's why, as governor, I will fire Mike Morath on Day One. I will end the rigged STAAR test and pause the A-F accountability system. I will end Abbott's voucher scam. And I will end corrupt vendor contracts and use that money to pay teachers.

This model threatens the development of our kids and attempts to replace teachers with robots. Human connection is at the heart of most of our educational journeys. Abbott's AI slop could never replace the critical role of having actual qualified teachers in front of the classroom. Already we are seeing curriculum that's been created by AI be totally inaccurate for both math and social studies. That's especially concerning in Houston, because the people making these decisions weren't chosen by Houston voters. Abbott's $1 billion voucher scam is stealing money from our schools, and I'm running to put a stop to it. Abbott and Morath plan to convert 100 schools to their AI model. Raised by a single mom, he washed dishes, worked in a warehouse, and plowed snow to get by. **Then, he spent 20 years as a firefighter in Bethlehem, running toward the smoke while everyone else ran out, carrying families to safety.** He's been showing up for working people ever since. As President of the Pennsylvania Professional Fire Fighters Association, he’s represented more than 8,000 firefighters across the Commonwealth, fighting for better wages, health care, and safer working conditions. **Now, he wants to bring that fight to Washington.** He's running to ban corporate money from politics, guarantee healthcare through Medicare for All, bring down the cost of housing, childcare, and groceries, and make billionaires pay their fair share so our government works for working families, not wealthy donors. Which explains why Trump and his allies are suddenly so eager to stop him. And his opponent Ryan Mackenzie? clean_body: | | | Peter — Donald Trump's super PAC just reserved $295,000 in TV and mail ads to stop Bob Brooks , the Working Families Party-endorsed firefighter running for Congress in Pennsylvania's 7th district.1 It's part of a $150 million cavalry charge to rescue Republicans in races they're afraid of losing.2 And it's easy to see why Bob's race made the list. Republican Ryan Mackenzie won this seat by a mere 4,000 votes last time, roughly one high school football crowd.3 The race is a toss-up again this year, and one recent poll has the race in a dead heat.4 In other words, Trump and his billionaire donors know Bob can win. So they're trying to bury him in MAGA cash before undecided voters get the chance to know him, and those ads could start any day now. Trump's billionaires can flood every TV screen in the Lehigh Valley, but close races like this one are won by volunteers knocking doors, making calls, and sending texts. In a race decided by 4,000 votes last time, that organizing can make all the difference, but only if we have the resources to make it happen. Bob's not your typical politician, Peter. Raised by a single mom, he washed dishes, worked in a warehouse, and plowed snow to get by. Then, he spent 20 years as a firefighter in Bethlehem, running toward the smoke while everyone else ran out, carrying families to safety. He's been showing up for working people ever since. As President of the Pennsylvania Professional Fire Fighters Association, he’s represented more than 8,000 firefighters across the Commonwealth, fighting for better wages, health care, and safer working conditions. Now, he wants to bring that fight to Washington. He's running to ban corporate money from politics, guarantee healthcare through Medicare for All, bring down the cost of housing, childcare, and groceries, and make billionaires pay their fair share so our government works for working families, not wealthy donors. Which explains why Trump and his allies are suddenly so eager to stop him. And his opponent Ryan Mackenzie? He's voted with Trump on nearly everything, and even landed a speaking slot at Trump's big midterm convention in Dallas.5 Now Trump is returning the favor with $295,000 worth of thank-you notes. So that's the choice in PA-07: a firefighter who stands up for working people, or a congressman who stands up whenever Trump walks into the room. Bob will be outspent. But with your help, he won't be out-organized. In solidarity and fierce resistance, Working Families Party Sources: 1\. , The New York Times, September 15, 2026. 2\. , The New York Times, September 18, 2026. 3\. , The Philadelphia Inquirer, September 10, 2026. 4\. , House Majority PAC, July 9, 2026. 5\. , The Morning Call, September 10, 2026. body:
# [](https://act.tammybaldwin.com/go/3095?t=1&akid=5691%2E35263%2EHlLREq)
Peter, have you heard my story?
When I was growing up, I spent three months in the hospital from a serious illness. My grandparents, who raised me, looked for an insurance policy after I left to cover future costs.
But here’s what happened: they couldn’t find a single policy that covered me — all because I had a pre-existing condition from my illness — which meant they had to pay for my care out of pocket. Peter, like so many others, the exorbitant costs of paying for care kept them up at night worried about how they would be able to afford it.
Seeing my grandparents go through that struggle was one of the reasons I ran for office. I didn’t want another family to go through what we went through and worry about how they were going to afford care.
As Senator, I was proud to support the Affordable Care Act and advocate to ensure insurance companies cannot deny coverage or charge higher rates for individuals with pre-existing health conditions.
**[I believe everyone should have access to quality and affordable care. I won’t stop fighting for that. If you are able, can you chip in right now to help me continue this work in Congress?](https://act.tammybaldwin.com/go/6050?c0=em-ms-tb-20260923-healthcarechampion.D6l0Nm&amount=10&refcode=em20260923-5691&t=2&akid=5691%2E35263%2EHlLREq)**

Peter, in our neck of the woods, workers ALWAYS come first. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139820399/648612180/-1060083271?refcode=em-9.23.26-all-a-2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS85MzkwNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkNTY5YTBkZS05N2I3LWYxMTEtYTZhOS0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=TI97KD8BbFNZ2KfjKeLnX_XwFh2YWrG4nKvItkKBtzw=) We rallied with our friends in labor in Rock Island this past week to talk through November and how we can build a better future for every worker who calls the 17th Congressional district home. Some of my favorite moments on the campaign trail are when I get to meet the tradesmen, farmers, and local unions in Illinois fighting for better pay and jobs. But showing up is one thing, and acting is another. And I am proud of my 100% pro-labor voting record in Congress. When I say I support the rights of working people, I mean it! Hey Peter,
---
I wanted to flag something that's been bothering me: the national debt has now crossed $40 **trillion**. Republicans in Congress, including our own Rep. Brad Knott, keep talking about "fiscal responsibility" while voting for exactly the kind of bill that makes it worse. Knott voted for the FY25 budget resolution and called it a blueprint for reining in reckless spending. But the centerpiece of that same agenda, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, is projected to add at least $4 trillion to the deficit, per Congressional Budget Office estimate. That's not a rounding error - it's one of the largest deficit-increasing bills in years, passed by the same party that campaigns on cutting the debt. Remember the “Big Beautiful Bill”? That’s the one that cut health care benefits for 11+million Americans (including more than 30,000 people here in District 13) to pay for tax cuts for the wealthiest Americans. It's easy to say you care about the debt in a press release. It's much harder to actually vote against a bill your own party is pushing when it blows a multi-trillion-dollar hole in the budget. Knott didn't do that. And it’s pretty heartless to do this in a way that helps the wealthiest while pulling the rug out from underneath those in our society who have the least. I’m running for Congress to be an independent voice for our community in Washington. That is why this campaign is being funded by you. clean_body: The national debt has now crossed $40 trillion.| | | | = Hey Peter, I wanted to flag something that's been bothering me: the national debt has now crossed $40 trillion. Republicans in Congress, including our own Rep. Brad Knott, keep talking about "fiscal responsibility" while voting for exactly the kind of bill that makes it worse. Knott voted for the FY25 budget resolution and called it a blueprint for reining in reckless spending. But the centerpiece of that same agenda, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, is projected to add at least $4 trillion to the deficit, per Congressional Budget Office estimate. That's not a rounding error - it's one of the largest deficit-increasing bills in years, passed by the same party that campaigns on cutting the debt. Remember the “Big Beautiful Bill”? That’s the one that cut health care benefits for 11+million Americans (including more than 30,000 people here in District 13) to pay for tax cuts for the wealthiest Americans. It's easy to say you care about the debt in a press release. It's much harder to actually vote against a bill your own party is pushing when it blows a multi-trillion-dollar hole in the budget. Knott didn't do that. And it’s pretty heartless to do this in a way that helps the wealthiest while pulling the rug out from underneath those in our society who have the least. I’m running for Congress to be an independent voice for our community in Washington. That is why this campaign is being funded by you. I don’t have PACs lining up to support me, or a rich brother who will funnel money to this campaign at the last minute, so I need your help. = = Early voting is less than a few weeks away, and we have to work together to do everything we can to make sure we have a representative willing to keep fighting for NC-13 in Washington. Talk more soon, Paul Barringer Candidate for US Congress | | | | | | | ---|---|---|--- | | | | Paid for by Paul Barringer for Congress | | | | Paul Barringer for Congress PO Box 114 Sanford, NC 27331 United States

Hey –

I’m not sending this email to everybody. Just to the folks I know care about this battleground race in Ohio and know what’s at stake if we don’t win.

Ohio will be the tiebreaking seat for a Democratic Senate majority. But with _The New York Times_ reporting that crypto billionaires are adding another $30 million against us, it just got a lot tougher to win.

A lot is riding on this race, and I don’t take that lightly. I know Ohioans are counting on me to mount this comeback bid and pave the path to Senate control.

But I also feel tremendous gratitude and optimism. I’ve never seen energy like we’re building, and folks are showing up in droves to make a difference this year.

When we win this race, it won’t be because crypto billionaires or Elon Musk came to my rescue (that’s my opponent’s strategy). No – when we win, it will be because a student in Athens gave $1, a teacher in Dayton gave $5 every month, and a concerned mother in Westerville gave $10 too. Any donation, no matter the amount, fuels our grassroots fight.

Californians may not have many exciting statewide races this year, but our direct democracy rules have produced a fat ballot with more than a dozen propositions. Over the next few weeks, I'll share my thoughts on most of these measures because many to walk through a handful of these. Many are genuinely confusing, and confusing ballot measures are exactly how bad policy sneaks through.
First up: the so-called billionaires tax, or Proposition 40.
Billionaires should pay their fair share; I've spent most of my career saying exactly that. It's a core principle for me as a progressive, and in Congress, I sponsored wealth taxes. In fact, I think Democrats should make an overhaul of tax policy a cornerstone of their next few years' agenda. But Prop 40 is a hot mess, and even the most "eat-the-rich" voters should reject it. Here's how I explained it in an op-ed for the _[San Francisco Chronicle](https://substack.com/redirect/68530c2e-bd67-477e-be61-2601f47481df?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_
> For too many years, working families across California have been shortchanged in an economy shaped by corporate elites and the ultra-wealthy.
> Worker productivity has climbed for decades while paychecks haven't kept pace. CEOs, meanwhile, are pulling in hundreds of times what their employees make. California families are getting squeezed by healthcare costs rising faster than their wages. Our state and federal policies often favor billionaires over everyone else, leaving ordinary Californians to pick up the tab.
> Creating a fairer California means calling out these deep systemic inequalities. We must insist that wealthy Californians pay their fair share of taxes. But holding that fundamental belief does not require us to rubber-stamp every poorly drafted policy that claims to champion tax fairness -- especially one that will fail to deliver on its promises and ultimately will leave our state worse off.
> Proposition 40 is a prime example of a seemingly progressive-sounding policy solution that ultimately just perpetuates the status quo. It does nothing to reform our healthcare system and would send billions in tax dollars to private health insurance companies and corporations that dominate our healthcare system.
> Despite what its supporters say, Prop 40 is not a solution to our healthcare crisis. Trump-era federal healthcare cuts and rising costs pose real threats to working families, but Prop. 40 delivers only a limited, one-time transfer, not the sustainable, predictable funding required to keep hospitals, community clinics and reproductive health providers afloat.
> Healthcare costs continue to outpace inflation, leaving most patients falling further behind. That is a serious policy problem that deserves attention. But Prop 40 does nothing to address skyrocketing healthcare costs.
> Worse, there is zero guarantee the measure's funds will actually help reach patients or ease the medical bills of struggling families. Instead, the revenue could easily be swallowed up by health insurance companies and executives -- the very entities that helped create our healthcare crisis in the first place. Prop 40 fails, for lack of even trying, to make any reforms to the broken parts of our healthcare system.
> It is hard to fathom how steering tens of billions of dollars to for-profit health insurance companies somehow solves wealth inequality or addresses our healthcare needs.
> Most people don't realize that the state contracts with private health insurance companies to provide coverage for low-income patients. These insurance companies are the biggest beneficiaries of our for-profit healthcare system. Unlike nearly every other major healthcare funding infusion in recent memory, Prop 40 does nothing to demand that these health insurance companies do more for patients with those dollars. It doesn't do anything to increase price transparency or competition in healthcare, eliminate middlemen or change the system's incentives to reward health instead of sickness.
> Progressives who have long fought for "Medicare for All," as I have, should resist a billionaire tax that entrenches a troubled for-profit healthcare system, rather than dismantling it.
> Buried even deeper in Prop 40's text is language that allows state lawmakers to divert funds away from healthcare toward other priorities. That is why doctors on the front lines of care, including the California Medical Association, the California Primary Care Association and Planned Parenthood Affiliates of California, are urging a "no" vote. Major tax changes should come with real strings attached to ensure the dollars are well spent. Instead, Prop 40 is a blank check to a broken system.
> Prop 40's errors aren't just limited to healthcare. It also threatens state budget stability. California already relies heavily on a volatile tax base driven by high-income earners. According to the Legislative Analyst's Office and economists at Stanford and UC Berkeley, Prop. 40 could actually shrink the ongoing income tax collections that sustain our state's General Fund. Trading recurring General Fund revenue, which reliably pays for schools, public safety and healthcare year after year, for a one-time cash infusion is a bad deal for California's future.
> Supporters of the measure want to frame this election as a simple choice: billionaires versus working people. But that framing ignores reality. California voters should not be fooled by false progressive bravado. That's why a broad coalition of teachers, building trades, firefighters and frontline healthcare organizations stands firmly against it.
> You don't have to agree with Republicans or corporate interests to vote no on Prop 40. Progressive voters shouldn't be fooled into propping up the status quo, which is exactly what Prop 40 does. Fighting for a fairer economy requires writing smart, durable laws that level the playing field for working families, strengthen our schools and reduce healthcare costs. Prop. 40 fails on all three counts. California deserves better.
Some have argued that the Prop 40 tax is "at least a start" or "better than nothing." Indeed, its own architects have admitted it is "an experiment." But a change in the tax structure has long-term consequences. Look how Reagan's huge cuts to the top brackets continue to drive inequality today. Prop 40 would cost California billions of dollars in tax revenue over the next decade. And in return, the money will be gone in a matter of months. That is not good budgeting, and it's even worse tax policy. Because Prop 40 is so poorly written, if passed, it will become the poster child for _not_ taxing billionaires at the federal level--exactly what Democrats should consider when they regain control in Washington.
Look, I've got three teenagers, and they have only known an America of deep economic inequality. It's fair to say that they despise billionaires. But it's exactly because of my kids that I'm a NO on Prop 40. It would create a fiscal catastrophe for their future as Californians.

clean_body: | | | | = Friends, I want to tell you about John Duresky, and then I'm going to ask you to split a donation between his campaign and mine. John is running to replace Dan Newhouse in the 4th, one district over from me. It runs through the orchards and farmland of the Yakima Valley and out to Hanford, and it hasn't sent a Democrat to Congress in a very long time. John wasn't planning to run for anything. He grew up in a union household, joined the Air Force, learned a trade, and eventually became an officer, retiring as a Major with three combat deployments behind him. He then spent the rest of a 37-year career in federal service, most of it at Hanford as a project control officer. Then Elon Musk's DOGE sent a million federal workers an email telling them to resign and take a buyout or stay and take their chances. A week later he was running for Congress, because as he puts it, he wanted to make sure what happened to his fellow civil servants never happens again. Thirty-seven years of service, and the thing that finally got him to run for office was watching how the people he worked alongside were treated. Here's why I like him. He doesn't take corporate PAC money, and neither do I. He wants to ban members of Congress from trading individual stocks, and so do I. He says the VA should be judged on what veterans actually experience rather than on what politicians in D.C. imagine. He also points out that nobody in Central Washington should have to drive a hundred miles to see a doctor, and you and I both know that isn't an exaggeration. It's just what rural health care in this state has become. Meanwhile, billionaire mega-donors are already trying to buy that seat, and AI-linked super PACs put $800,000 into the primary alone to elect Trump-backed Republican Amanda McKinney. I know exactly what that feels like, because Republicans are spending about $12 million to take mine. Neither of us is going to match that kind of money, and neither of us is going to try. What we can do is have enough people standing behind us that it stops mattering. = = Thanks for being in this with us. Marie = John Duresky is a retired member of the U.S. Air Force. clean_body: I am asking you personally to read this message >>| | | | = Inside Elections was the last major forecaster holding out on our race, and they just shifted their prediction of the Alaska Senate race in our direction.= They’re joining every other major election forecaster in recognizing that the momentum is on our side. They know what we know: We are going to win this race. Alaskans are ready for change. I’ve spent the past nine months traveling to communities in every corner of the state – from Prince of Wales to St. Lawrence Island, the Kenai to the Arctic. And everywhere I go, I hear the same thing: Enough. Enough of Dan Sullivan’s self-dealing. He’s tripled his personal wealth since getting to DC, and Alaskans are paying the price. We are getting crushed by corporate greed while he turns the other way, and we’re tired of it. I’m angry that the millionaires and billionaires have rigged the system in DC against working Alaskans. I’m angry that it doesn’t work for us anymore. But I’m also optimistic. Alaskans are can-do people. And together, on November 3rd, we’re going to take the first step toward taking back our state. We won nearly 50% of the vote in our open primary election last month, against 15 other candidates of all parties – including incumbent Senator Dan Sullivan. More than 82,000 Alaskans cast their ballots in favor of our fish, family, freedom campaign for a more abundant Alaska. We beat the incumbent by more than 8 points, and in the first poll of the general election, we’re leading Dan Sullivan by 1 point in the final round of ranked choice voting. Because while Alaskans are sending a clear message that we’re done with the self-dealing politics of the past, we’re going up against the entire DC establishment and their billionaire-backed super PACs – and they are pummeling us with attack ads. They’re noticing the momentum that we’re building in Alaska, and they’re spending BIG to stop us. That’s why this race is so close. It’s the closest race in the country, a true 50/50 toss-up! And while I feel confident that, in the end, we are going to win, it isn’t going to be an easy fight. We are up against a corrupt DC system, and they’re fighting with everything they have to keep it that way. = = I’m proud to be running a grassroots campaign. But it means that each and every one of us has to chip in what we can, when we can, to help us win this all-important race. For Alaska, and for the whole country. Thank you for your support. It makes all the difference. \- Mary = | | | | | | | Resist Reclaim Rebuild is an organization committed to helping Democrats win up and down the ballot, nationwide. A Record Close, Built Almost Entirely on One Company's AI Announcement
The Nasdaq's record close had almost nothing to do with Iran, oil, or the Fed — it was Meta's new AI product. Three separate stories are now trading independently, and Tuesday showed all three moving at once.

**Verified fact:** the Nasdaq closed at a fresh record Tuesday, up 0.45%, and the Russell 2000 gained 0.68%, even as the Dow slipped 0.36% and the S&P; 500 finished essentially flat. WTI crude fell 3.19% to $89.42 and Brent fell 2.69% to $97.64, while gold slipped 0.78% to $4,349.50 and silver fell 0.57% to $66.04.
| | Rotation Signal 01 — The Real Story Wasn't Oil or the Fed. It Was Meta.
---|---
**Verified fact:** Meta Platforms surged nearly 12% Tuesday, the primary catalyst for the Nasdaq's record close, driven by the release of its new autonomous AI agent, Muse, which analysts described as generating “strong demand and resurfaced optimism about the growth outlook for the so-called AI trade.” **Our interpretation:** this is a genuinely independent catalyst, unconnected to any of this month's core stories — Iran, the Fed, or even the Trump-Xi summit — and it was large enough on its own to be the dominant driver of Tuesday's headline index move.
| | Rotation Signal 02 — Oil Kept Falling Despite Harder Diplomatic Evidence Pointing the Other Way
---|---
**Verified fact:** oil's decline continued even as Trump's UN remarks included an explicit ultimatum and Iran's delegation staged a walkout during his address. **Our interpretation:** this is a meaningful divergence — the harder diplomatic data available Tuesday (a walkout, an election-timed deal framing) argues against near-term resolution, yet oil priced the opposite. This raises the odds that oil's recent slide is now driven more by supply-side fundamentals (the Aramco pipeline restoration, recovered Hormuz throughput) than by diplomatic sentiment specifically, which would make it more durable, not less, if that reading is correct.
| | Rotation Signal 03 — Three Independent Trades Are Now Live Simultaneously
---|---
**Current classification: Three genuinely separate regimes, each moving independently: AI/tech (Meta-driven), energy supply (Aramco/Hormuz-driven), and geopolitical diplomacy (Iran/UN-driven, and currently the most negative of the three).** Tuesday showed all three moving, with the market's headline gain driven almost entirely by the one story (AI/tech) least connected to this month's dominant narrative.
| | What to Watch Today
---|---
Whether oil's decline is confirmed as a supply-driven, more durable trend independent of Tuesday's negative diplomatic developments, and whether the AI-trade rally broadens beyond Meta specifically or proves company-specific.

Why? Because they want to try to buy a Senate seat and pass laws that will benefit Donald Trump’s and crypto billionaires’ bottom lines – at the expense of families like yours. I want to do everything I can to make sure Republican opponent Jon Husted, Donald Trump, and their billionaire crypto cronies can’t buy a spot on the Senate floor. We don’t stop a crypto PAC with our own billionaire spending. We stop them with $15, $25, $50, or $100 – whatever you can give today to support Sherrod’s campaign. When he wraps up this fundraising quarter and the numbers go public, I want to be sure you are the reason we have a fighting chance to win back this Senate seat in Ohio this year. [**Will you split a $28 donation — or whatever you can — right now between Sherrod’s campaign and this grassroots movement to help Sherrod take a stand against these crypto special interests, win in Ohio, and flip the Senate?**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/3807?amount=28&t=8&akid=3035%2E4032634%2EL1J0cF)

So now they’re coming after Sherrod with a $30 million targeted ad spend.** Democrats will continue doing our part to push back on these bad deals and demand bipartisan crypto legislation where working people get a say, not just industry insiders. Peter, **Today I sent a letter to Elon Musk, and I want you to know why.**
On September 19th, I filed a police report with the Travis County Sheriff's Office. Dan Patrick's account on X posted two AI-generated deepfake videos of me. They violated Texas law by appearing within 30 days of an election without disclosing they were fake.
The New York Times covered the police report, and the following day, __the videos were gone.__
**_That's a problem._**
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139824434/648626315/489150112?refcode=du_em_09232026_elon_i1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDM3NDAiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZDBjODJiOGYtYTViNy1mMTExLWE2YTktMDAyMjQ4MmE5MzNiIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=1dWC71apI81ZX2Wanxv0MQMkyVD-Lbr0J_pHdWqe_qI=)

_**Those deleted posts are evidence**_ in an active criminal investigation into whether Dan Patrick violated Texas law. They were wiped from the platform before law enforcement could review them.
I'm not waiting for Dan Patrick to come clean. Based on his record of corruption and neglect, we know what to expect from him.
So I wrote directly to Elon Musk — the owner of X — and asked him to provide the two deleted posts to the detective on the case from the Travis County Sheriff’s Office. I doubt he'll comply. X has a pattern of going quiet when the questions get uncomfortable. But here's what I know: **_Innocent people don't delete evidence._** We’re up against a campaign willing to put out AI-generated videos of me and erase the proof once they get caught. Peter, the response to my new book, _Go and Do Likewise_ , has been truly humbling.

I'm grateful to everyone who's picked up a copy — and to everyone who's come out to talk with me about it, about their faith, and about their own communities.

[_**If you haven't gotten your copy yet, it's in bookstores and online now:**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139824517/648626713/-1106739200?utm_campaign=itt_ata_em_nf_bookpromo_260923_t1_1&utm_source=itt_email_260923&utm_medium=email&refcode=ITT_ATA_EM_NF_BookPromo_260923_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjEvMS8xMTAzNjMiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMjlhYWU3ZmEtYTViNy1mMTExLWE2YTktMDAyMjQ4MmE5MzNiIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=rYqAH5N5qe8vcPyAjAEUD6pQ-uDg5qA6LXs4N6CX4xk=&emci=d2519cc8-9fb7-f111-a6a9-0022482a933b&emdi=29aae7fa-a5b7-f111-a6a9-0022482a933b&ceid=17458827) [ORDER NOW](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139824518/648626714/-1106739200?utm_campaign=itt_ata_em_nf_bookpromo_260923_t1_1&utm_source=itt_email_260923&utm_medium=email&refcode=ITT_ATA_EM_NF_BookPromo_260923_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjEvMS8xMTAzNjMiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMjlhYWU3ZmEtYTViNy1mMTExLWE2YTktMDAyMjQ4MmE5MzNiIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=rYqAH5N5qe8vcPyAjAEUD6pQ-uDg5qA6LXs4N6CX4xk=&emci=d2519cc8-9fb7-f111-a6a9-0022482a933b&emdi=29aae7fa-a5b7-f111-a6a9-0022482a933b&ceid=17458827) **My faith shapes everything I do, and it’s time to reclaim it from those who use faith as a weapon to harm or discriminate.** The Golden Rule teaches us to love our neighbor as ourselves. The Parable of the Good Samaritan teaches us that everyone is our neighbor. Not just the people who vote like us. Everyone.

There's a lot of work to do to heal this country, and a lot of good people are already doing it. That's why I wrote this book — not just to talk about what's hard, but to lift up the hope that's still out there. Folks are tired of the anger. They're ready to heal.

I wrote this book hoping it would spark conversations between you and your neighbors, or get you thinking seriously about how we bring this country together and start treating each other with decency and compassion.

Friends,
**As we get ever closer to Election Day, I want to take a moment to thank you for being here.**
I joined Substack to share my thoughts directly with people like you. Deepen the sense of community and connection among my grassroots supporters. Bring you news from the campaign trail. Tell you about behind-the-scenes moments. Most of all, I started these posts to talk about my plans to make Kansas and the country better for every single one of us.
The fact that you're with me on this journey means the world to me, my wife LaVon and my entire team.
I'll be honest: The surge in momentum has been incredible -- and it gets better. You've probably heard me talk about former Republican Governor Graves' **endorsement** of my campaign. Or how election experts, from Nate Silver to Fox News, have moved this race closer to **" Toss Up"** status. And the latest poll from a respected, independent outlet shows me with a **2-point lead** over Roger Marshall. In fact, just a few days ago, _The New York Times_ called this race one of the **most competitive** in the country.
Every single one of these achievements is because of the support of people like **you**. Everyone who has shared one of my posts with a friend, donated to my campaign, offered words of encouragement or shared their concerns with me has played a pivotal role in this movement.
Folks, we are sailing into the end of quarter with the wind at our back. But there's one problem -- and it's one I've also shared with you before. Roger Marshall and his wealthy corporate allies see our campaign's momentum. **They know Kansas is the unexpected battleground of 2026** , and they're pulling out all the stops to beat us.
With the final FEC end-of-quarter deadline of this race just seven days away, we need to keep the momentum going strong and show them we have what it takes to **hold onto the lead and win in November**.
I know things are expensive right now. I know you probably have a lot of people reaching out asking for your support too -- so I wouldn't ask if it wasn't important. **[But with just a few days left before this crucial FEC deadline, we need everyone who believes in what we 're trying to do to pitch in anything they can spare to help us reach more people with our unifying message, fight back against Roger Marshall's attacks and get every single supporter to the polls on Election Day.](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/e78b265c-dbb4-4bbf-bbb6-b7a78052b7c5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[Donate](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/e78b265c-dbb4-4bbf-bbb6-b7a78052b7c5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Roger Marshall and the Washington insiders backing him never dreamed that Kansas might actually be in play. But it is, and we have a real shot at bringing this thing home.
Thank you for your support,
Adam Hamilton

"Bailey" was six weeks along when her boyfriend saw the pregnancy test. His face didn't light up. It twisted with disgust. _"What about our five-year plan?" _ Then he brought up the unthinkable: _abortion. _ "Do it now," he told her. "Before the baby gets bigger and while the decision is still easy." But nothing about ending her baby's life felt easy to Bailey. For weeks, he pushed. He threatened to kick her out of his home if she didn't go through with it. Two young kids, two part-time jobs, and now this -- a boyfriend giving her an ultimatum instead of support. Bailey moved out. Alone, scared, and out of options, she searched online for help. **That's when she found Human Coalition. ** One of our nurses talked her through it all -- gently, without judgment. And Bailey scheduled a free ultrasound with one of our clinics. At her appointment, she saw her baby for the first time wiggling on the screen. And in that moment, something in her settled... This baby was hers to protect, _no matter what anyone else decided. _
---

Bailey gave birth to a sweet baby boy named "Andrew", and today, she's raising three children. Her boyfriend eventually came around to her decision, and they reconciled. They started going to church together, and recently, the whole family was baptized. _God was truly at work in restoring this young family! _ But without that ultrasound, Bailey might have believed her boyfriend was right: that this baby didn't fit "the plan," and the easiest thing to do was make the "problem" disappear. Instead, she saw her baby moving on a screen. She heard a heartbeat. And in that moment, "the plan" stopped mattering. That's what your gift makes possible -- not just an appointment, but the moment a mom realizes her baby is a person worthy of protection. And that she wouldn't face her pregnancy alone. **Friend, right now, another mom is searching online for an abortion. ** She's scared. She can't see any other options. And in the next few minutes, _she's going to make a decision that can't be undone. _ Human Coalition exists to reach her first -- before the abortion industry does. Since 2009, we've rescued **over 36,000 children** from abortion by meeting abortion-determined moms with: ✅ A free ultrasound, so she can see her baby is real ✅ Licensed health care, no strings attached ✅ Help with housing, employment, and education -- the real reasons so many moms feel like abortion is their only choice **Every single day, we impact the lives of 188 moms and babies. ** But we can only reach the next Bailey if someone funds her appointment and ultrasound before she walks into an abortion facility instead. _**Will you give to save the next baby in danger? **_ Every $26 you give today helps us reach another abortion-determined woman and connects her with one of Human Coalition's pro-life nurses. And, if you are able, a gift of $202 not only helps us connect with another mom but also helps fully cover the cost of her appointment and ultrasound to see her growing child in the womb. **[Regardless of what amount you choose to give today, your gift can offer an abortion-determined mom real help and hope — moving her closer to an appointment that can change her mind and save her baby’s life.](http://links.conservativesdefendingfreedom.com/u/click?_t=91d01aa68bbe4105984439520ca0f0af&_m=a1034d4e9ddb4636992e4910da67f427&_e=JMSnqAdp1Xq-0nPOGXM5Ljm4agO5eKWbcHXelInaDGoSFgFxfDhZvkms6M675sfYlxv1P6Q-056F6s921lAr7iaDkMnAf9BwCcNO_6JbsvIySqSkWdUbBXu83YzFHK1UAB_zZSvfoHWgN6jaRLhXpe7GVz7dx9LlDjjkbd_GMpR6RCtk9HN107L2WtGKxZfyfxuzaXok-csYoxcw4BLlqMC2_eX7fCdr_iFbBqd1ARb48YS6zl8-Ilf1bI0jLAa-P5eb2kstCiaoDXepUPknXehqgzJa3X3Kn181sLa5u_nIizvEPU0qhmrLxW77KPycQDhPMfTKVdsrUjxYBIzizDI0pLUkOkSuFhjE8xI7cjmxjwIFBK41pAL0DZq_C2eCCuPdK4h8hCwcjgh25LWcVmTa_Wsj5V4DgLCjmNKoJ8AmuvniOGkWYNIVVVQcv2edY7fJdHjEq4p733gezjefXHFcD1vJqkwQrbAD8ayLFXEdtYI7gzKSJhhjaTfU_weFJ0Kt-BV6rEKVxntolEgbUtskhFaM2tD9yYvLUa3PhLxDVt03Htzh5o85UQyvKnsfOVdpLwMNVzBpJyu9TFj5c7G_qGntAc23aOVkFzbPXI9HKYMFS-EANx5L2Jp55Lok)**

But because of our generous supporters, a nurse was there for Bailey. An ultrasound machine was running. And a mother chose life for her precious child. That's what you can do today. Thank you in advance for standing with moms and babies who have nowhere else to turn.

clean_body: | | | | | | | Friend, "Bailey" was six weeks along when her boyfriend saw the pregnancy test. His face didn't light up. It twisted with disgust. "What about our five-year plan?" Then he brought up the unthinkable: abortion. "Do it now," he told her. "Before the baby gets bigger and while the decision is still easy." But nothing about ending her baby's life felt easy to Bailey. For weeks, he pushed. He threatened to kick her out of his home if she didn't go through with it. Two young kids, two part-time jobs, and now this -- a boyfriend giving her an ultimatum instead of support. Bailey moved out. Alone, scared, and out of options, she searched online for help. That's when she found Human Coalition. One of our nurses talked her through it all -- gently, without judgment. And Bailey scheduled a free ultrasound with one of our clinics. At her appointment, she saw her baby for the first time wiggling on the screen. And in that moment, something in her settled... This baby was hers to protect, no matter what anyone else decided. Bailey gave birth to a sweet baby boy named "Andrew", and today, she's raising three children. Her boyfriend eventually came around to her decision, and they reconciled. They started going to church together, and recently, the whole family was baptized. God was truly at work in restoring this young family! But without that ultrasound, Bailey might have believed her boyfriend was right: that this baby didn't fit "the plan," and the easiest thing to do was make the "problem" disappear. Instead, she saw her baby moving on a screen. She heard a heartbeat. And in that moment, "the plan" stopped mattering. That's what your gift makes possible -- not just an appointment, but the moment a mom realizes her baby is a person worthy of protection. And that she wouldn't face her pregnancy alone. Friend, right now, another mom is searching online for an abortion. She's scared. She can't see any other options. And in the next few minutes, she's going to make a decision that can't be undone. Human Coalition exists to reach her first -- before the abortion industry does. Since 2009, we've rescued over 36,000 children from abortion by meeting abortion-determined moms with: ✅ A free ultrasound, so she can see her baby is real ✅ Licensed health care, no strings attached ✅ Help with housing, employment, and education -- the real reasons so many moms feel like abortion is their only choice Every single day, we impact the lives of 188 moms and babies. But we can only reach the next Bailey if someone funds her appointment and ultrasound before she walks into an abortion facility instead. Will you give to save the next baby in danger? Every $26 you give today helps us reach another abortion-determined woman and connects her with one of Human Coalition's pro-life nurses. And, if you are able, a gift of $202 not only helps us connect with another mom but also helps fully cover the cost of her appointment and ultrasound to see her growing child in the womb. There is a mom right now sitting alone with a pregnancy test and no one telling her she has another option besides abortion. She doesn't know Human Coalition exists yet. Whether she finds us in time may come down to whether or not this ministry has the resources to reach her first. Without good people like you, Bailey's story might not have had a happy ending. But because of our generous supporters, a nurse was there for Bailey. An ultrasound machine was running. And a mother chose life for her precious child. That's what you can do today. Thank you in advance for standing with moms and babies who have nowhere else to turn. For Life, Jeff Bradford CEO/President Human Coalition | | | P.S. Peter,
We prayed the first poll was an outlier...
_**47-47.** _
A fluke. Bad sample. Democrat pollster with an agenda. That's what everyone wanted to believe.

_**45-45.** _
_Same result, different pollster._
**Two polls. Two dead heats. Trump-backed Ashley Moody is tied with Angie Nixon in the biggest Senate special election of 2026 – for the seat Marco Rubio held for fourteen years.**
